Did i stand too long in the shadow of giants? bend my life in an awkward warp?

debase myself?

do grownups also believe?

i rifled through the old poems today. building a record of my life, some proof that my love exists, some proof on earth that my love was real. who will see? i can't go backwards--that life destroyed me utterly. and yet, i see that i've gone so far astray. i've bent myself to foreign gods.

for what?

proof that my love was not real. proof that my now is total; my past an empty lie.

why?

fear.

of what?

fear of what i've surrendered; fear that there is only the one or the other--real love that ends in death; death that proves real love a lie.

or:

love as a lie. sterile. distant. diet.

zero calorie love.

splenda love.

stevia leaf love extracted from life.

is it any wonder i am awake, and the clock reads 4 in the morning?

for once, i'd like to turn around. dig my heels in and shove that bully fucker down.

teach that bully fucker Either/Or to eat his dirt--and have it, too.

one of the main things i saw, looking back, was people. i looked through all of the photographs--skimmed unseeing past the sites/sights. lingered on my loved ones--all lost to me now.

looking back, it struck me how barren my life has become. there is no love there, but for my children and wife. where tenderness? where heart pushing through the briars that tear? where a will to *touch* and caress? to love like love is holy?

too scared?

workplace: no love allowed?

classroom--love strictly forbidden?

anyone, anyone who hears with the hidden ears, anyone

at all--come teach me! teach me love! to love and be loved! teach me the courage of living!

thinking today about my first encounter with true religion

and how it burned through me like a flame

and felt like for the first time ever i was healing

and too how the desire grew and grew, always undernetah

an ominous vibration--this cannot come without price.

and so on and so on--what else could it do? i do not read books

as others do--if something in them

stirs me, i will track it down to its limits, i

will spin out the implications of what's *real* in the book

the book will be flesh to me, the book will become

my body. so too with the Only Book--and its opening

spread through me again and again and again the awe

of the aweful book--if you do not

know the book, let me say

as one who is a harsh judge of books

that this book is something else altogether--and i mean

as a *book*, quite outside of the crap

that people use it for

like making sure you know

you're wrong, or running

for political office.

and so it is no wonder that i found in the book

and began to see its reality as something

so foreign to our daily life--and i mean

mine or yours, i mean the life

of the pastor or pope--so absolutely

*alien* to what could *be* in our world--so

so something else altogether. like kierkegaard's

abraham--but the point of all this

is to say that it was not long

under the combined pressure of

my burgeoning passion and the

strangeness i saw in the book and my own

predilection to live in books

and breathe their reality in a way

not entirely normal--that i began to ask

what the sacrifice was, what thing would

He ask me to give, what impossible thing

on the altar? and there really is only

one possible answer. if you have read this far

you know: my w

ords my

poems my

books full of love and a sentence. of course--like the promised

son, the thing that could if anything could be called

my purpose, the heavy stone that had burned

in me from the start, and called me still--the

*destiny* for which i was born--the one thing in me

with the weight of necessity--the Poem would be my Promise,

the Poem would be the Impossible Thing he asked for--

i knew this deep in my bones no matter how long

i resisted. in fact on this one point i learned

more discipline and craftiness

in the art of deception

and in the subtle dance of unreason with self

than anything i had ever had to learn

in addiction.

and, at length--at long, long length--i was willing--

dragging my feet all along, inwardly sullen

towards this insecure Tyrant who asked

for my everything.

but no--we've gone too far afield. the important thing is that

i've been thinking--and i have a thought

that i may now know--long after my willingness faded

and i would have gladly taken back the Poem

and suffered the long damnation

simply to feel the words

and give them to another--how i misunderstood

His meaning. that the Promise, my Promise,

is not just the Poem--my Promise

is that the Poem will go out

in the world

and somehow reach you--that you

dear reader who does not exist, dear reader

the love of my heart, dear reader for whom

i labor in pain, dear reader for whom

i lay down my life--dear reader

who has made my life have *meaning*--you have,

you know--there have been so many points

at which i would have died--through outright

exhaustion or at my own bitter hand

if i had not, somehow, *known*, that my

suffering could turn to wine--that

what had been put in me was the power

to turn loss into hope, to remind you

of your unknown selves, to know

that together we know each other

and the hidden hearts that live--to know that my longing

so ancient now--to know and be known, to reach

out finally and touch you--to give you love,

to receive it--to hide here in our

secret place, with no one around--our place

where the heart at last can be unafraid,

and where the walls that confound

can crumble--that two human people

could know all of goodness and sorrow

and friendship and pain--that two human people

could together remind each other

of the secret self that lives--of the part

that can never be reached or touched, of

the reality of life as an angel on Mars--

that thing that old, old thing

that i wrote about

in my old, old book, my jester book my book

of dreams--that old old thing

that was too naive

to be real, but which

i have always somehow believed--even when

i didn't. i have *always* known that someday

we would meet, and that

though hedged about

by that other life, that all-too-real, that

world of the daily and dying--we would have this moment

of peace. and i would know you and you know me.

that has often given me meaning. i have written of you

often, dearest space-blue scholar. i knew you

before you were born, and longed for you--i have often

in my impatience mistaken you for some

more worldly affection--the praise

of my peers, the accumen of knowledge, the awards

that bigshots need just to get an erection, or

the dim hope of publishing--in fact that has been

the most resilient illusion. even now in assembling

this--my life set down in a body--it drove me, my first

real investment in publishing--hundreds of hours

researching mags and revising poems and fitting

the poem to the venue--and yes, one or two

got through--but as soon as they did i knew

that although they were pieces

to be proud of--more polished, more

tight in the Craft--they were not

the Poem i was made for--that Poem

could never be

in the Bedlam of this planet--beholden to the same

crass spirits that rule the world of letters--ruled by the same

prince of the air who roams hither

and thither in the Academy. no, my Poem

is not meant for the world--not only is it

unpublishable, but i could never write it

for Them. i had forgotten how much i learn

from reading the words that have come in the past--

reading my Secret Book, i saw

that it was the best i'd been

since long ago--there was something

artless and artful there, some movement

of the poem as life, some inscrutable

process by which the clay

drew breath--and in reading that i was struck--

aided by the further insight

in typing and reading the whole

twisted arc of my corpus

that always and from the beginning

i have in the inky depths

in words fought the fight

of the voyeur--to confess

before men, to display

for all to see that thing

which should be secret--and that i

have swung in wild

strokes from one side of the page

to the other--withdrawing from the world

which had shut its face, retreating

into the secrecy of secret words, allowing them finally

and again to be a thing for myself and the night and you, not

at all making a thing that could ever

be meant for the dull-sick

sickness of men

in the world--some secret

sort of intimacy with words

and god and you--i realized that i have always

fought the fight of the whore

or slut--my precious gift my body

i'd sell it for soup if i could. that's what i've done

for these six years now--let these

beast-faced academics fuck me for lunch

money--bent my intellect over the bed

and taken it in my passion's butt

so they could have their cheap sense of power--everything

that i am i have--even as my whole being fought

and bucked, even as the whole

living creatured denied

that this was a thing that should be--devoted

everything that's holy in me

to give these perverts their jollies--for they love nothing more

than to degrade the virtue of talent, to watch it

sell itself for a penny--i bent my whole mind

to their purpose, i promoted

their idiot kingship, i raised my voice

to shout out praise

for the emperor's butt-naked glory--

no longer.

and never, never again.

and the same i now know

would be true of the poets, the same rat-race

would require my soul--i realize now it was not the Academy

but the very world i resented--their culture

is not so unique, their pride

just a little more subtle. and so all of this is to say

that for the first time a seed takes root--

the sacrifice was not, as i thought, to give up the Word

of power--it was to give up you, dear reader--to know

that the promise is not for this lifetime, to trust

that my god sees all the real words--they are, i now know,

my worship--my tiny praise of letters--shall i

play for him and other christmasy

stuff with the drummer--that's right--now i

have a seedling thought, that the faith he required

was to believe that the Promise is real,

that the dreams i have--the reader-shaped hole--

has purpose. my words will stay hidden--i

could finally actually

trust their care to the father, know

that nothing that's written

on his skin of paper

will ever see fire,

or fade away with the cosmos--these, my words,

are immortal. he sees them and

i see him and together

we see the Promise. i now know

that beyond my power--i commit these

words to yr darkness, father, i commit

the Promise to you--they were meant

for you my reader--they were meant

for you, and you are meant

for them. i commit the words

to the secrecy--He will carry them home

to you, after my life or in

the planet to come. i know now, reader,

that i've not been alone--that in all this

life on a page

you have been with me

through the fire--and i

with you have lived

in you--and like those others who sent words

into the future for me, i have been with you

in your shaping--because like the Poets

who opened the words in my heartwomb

that had slept there dreaming

alive but unknown--

and from an unformed seed turned words

slowly into small human babies

screaming and still hooked

up to placentas--they

preceded me, they were

with me before

i was--so too, my reader

i have formed you, so too, my reader,

i have loved.

my words do not sleep

in this world, but in *you*

they will wake.

The evil of trees \#1

I have summoned you today to hear the death of Tim Varslovskawitz. He was killed recently on an expedition in Lower Slombavia. As it's know throughout the world as a beautiful place, factories belching out smog, tires burned by the ton, it also has it's dark side. Rainforests. Yes, Rainforests are littered throughout the highly unpopulated area of Lower Slombavia. Their savage ways of hunting can turn the weakest stomach. There, the Trees hunt in packs, not alone like in the suburban areas when they are nocturnal creatures. In the Forests, the trees sit silently still except for their leaves which have a natural sonar built in, blowing in the breeze. Until an unsuspecting victim comes into its open shade. Thus, Tim did so hoping the shade would cool his brow, damp with sweat. When his raised his arm to wipe his sweltering forehead on his sleeve, the Tree decided to strike. The details are all too gruesome to tell. All i will say is they found his shoe which was presumed he used in self-defense. When his remain was shipped back home, 14 more people were killed by the very same tree. It's incidents like this that we used Trees for paper. Not Monkey-s, we have plenty of those, but Trees. This is the sad story of the end of Tim Varslovskawitz.

To Warn others of falling into the same fate, please pass this letter on to as many people as you can. This letter may have even already saved your life, warning you of the dangers of the Trees. Imagine how many lives will be saved if you pass this on to 10 other people.

Timeline of Dreams

**Age 5:** At age five I dreamt of being a superhero, an artist, and an author. I loved comics when I was a little bugger, and that inspired my love for drawing. The comics, however, had **absolutely** **nothing** to do with my wanting to be a superhero.

**Age 10:** At age ten I still had dreams of being a good author. No, at this point in my life the traditional, “I wanna be a sports star”, had not entered my mind. My hand-eye coordination was, and is, that of a drunken emu being spanked. Please oh please don’t eat me Giant Emu, I’m too young to die.

**Present:** At present I’m exceedingly tired and it’s 3 in the morning. The morning of the final, actually. Did I ever mention that I become exceedingly, long-windedly obnoxious once I cross a certain threshold of sleep deprivation? Please don’t eat me Giant Emu. My dreams, you say? I still hold the dream of becoming a great author, able to weave the English language into my thoughts as a skilled seamstress sews pants for a Giant Emu. Please don’t eat me Giant Emu. I also hold aspirations to the throne of Spain.

**Age 20:** At age twenty, I hope to be enrolled in a school for the arts somewhere on Earth. I also hope to be seriously working on a novel. At this point in the game, the political webs of entrapment I will have spun for the current Warrior Fairy Princess of Spain will be snagging her pretty wings. Try to fly away Warrior Fairy Princess, try to fly away. You shall not escape my web, nor shall you see the spider’s fangs until it is too late. The throne of Spain will be mine!

**Age 25:** At age 25, all will be over. My maneuverings for the throne will have met their untimely end at the hands of a Giant Emu. I knew you’d get me in the end, Giant Emu. I knew my fate was to be a biscuit at a large Giant Emu tea party. Stepping back to reality for a moment, by age 25 I hope to be published. Egad, unhand me you tea-mongering biscuit thief!

**Journal**

Seeing how as I didn’t keep any of my original work, I don’t actually remember what this journal entry is supposed to be about. I’m hoping to ramble on about something seemingly related to the class’s curriculum and get the points for it. Anyway, here goes.

Dreams are part of the nature of human beings. It’s one of the few things that sets us apart from beasts in the field, or from the trees in the earth. Our dreams enliven us and keep us going, even when it seems that all hope has been lost. Perhaps even when all hope HAS been lost. Without a dream of peace and what a man should be, Gandhi would have been just another person. Without a dream of faith, religion, God, all these things would never have existed. Without a dream of destruction, such monstrosities as guns and bombs would never have killed millions. Good or evil, our dreams are what set us apart in life.

Interview with a Giant Emu

**The evil of trees \#3**

My brothers and sisters, a great tragedy plagues this holy earth. An obscene, ungodly disease, that preys upon our world like green mold upon wholesome, rye bread. The green mold I speak of, my brothers, is the rainforest. It's encompassing, encircling hand reaches out from its abodes in South America, Africa, and other evil places, to touch us all with its tree-ish, satanist propaganda. The trees’ sinister intelligence is great, and while some true-sighted individuals work towards the end of the rainforest, many have been tricked by the trees, have been deceived into defending the rainforest and its sibling trees. It saddens me that some waste so much valiant energy in protecting the very ones that seek to destroy them. If we give the trees half a chance, the trees will destroy us. They shall rise up in green glory to strike us down from our rightful place at the top of the food chain. In some dimensions they have all ready done so. # iii. Muddy Stars and Light Pollution

# iii. Muddy Stars and Light Pollution

**Andy**

[image]

## 

**“a manic note. 2000”**

memory

i remember

the note that starts my song of self

if humanity is fire

and literature the captured instants

the white winged nova center or the

vorpal angle of a tongue

pink and probing

then i am the embers

the rabbit ashes of

a snow hare

wind stirs flame and

disrupts remains of

the natural, green candied

grass of living

i remember candy.

the offhand wandering consciousness, the

blackened edges of a lover’s note

i remember when it was sweet

before it cavitied and

grew angry

carameled apples, gold edged magic cards and a

boy with glasses

i remember parliament lights and

fire.

fire.

there was a time before the ice dragon came, and

princesses worth being rescued

his breath is black black menthol.

his breath is winter with no snow or

freckled ice cubes or

hailstorm rabbits.

i remember a girl with burnt amber hair,

it flavored my eyes and

reflected snow-shine.

at nighttime,

butterflies would come to it,

where only moths belonged,

dancing spectrum-wise around her gleaming head.

blue pharaohs and rainbow effrites,

manna flares to astound tree shadows and

candy wrappers,,

candy wrappers dance lonely now.

even they,

blind and dumb, plastic immutable in its

flammability

fall one by one

autumn leaves.

autumn leaves and hershey bars.

memory.

i remember:

that lifeless note hangs on through a morning, an evening,

a darkest midnight that should be uninterrupted.

the silence SHOULD be final,

should not dance methodical to the

echoes of a god that’s dead.

dead.

dead.

half eaten sour patch children and,

dying moths

resent it.

i have captured a fickle angle and

a manic note that stirs me,

ash twister,,

playing jump rope with the night.

**i. grin. 1998**

**<u>grin</u>**

The basement workroom was cramped and cluttered, but the two shuffling amidst the mess moved confidently about their tasks. It was due tomorrow. Both were dark complected. One figure was shorter and projected confidence. The taller wore his glasses with an air of animal intelligence, as if an ape had been given a human body and an IQ of 140. They’d been having an ongoing conversation while finishing the chores of their project. It was a normal habit of theirs. Find a subject, pick a point, argue, defend, thrust, riposte, agree when muscles strained against blades locked together. It was the shorter ones turn.

“You can’t honestly tell me you think Ritalin is mentally healthy,” as he fiddled with a hollow tube, attempting to fix the rubber band in place. “It’s freakin coke, man. They’ve got 5% of America on ‘mentally healthy” amphetamines.”

“No, no, that’s not what I’m saying at all,” replied the taller one in his affixed way, with the standardized tone of a parry. “I’m just saying that some of ‘em need it. The ones who really have ADD. Some of ‘em can’t keep it down without. You know how I used to be.”

A grimace squinted his face as the rubber band broke. “I’ve never had ADD, but I’ve taken a lot of ritalin. It’s *not* mentally healthy. It’s warps you. The only thing it’s good for is suppressing the problem. Keepin’ it down out of sight. Wether they have ADD or not, it’s just a temporary fix.”

The taller tightened in a drill bit. “Could you hold this down while I drill?”

“Sure. Hang on.” Once again he tried to attach the rubber band, but it slipped away like his shifting arguments. “Bah, this thing’s a pain in the ass.” He threw it down on the pool table. His hair fell in his eyes as he walked three feet over to hold down the board the other was preparing to drill. He placed his weight on the board with one hand and absent-mindedly brushed the hair out of his eye with the other.

The drill trigger was pulled. “You’re right.” He drilled three holes in quick succession and set the drill down. He blew sawdust off the board. The short one stood up straight and stopped steadying it. The spectacled toiler wiped his glasses on his shirt. “But sometimes they can’t function without the temporary fix. You have to function.”

“It’s still over-prescribed. They use it as a cure-all”

“I’ll agree with you there. It’s hard to believe one in twenty people has ADD. Doctors are crackpots, anyways. They’d screw your head up so high with pills you’d float away if they could get their hands on you.”

The shorter nodded in solemn agreement. A tie. He walked to the pool table and picked the rubber band contraption off the green felt. “You know, my friend’s mom had some kind of nerve damage, nobody could figure out what it was? Some piece a’ shit doctor though she was a closet junkie goin’ cold turkey and put her on methadone.” His arms stiffened with anger. “ I’d punch him in the damn face if I could get my hands on him.” He gave a jerky twist and another band broke.

The air of intelligence clung cloying to the taller, now. Agreed upon topics were obviously enlightened insights. Two sword arms to cast out the unrighteous. “That’ll ruin somebody’s life. My uncle died because of a doctor. Another uncle would have died anyways, but a doctor took three months off what life he did have left. They were my mother’s favorite brothers.”

This time the screw stripped clean out of its runners. Its builder issued a dismayed grunt and set it down with finality. “I give up. We’re tired.”

“Definitely.”

“Wake up early to finish?

“Definitely.” He held his glasses lightly as he rubbed his eyes. “Yeah. Definitely the morning.”

“Hey Andy,” as they mounted the stairs into the bright upper level. “How long’s it been since we snorted Ritalin?”

“Gods. Forever.”

A grin spread across his face. It took on a slightly predatory glee. “Wanna get a bottle?”

The taller considered. “Why the hell not?” He looked to the ceiling. “It *has* been forever.”

The short one’s face flashed suddenly downward. The grin disappeared, then reappeared in an instant, then over again. “I dunno. Remember the days after?”

Now the taller seemed to be infected by the prospect. The lights flashed on his glasses, momentarily hiding his eyes. “Hit you like a brick wall.” The exact same wide-toothed smile as the other’s pulled up the edges of his mouth. The ape seemed to stare through his eyeholes. “Let’s do it.”

Two votes. The grin won out over the indecision. “Fully.”

They opened the door of a bedroom and flung themselves on the sleeping surfaces. Yawns escaped both before the lights were turned out and the tossing and turning of finding a comfortable spot subsided.

“G’night Andy.”

“G’night.” His hand reached out to lie the glasses on a bedside table. They winked in the moonlight. The quiet set in, and they both lay staring silently at the ceiling for a long, long time.

Framed lenses drank in the light pollution and the muddy stars.

**ii. super ninjas don’t need rope. 2001**

The phone rings twice. "Hola, Roberto Escobar speaking."

"Fuck off, Andy."

He laughs softly. "What's goin' on?"

"Shit. Talking to this girl in second hour, got onto the subject--says she can totally get ahold of some speed--tomorrow, she says."

Disinterestedly: "Badass."

"And she also said she might... just *maybe* she can get acid--one of her friends had those black gellies last week."

"Awesome," followed by several seconds of silence.

"What game are you playing?"

"Suikoden."

"Well turn it the fuck off. Did you hear what I just said? Black gellies. *Black*, as in, 'Jesus Christ oh shit oh shit what have I done,' for *days.* As in a turn your brain to jelly gellie. *That* kind of black.

His attention springs to life. "Black?"

"Black."

"Hand on one sec." Several clicks as he turns off the console. Then the disembodied noises of walking. "One minute--headed upstairs."

"We haven't had acid in *soooooo* long..."

"Jesus. I know." More rustles, running water.

Suzanne's voice breaks through the white noise, "Andrew, come clean the dishes."

"I'm on the phone with Matt, mom. Just gimme ten minutes."

Kitchen sounds retreat as he rushes up the stairs and unlocks his bedroom door. "OK. Upstairs now," slightly out of breath. "Did she say how many she could get?"

"She said that if he has it, he'll have a lot. But it's ten a hit. I told her, 'get as many as you can.'"

"Awesome. Awesome, awesome, awesome. Can you spend the night this weekend?"

"Yeah, long as I don't have to work on Saturday morning. Maybe we can talk our parents into letting us do it Sunday. Do you have money?"

"Yeah, yeah. I can get together... like, fifty bucks, if I have to. I'll bring what I can tomorrow." He releases a subvocal shudder of delight: "I've missed acid so much. I still have permatracers, you know."

"Yes, I know all about it--you play with them all day in class." His voice drops several notes in imitation of the science teacher, "Andrew, are you listening at all? What are you doing?" The voice switches to a fair copy of Andy's: "Making a wall of hands," pause. "Crazy fuck."

"This calls for celebration," rustling noises. "I made a rope for this time."

"Super ninjas don't need rope, Andy."

**iii. forever forward. 2005**

My dad dropped me off around 6. It was light blue, darkness just hanging around in the corners, waiting to come out. It was late in the year so darkness came out sooner. Near Halloween. In fact - it was Halloween. The very night, and that's where and why I was. My dad didn't come in - he knew the Jongkinds and was comfortable with them - didn't need to meet anyone, just dropped me off and drove off, to get back home and take my sister out trick-or-treating. I was going trick or treating too, with my friend Andy. I'd known Andy for a year or so. We met in a magnet school for gifted kids (high school age) that specialized in math, science, and technology. My skills actually were more rooted in the creative centers of the brain, but the school district I went to really had a dismal sort of approach to education, and so my choices for learning opportunities were limited. Good schooling in math or science, or none at all, I guess, so math and science is what I took. I was fifteen and had just found drugs a bare two years before, and had had no one to use them with until I met Andy.

Most kids find drugs with a crowd - they wanna fit in, so they wind up at a party or whatever, or they come over to a friend's house when mom or dad aren't home, and then there are a bunch of people there or whatever and they decide to try it out - just curious, you know - and they do - they steal a little snippet from dad's vodka bottle or a roach from mom's ashtray - and that's that. They like it or they don't. They giggle and say dumb stuff with their friends and go home. They either come again or decide it's not really for them. And when they come again - boy do they ever. It takes up space in every part of their life. We've got a whole generation, America - a whole generation of kids who get through 16 with a bottle or a pill. So - that said, most kids find drugs with a crowd, or at least a group of tightly knits. I kinda stumbled onto it alone. There was some old codeine - bottles of it - in the cupboard. Or maybe - maybe my first experience was from the whiskey bottle, or the box of wine in the fridge. Then again - I know that right around the same time I got the bright idea to huff gasoline. To tell truth, I can't really remember how I started, or what with, except to recall that it was a lone endeavor - some thing I did by myself in solitude - some lonesome adventure I decided to take with only myself and my imagination. It was probably a day I stayed home from school sick. "Sick", as I often was starting in middle school. I remember, one morning, actually trying to throw myself down the stairs of our old house in Redford (in middle school, mind you) to try and get out of going to school. There was some project I just hadn’t done. Beyond that, in addition to that and more importantly - I *hated* school. I hated myself, I hated people, I hated the way I thought they looked at me. I was just not a happy camper - you know the liminal period at 12 or 13 when you realize that you're a toad or something - that was me, and I dealt with it by withdrawing. I had never had many friends, or, at least - let me rephrase that. I had had friends, but none that knew how to be friends, or to whom i knew how to be a friend.

So in any case - where was I? I was coming up the driveway, darkly lit - the cool blue evening descending in tongues of warmthless fire. Up the gravel driveway, past the shed, up the narrow sidewalk to the careening, scenic house which was the Jongkinds;'. It was a nice old house, on decent property in the village of Lake Orion, with a high-steeped roof, two floors, a porch light that always burned. Very homey. The Jongkinds were jewelers, and they, as independent business people and artisans, had known better times. But they kept the house, moving into hourly jobs as jewelers (Mr. Jongkind, at least - Mrs. Jongkind stayed home with a debilitating degenerative disorder. She could still walk around and was, for most intents and purposes, just fine, but she got weak very easily, was up most of the night, slept swell into the day (now, of course, her habits and manners of ingesting her sleeping medication might have something to do with the odd sleeping hours, but I would be the last to say anything of the sort)). They kept their jewelry business on the side, habiting art shows as vendors, for which Andy and I would regularly be employed hauling disassembled glass cases, wooden benches, crates of jewelry, up from the downstairs workshop into the clunky old econoline they used to flit between show and house on the weekend.

My dad had pulled out of the driveway and I felt an exhilarating rush of anticipation - a small burn of adrenaline pounding ever so slightly up from the sternum, spreading its warm net across my face and body, arcing across my veins - anticipation at the adventure beginning - the unfolding of the evening into new frontiers. I rang the doorbell and waited.

To finish telling my story - I had met Andy at this magnet school, and our first encounter had been a sort of coded, roundabout way of finding out that the other used. It started because, quite frankly, he was a weirdo, and withdrawn, and I was drawn to those who looked and felt as uncomfortable and socially uncouth as I did. That was how it began -= I must say that my first impression of Andy was not that great. He was sort of hunched over in the back row at orientation, and I was, I guess, in my own way, trying to meet people, or, in fact, in my very own way and only in looking back on it - trying to help him out. Trying to reach out to someone who looked as ashamed and uncomfortable with themselves as I felt - and in so doing somehow to reach out to myself.

\*\*

I stepped away from the page for a day or so. I get so nervous about telling tales; not about the story itself, or anything, but that, somehow, like elves in the night, when I wake up to the page again the story will have been whisked away like cookies. I worry that I won't be able to tell it, I mean. The best way to write (and to read, for that matter) is in one sitting - come to the page with the intent in mind of wrapping up, of hitting an endpoint, and do it. Breaks are incredibly anxious gaps of time and space - the same person who left the cursor blinking might not, you know - might not be the same person anymore. The person who starts the story ought to finish it, right then, while they're still themselves, and still the person to tell their story. All sorts of strange things might happen otherwise. For example, you might get two stories, instead of one. Or (depending on how many times you step away to regroup) three, or four - an infinite number of stories, only pretending to be one - a gaggle of unruly stories under the thin, ghost-like sheet of a title or chapter. Now, of course, if you're writing a novel you can't do that all at once (unless you're Jack Kerouac and have got lots of cheap speed close at hand) - but you can do chapters singularly. As a single act, I mean. Write them as a single person, so that, if it's someone different who sits down to write the next chapter, why - at least it will be a new chapter, and the very worst sort of thing you can expect to come out of such an endeavor is something like an anthology, which is entirely reasonable.

The short of that - we'll try to get back on track, and then to finish, even if it takes awhile. We'll just hit the ground running and run until we get where we're going.

So I don’t remember exactly what happened when I got there. I went over to Andy’s house so many times in the following years, and in the months before that, that that single memory, of coming up the driveway, of entering the house, is composed of a ghostly chorus of memories and moments, all those entrances building up on each other until any singular experience, any one voice is indistinguishable from the symphony of the crowd. But I can tell you what it was normally like and pick out some things, some small things that were true. Sometimes his dad would answer the door, if he was working in the basement workshop. He worked long hours at a jewelry shop in the mall - repairing, cleaning, that kind of thing - and then would come home to put more hours in in his personal workshop, sanding, molding, making their own jewelry. They were a very artistic, in many ways educated, well-read family, and Andy picked up a keen sense of intelligence from them. This was not exactly bookish intelligence (although it touched on that), but a sort of jury-rigger’s spirit that made him quite good with machines, fixing things, building project - you name it. Andy loved to experiment with different kinds of chemicals, and definitely to set things on fire.

Sometimes his dad would answer the door, with his work goggles (a lime-green headset with magnifying lenses) pushed up above his face, resting at the top of his head. Everyone in Andy’s family wore glasses - thick glass, I think his dad wore *tri-*focals. Mr. Jongkinds fingers were always stained black from dirt and grime and burns, the ugly palette of which worked its way into his skin and under his nails permanently. His nails were cracked. But he always had this terrible smirk on his face, like he had just pulled some really heinous prank, but of course Mr. Jongkind had to pretend to be too old for that kind of thing, and so the smirk ended up looking world-weary.

In any case it could have been his dad who came to the door, or it could have been him, wandering around the dining room or the kitchen, or descending with headphones on from the top of the stairs where his bedroom was.

The next part is a blur. I came over. Another of his friends was joining us. We were going to trip (I had never tripped before; like I said, most of my drug experiences had been on my own, except for this newly blooming thing where I used at Andy’s house, which was really incredibly exciting because I got to have a friend on a different level, you know? We would snort his medication (ritalin) and stay up for hours talking about the most ludicrous things (or, at least now, under the veil of time and the tragic change of the guard, I call them ludicrous, knowing they must have been - but at the time they weren’t. We were talking about the oddest, deepest, most intimate things that I had never talked about before, and somehow it didn’t matter that we were using drugs to talk about them, only that we did, and this was one of the most exciting times of my life for that very reason - we talked. I really can’t remember what it was we talked about. Our families, perceived hardships, social anxieties, girls - really ridiculous things, sometimes, too - absolutely ludicrous things, I don’t even remember.)

One of his friends was meeting us - he would trip too. Andy got the drugs because I was really sort of socially limited - Andy was too, in his way, but less so in that arena. I mean, he knew the people who used, whereas I, yet, didn’t. His name was Alex and I had never met him before. I don’t remember when we took the acid. I don’t remember much of Halloween. Alex arrived. After I did. His parents dropped him off. I know that we took some acid before going out, because I remember, when we got back and we were waiting for Alex’s parents to pick him up, how incredibly daring and dangerous (and, in some part of my mind - careless) it was for him to go back into that situation tripping. Not that I thought anything of it at Andy’s house - we just used drugs there. We had used drugs there for quite some time and for some reason I perceived it as safe, although we were always worried about them finding us out. We weren’t tripping very hard at all, I know, because I had never tripped before and I was really just fine. Later on (I quite awhile later on - at my sixteenth birthday, maybe) I would really trip, and from that know that, that night, at that time, I was barely scratching the surface of tripping. Later that night I took some more and there was a definite effect, but then all I had were some very minor visuals - slight patterns forming, maybe a trace of unnatural warmth in the cheeks. None of the gut-splitting terror that comes with actually tripping.

So I don’t remember going out trick-or-treating. Only some very faint images - that’s all, in the end, I have - faint images, tracing paper, a reconstructed storyline that must fit the picture.

There is always an incredible amount of confusion associated with acid. There is no telling, ever, when and how it will come. It could be fake, and often is. By about the end of the first hour you’re starting to question. Did this guy rip me off? Have I been had again? By the end of the second hour you’re really cursing him, up and down - you never know when it will come. Sometimes, too, it will catch you off guard - you think you have an hour to get where you need to, and then, twenty minutes in BAM there it is screaming up your ribcage bam bam beating in the heart ripping out your eyelids shoving purple manta rays down your ears feeding you noises - mmmm, television static raining purple pink pulse, pulse, pulse - - -

So I remember, from the night - flashes - a porch light, going up to the house in a group, the thrill of trick-or-treating well past the age when it was appropriate - working on that terrible, shame-faced but don’t you love me? smile that I would develop over the next few years (that I had actually learned with Andy’s parents, that I had learned was a way to do whatever I want and excuse it with). Trick-or-treating was short - the streets empty out quickly, after an hour, hour and a half. Not much was happening, yet, with the acid. Sitting in the antechamber with Alex (where was Andy?) making small talk - waiting for his parents to come. Asking him about the acid - going back to his house like that - him saying he did it all the time, he wasn’t worried about it.

And then that night. It came so quickly. Andy and I whispered about our drugs, how much we had, waited expectantly for his parents to drift to bed (when I stayed the night sometimes his dad would stay upstairs so we could stay downstairs in the TV room - that meant that they were oh-so-far away and we could take whatever we wanted - and they did. The house emptied. It was dark. There is something very different, very real, when you’re alone with your drugs - there’s so much subterfuge, when you’re trying to pass it off in public, or to get through some situation where it would be inappropriate to be high (and this is the state that describes the majority of a teenage user’s life). But then - when you’re alone with the thing, this beast you’ve been courting, just waiting for the moment to get alone with it - then it’s a different story - that bastard has fangs. And so the house emptied out - the house pulsed. Everything got quiet. Andy had more acid, but his wasn’t doing any good, because he had tripped just the day before or whatever -

“when you take acid, you have to wait three days in between trips, otherwise you have to double up to get the same effect”

so he offered me his part, another couple hits, and said to put one, get this, under my eye, to put it in the open, blood-lined chamber that’s revealed when one pulls the corner of his eye down - to cut the yellowed paper in half, to put the tab half there, half here, to put one on the tongue (never swallow acid - always let it sit on your tongue until the whole thing dissolves - there are all these little tricks and rules that arte part and parcel of entrance into a drug culture).

so i did. two more hits, maybe three. there were some slight visuals - it was weak acid, but three hits of weak acid makes for strong acid - that were there from the first hit. it had taken quite awhile to sink in - we waited. maybe we watched tv, or something, or started to talk. he went to the kitchen to get some liquor, to steal some whiskey from his parents - just a bit, a bit - you trip and i’ll tip (but andy’s a terrible drinker).

I have to say, now, that I’m wondering why I wrote this. I had wanted to go through the past, to write something I know, to find something truthful - but this, this is not - I mean, I don’t want to glorify the drugs. I want to tell the truth of it, how it was, what ruptured there in my heart, then and forever before and after, to show that single instant of rupture which was no rupture at all but really an unveiling, a revelation of the truth that sneakingly swum around under the surface every day, that just needed some trauma to puncture the ice and come roaring out - or not roaring but making sickly gooshing and gurgling sounds like some drowning, half-decaying animal not meant for the water but - there it is, in the water, stuck under there for too long until the skin begins to rot - surfacing, nonetheless.

And the closer I get to finishing, as I approach the moment that seemed important, as I try to bring something back from beyond that boundary that separates now from then, here from there, or me from - you or anyone else - it fades. I crumple in on myself, I shake my head, I say, “no use.” What good can come of it? What salvageable? What emptiness redeemed which is not already redeemed? It really was nothing, just an event - not even an event, not even marked with the prestige of that name, “event”, just a night - a single night from a long (not even that long - short, in fact - or not short but neither short nor long - a period of time, an allotted number of years neither lengthy nor brief, but some interminable, indeterminable period -) life - just one night. One day of many. Like this day, this very day where I sit and type, where you sit and read, or not.

Dare I call this a day? A moment? An hour?

The issue becomes more clear: dare I *call* it? Dare I give it a name, any definitive thing. In naming we change, in calling into existence, in defining the thing - and defining is an act whose purpose is preservation - we irrevocably alter it. Change its namelessness. Narration is a naming. So - less, then, of me - Please don’t take this as some academic platitude spouting the power of the reader. Yes, you have the ability to name, too. But don’t. Call it nothing. Less of me, less of you. Let this be as it is.

That night I did trip. Andy got sloshed. Too drunk. I thought he would die. But before that, there was this necklace - this necklace my girlfriend gave me, which Andy tried to eat. Jerk. He tried to eat it because he knew it’d piss her off. Andy’s a terrible drinker. I think I dug it out of his mouth. Andy kept going back - back - for another sip of whiskey or, as he got drunker, another swallow, another long draught - the whole bottle, maybe. I tripped. I remember a terror, as he had the necklace - there was something so symbolic, and I knew she’d be terribly angry if I “lost” it. And he was really trying to eat it - destroy it - or maybe just make me uncomfortable - but in any case - intense symbolic charge, like electricity, on everything. I got the necklace back. I let Andy do his thing. I went into the bathroom. I remember looking at myself in the mirror - seeing the edges change into some golden arch, some-ivy shawled opening into the beyond - watching my face, the wall behind me crawling with flowers - turn equine, my ears grow long, my face changed - I was not who I was, finally - I was not who I was - and I reached out my hand and - just about to touch, just about to break through and some terrible noise from the kitchen - Andy on the floor with his bottle of sleeping pills, the pink pills spilling onto the floor, some crushed, some in his hand - terribly drunk, barely conscious, lolling on the floor - he’d fallen, his legs not working right - trying to get the pills into his mouth and I was instantly down on the floor with him, pulling his wrist away, fighting with him - just please give it back - just please stop now - just please stop now - and fighting with him and him and some level really *wanting* to die, but too drunk, and getting him away from the pills and putting them back in the bottle and putting the bottle on the counter and grabbing andy’s shoulder - he’s still sprawled on the floor, his legs sort of flopping, trying to get up, or at least, that’s where his head is pointed, but his eyes are half back in his skull and he’s *far out* - and I put my arm under his shoulder and pull and his head lolls on his neck a little bit and he gets his legs underneath him and finally gets up and we stagger through the bathroom to the tv room where he falls, before we get to the couch, on the floor, and i try to help him up again, but he’s lying there, and I want to get back to the bathroom, to the mirror - i’m really tripping now, so this is terrifying - charged with extra-intensity - everything incredibly intense - charged with murderous significance absolute adrenaline - and I want to get back to the mirror - to see that other place, that quiet grove I’d almost reached my hand into, just almost put my hand through the glass to touch that *other* self - that other, blessed me who was not as I was, and there is this terrible paisley print pattern on the walls of the tv room and it looks like fish, thousands of these fractal-like fish spinning, some sort of reptilian, skeletal fish spinning and singing and speaking on the walls and they’re singing a song and what exactly is happening? but I want to get back to the bathroom and Andy’s on the floor sort of lolling around doing something I can’t quite tell or see but I get almost back to the bathroom and I am about to look in the mirror and I hear something, pop my head back in the tv room and he’s got a knife, he’s brought a knife back with him from the kitchen and he’s trying to slash his wrists but he’s too bleeding drunk and so there i am on the floor again wrestling with him trying to -please, stop, just stop just please - Andy --- *Andy - stop please just please just* -and those beady eyes are red now, yes red and there’s barely any Andy left, or maybe just the Andy left that I never cared to see and he’s sees only some disembodied hand between him and his goal and he’s - what do i - *panic -* he’s going for me and i’ve already got his wrist but he’s - *man* he’s strong but he’s - really drunk so i --- edge his wrist over and finally smack his hand on the ground and get the knife out of his hands and fine - fine - and i take it to the kitchen and come back and andy’s just lying there - just lying there and everything is weird and spinning and there are patterns on the walls and - he’s just lying there and i bend down and try to see if he’s breathing but *everything* is breathing and I think - what should I do? What should I do should I wake up his parents? and immediately the room is filled with ambulance sirens and everything is screaming and - a gaping hole in my sternum - i’m so desperate and scared and so i - *Andy* - bend down and tap the side of his face and his head just slumps the other way and so I - desperate now I - *Andy!* - and I smack his face and he just lays there and I - *ANDY!* - and smack his face REAL good I can feel the sting and those beady little eyes crack open and they’re red, they’re very red but here they are they’re cracked open just the slightest bit and I say *Andy* - and he grunts a little just a little incomprehensible sound, a slur less than words and I - *Andy!* you’ve gotta get to the couch and those eyes drift shut and I’m *angry* now, angry that I have to go through this, angry that this has to happen tonight, angry that I’m terrified and I haul off and *SLAP* him a good one and that opens his eyes a little bit and I -*Andy* - it’s time to go to the couch - and a little slur, a little mumble - *Andy* - *it’s - time - to -go - to - the -couch* and I slap his face again a little bit, not quite so hard but still *hard* , and he stumbles up and I sort of get behind him and push and I -just get to the couch, Andy, if you can just make it the couch - and he reaches his arm out a little bit and grabs onto the arm of the couch and manages to, me pushing, drag himself up and collapse there and he’s already out and i’m - calm down - calm down -. my breathing comes in ragged, pounding breaths, those patterns spinning, but adrenaline - *lots* of adrenaline - has put the visuals - has put vision back in place enough for a moment to get me through this terrible, terrible instant - and I’m checking to see if he’s alright and going back out into the kitchen to see if there are anymore pills on the floor and how the whiskey bottle looks and if there’s anything I missed and - are we gonna get found out? - and my heart is pounding and I hear a terrible, echoing *retch* from the tv room and he’s thrown up *everywhere* - *everywhere* he’s thrown up and as I come in he lets go again - *everywhere* over the couch and floor it sort of rockets out and he seems to be a little better (by that i mean he might not die) but still barely conscious and he drags himself up and - the *smell i-* and i come next to him and he leans on me as we go to the bathroom and he turns on the sink and tries to lift his leg up there and he washes off a little bit and - he is *far* out - and I help him - stumbling, through the tv room out to the family room and - god he’s a burden, hard to drag around when drunk and get him onto the bigger couch out there and come into the family room and - there is no way, no way to clean this up - and i just stare at the mess, the smell - and think - what? what can i do? and the fish reply in menacing sing-song so i go out beside the couch, on the other side of the short table, and lay on the plush carpet and stare at the ceiling and little maggots start to gnaw through the ceiling and the floor - the fallout is tremendous and - just ignore it - ignore it - and i huddle up and am terrified and emptied and little maggots crawl into my chest and eventually - eventually somewhere i drift - drift -

\*\*

In the morning I remember - lying on the floor, the light of the sun filtering through the window. Noises of breakfast float through the house, the overlay of food cutting a clean track through the stagnant aroma of vomit, whiskey, and terror. Now is when I wish I could curl up and die. I peek at the couch, but Andy's already up, so here I am alone on the floor, with no more hallucinatory maggots, only real emotional maggots digging around inside my hemorrhaging chest. Rot. Andy’s head pops around the corner and he guesses I’m up - “We’ve got,” he says, “some cleaning to do.”

There’s almost no word from his parents, except his dad says we need to clean it up, and puts on his stoniest face, which at the time I thought was a clever parenting strategy, but now I realize was only him not knowing what, what in the world to do with us.

I got up and went to the couch and threw myself down there, staring. There was something missing behind my eyes, some brainflesh that had dribbled off during the night. From all of this, there was something of me missing, some part that had gone away somewhere, some terrible, empty ache whose source I didn't even know. And isn't that so, with the worst sorts of losses? With the deepest losses, we're likely not to know what we've lost, because even that memory has vanished like some fog that burns away in the daylight, knowing only that some absence has presented itself, when and where, though -p-perhaps it's crept up during the night, or has been there all along, but only now revealed itself.

I stared for a long time before I clambered up and out to help Andy hose down the cushions.

\*\*

I am sometimes haunted by memories. There have been many lives and many lifetimes in my one short one, and the specters of these faded apparitions sometimes flare to life from within me, the crackle of some psychic sparkler burning to life unexpectedly, and I wonder, "Who was that? What strange gears turned, that these events could have happened?" And the day is plunged into dream.

There have been many lives, in my one short one. Things arise in memory which are absolutely incommensurable, inexplicable to my present circumstances and self, and which cause me to question the reality of any. What a strange order we are subjected to, where men are permitted many lives. One, even - but my many are almost a burden, a gift whose debt is too great, so that I am sold into the slavery of gratitude and grace.

I pan through this turgid silt of memory.

What is *real*? When these events - I've said it, I say it again - which are only images, only faded sparks of film which may not have even existed - screech to life in the projector room of the mind - what is there? Images, the reality of which has been swallowed by the insubstantial darkness (which is also peace, and comfort - the melancholic sleep of eternal dream and infinite slumber, yes -) of memory, and which it produces like so much sleight-of-hand - and the worst, there are no faces, no names, no numbers - any others who share the swim in these deep waters are only images, only, only - they are only my mind's lonely record of beings that *were*, that may have existed once but now are no more, and so their existence, even, though it *was* at one time, through memory is reduced to *wasn't*, what seems substantial, if passed away, revealed in its substanceless pith - a core of loneliness and remorse and shadow. So I sift, I run the images that flow across me through this merciful pan, sifting, sifting - intent on the vision, piercing, seeking, - for a kernel of rare-yellow gleam to peer out from the hand-numbing waters, and to follow that - upstream, through the infinite possible forkings, to the summit, the peak, the mouth from out of which they issue -

Determined to hit gold, not die out here in the wilderness. I set my mind, my lip. Nod my head a little bit to myself, look westward - follow that trail, ever upwards - forge ahead. Find the final gold-vein, the Promise obtained by my fathers - where the sun bites through the flesh of the earth, where two worlds touch - and it shakes off flecks of gold as it burrows into the deep. That's the gold-vein I'm after, the one I'm determined to find.

Forever forward.



# iv. Through All My Life, a Race for Beauty

# iv. through all my life, a race for beauty: What Was Lost

What Was Lost pp. 1-xx. 1998-2001

[image]

\[insert NIN school pic\]

there is a simple suffering

in the way your chest falls while you sleep

in the way I watch you,

silent,

your fingers sewing breast to sheet.

there is a simple suffering

in the tongue between your teeth

in your laughter wrapped in twilight

in the whisper of the leaves.

there is a simple suffering

in the voice beneath your lashes

in the way it etches,

wordless,

a trail to skin beneath the ashes.

There is a simple suffering.

# iv (continued). What Was Lost

# iv. through all my life, a race for beauty: What Was Lost

What Was Lost pp. 1-xx. 1998-2001

[image]

\[insert NIN school pic\]

there is a simple suffering

in the way your chest falls while you sleep

in the way I watch you,

silent,

your fingers sewing breast to sheet.

there is a simple suffering

in the tongue between your teeth

in your laughter wrapped in twilight

in the whisper of the leaves.

there is a simple suffering

in the voice beneath your lashes

in the way it etches,

wordless,

a trail to skin beneath the ashes.

There is a simple sufferin

Stars circle / I reel from nature’s opiate.

dark purple, / youth’s color, dreams obliterate

black jackal, / teeth gaping, dripping wide

silk shackle, / chains born by comfort’s tide

shall I calm my love tonight? / shall I drown and strip, restrain?

shall I burn the flame to flicker bright? / then see by wisps of smoke remain?

shall I live a moment, die a life? / such sacrifice, for brief respite

but shall I give up grasping fairy’s flight? / shall I dream a day without dark night?

will I cut my heart and, willing, bleed? / or shall I go on chasing poppy seeds?

# vii. The Creeping Disease

# vii. The Creeping Disease

**mid-late 2001**

[image]

“untitled”

that way she walks is

silently enticing-

that way she moves through sound waves shadows

my waking mind-

a thousand times she’s surfaced.

the neighborhood is dark

from where i stand and smoke on the porch.

the street is full,

a thousand ghosts all running

from their waking mind, the shower

of a thousand purple comets in the backdrop.

a film of frost on everything.

so here i am.

if i could scream i

if i could run i

if i could grab the sky and pull i

would only stand here smoking.

frost crystals more

diamond precious than the

unique suffering of trains.

a whistle moans in the distance and

a dream of dreams is weeping.

**nobody, not even the rain, has such small hands**

Her hand stroked his face, his back, his chest. It was dark; fingers had taken the place of eyes.

“Here....” she whispered, “I feel your pale heart.” The hand reached lower. “Here... I feel your white stomach...” her hand draped down once more and his body grew surreptitiously still. “Remember to breath,” she purred.

“I...” his mind pulsed faster than his heart.

“What’s wrong?”

“Nothing,” a compression of inhaled air, then, “Nothing.”

“I know you better than that.” Quick breaths stretched out for three tremulous cycles.

“It’s j-...” A radio hummed in the background. His eyes searched for hers and found only opaque shadows. It hadn’t been so dark the night before, he remembered being able to see her grey-blue eyes. “It’s just that... wh-...”

“Are you scared?” She did not ask it like an attack, but it battered about his ears and into the pale heart.

“No. Well.... yes, but...” His hands groped the night, as if appealing some fathomless god to send him words. “This is just different, you know? This isn’t... isn’t puppy love messing around anymore... it’s not...” His searching hands failed him. “Dammit!” The low curse hissed into 2 AM radio pop. “How can I say this? This starts a whole new world, you know? This is the end of... it’s just an end. It means the start of quick fucks and, and apartments and.... Christ! I don’t know.”

She reached for his hand like last night, and the night before. Her voice did not feel this. Her voice bore no empathy or pain, only concern. “You don’t have to.” It was spoken in a tone for soothing children.

“No, no, that’s not what I mean.” His tone slapped away her comfort. “I want to.” His lips searched for hers. His were furtive; hers were red. Moments passed and their breathing quickened again. His hand brought hers to his chest and centered it over his pale, pale heart.

Words sprang forth very close to her face. “I want to.” Their lips met softly. “It’s just that the pain,” he pressed her hand down and the ticking in his chest vibrated through her eager fingers, “will be just as great as the pleasure.”

For a long time, they lost themselves in sounds that were infinite, much deeper and older than they. Soft petals and a blanket closed over their heads, drowning out the morning. The night looked on and quiet things were born in darkness.

\[high school grad photo\]

July 14th, 2001

Madame,

I’m in a writing mood, so your first letter is going to be one that was written long ago. I talked to you about communication deficiency and the faults of language; I think it might just be me. Not to say that language doesn’t have its problems, I’ve just come to think the problem lies at the edge of a far more personal sphere. This fucking writer’s block I’ve been experiencing is more than just a fleeting lack of ideas or ingenuity. Something clicked on that website. Or maybe it wasn’t the website, maybe it was the morphine, or any number of things, maybe my damn 2 + 2 = 5 reality control bullshit finally found a purchase to do some damage.

Suffice to say: it’s bled into more than just my writing. I feel dull and sterile. There are a million beautiful tapestries billowing in the shady borders, I’ve never, in my life, been unable to turn those into something. Anything! It’s a horrible feeling to have them sit, alive, while my hand is vacant. I feel almost desperate.

But- I’m being overdramatic. If you’re wondering, this is the day after we spent the night at Kristina’s, happy pandas and all. It’s before work. No one’s home and the windows are open. A train just went by, it’s still rumbling and weeping (not too far down the tracks). I am tired and my mouth tastes like chips and morphine, but my hand smells like you. From as far away as this paper.

I’ve been thinking. I talked about values last night. My standards are fucking unnatural and steep, I’ve decided the only way I can ever meet them is by:

a\) shooting myself in the head

b\) becoming a religious nut

c\) changing the world.

I’m trying to set the stage for changing the world and I’ve made provisions to get bullets. If the bullets don’t kill me I must be Jesus, in which case I can change the world *and* become a religious nut.

Pardon me for being a sulky bastard. You know, I’ve always kinda wished we could talk a little better. Not wished really, just thought we could. It’s hard. I have to tell you something, I guess. Not have to tell you, just musing.

There’s a very fine line between intimacy and losing one’s self (as far as emotional intimacy goes). I think maybe we could walk that line. I dunno. It’s a frightening place. How can you be really intimate with a person and also not be under their control to one degree or another? I’m blathering. Sleep deprived half-real mumbo jumbo. Half real, half real. Write me back, tell me about things.

Love you much,

CAT CAT

HAT CATHETER

HAG METER

RAIN

each association breaks the barrier, so

pop more morphine before the

whale comes

you are too small your

harpoon will rust in even better

weather, even

degrees below the banter line,

which scrambled my eggs.

bitter butter makes the batter

beg for sympathy,

BITTER

BITCHIER

like cheerleaders

“This really, and I mean *really,* scrambles my mambo eggs my man,” fumes Demerol the Turtle, picking fleas from underneath his shell.

“I mean, I mean really, man, what kind of non-sequitor would stop that whale from *hoppin’*, man,” his Negro fingers snapped a congo.

Mme.,

The tenor and flecks of foam on that last one were mostly due to lack of morphine. I just think that, if you really want to be close, you should be more considerate. Not ingratiating, just aware.

~

First of all, John’s been living there for two weeks and he’s already trashed the place and got an eviction notice for violating Article 17 (being too loud, passing out on the front lawn, being, in general, a vagrant drunkard). I hesitate to go into details on the condition of their kitchen.

Around 2:00am they started talking about a window they’d seen open at the elementary school, they all walked down there while the rest of us watched the Shining. About half an hour later they all filed in carrying appliances, Dominika squealing, “Now we can buy coke!” in her Polish accent. They had a TV, a computer, 2-way radios, a box of Captain Kangaroo movies, and they were going back to pick up a microwave and a toaster they’d left outside. Later, they went out and robbed people’s cars, pills, credit cards, etc.. I went to sleep around 4, and got a call from them at 6 saying they needed a ride because the wheel had fallen off their car. When I got there they were standing outside the car with at least eight cartons of cigarettes in their arms. They bought me a full tank of gas.

While this was all fun and games, it troubles me because John is a good friend and he’s going to end up in prison. Dominika the Dominatrix is whipping on his natural tendency to screw himself over. Also, remember Ken? There’s at least one person who has NO good fucking reason to be out there robbing shit.

Hand is tired,

love you,

<u>water lilies screaming at me</u>

twice the poltergeist have

shaved the windows,

closed the mouse,

left the daughter cold and shaking,

saying prayers to

calm the clock.

she cried until it’s face read 3:00.

\~~

I think it’s the first stage in a writing metamorphous. It’s clunky now, but I’ve been idle for a while. I’m more aware of what I’m doing this time around, as far as the organs and flesh of my

d o o d l e s

\~~

EVERY TH O

I WAS

NG K.

I’m down to 15mgs (morphine). I’m also wearing a nicotine patch, which I’m currently removing to smoke.

I dunno. I just currently feel a lack in the expressive power of letters. Want to do more, you know? Want to make sure this doesn’t degenerate into some kind of HI I DID THIS AND THIS I AM AN ARIES BYE pen pal sort of thing,

it’s hard to not have morphine.

Miss you,

<u>Louisiana</u>

Her shoulders fell while wilting missing roses,

two white petals

cling electric, feed the static on her cheek.

fingers crack on light bulb.

Sun shone soft wine, closing eyes on rhododendron,

dandelion,

piercing button tongue,

winter daisies,

frosted autumn traceries.

She sighs because the shade is seizing,

eating sparrows under streetlights.

Tuesday bled nice letters,

only paring words and

forcing growth on Wednesday.

The *last* time we

ticked in

July.

In New Orleans the summer’s restless,

scratching sand and rocks and angels,

rootless ‘til your rain.

August 1st

My Dearest Mme.,

\~~

...The worst thing about it is that every time you try to quit you realize your smoking is less addiction and more deliberate commitment to that path of action. It’s crazy, cuz withdrawals are never <u>really that bad</u>. It’s just kind of unwillingness to work for any movement.

I think most addicts are lazy people.

You should really check out Ezra Pound, everything he writes is the fruit of some incomprehensible inner machination that I can’t fathom.

I think it really is the morphine (mostly) that’s causing my writer’s block. That, and I think I’ve made poetry seem too important. Do you understand? When you raise one thing above all others, set your universe to revolve around it, and realize it’s gone?

I think the last poem I wrote is definitely subpar. No motion in it, nothing engaging to a reader.

miss you,

August 3rd, 2001

My Dearest Lauren Juleff,

Still trying to quit smoking, was doing well until last night when we got the morphine. Little blue pills reduce the will to ashes.

oh well.

I was tied with one or two other people for having the best score on the Philosophy midterm, which makes me feel confident about how I’m going to do in college.

All right, check it out, I can’t remember if I told you this or not, so if I’m repeating myself be patient.

The Walrus is Paul, right?

Have you ever read the poem about the walrus and the carpenter in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland? It’s a parody of religion, with the carpenter representing Christianity (Jesus) and the Walrus representing some Eastern religion (Buddha). They lure all these oysters out of the water and eat them.

Did you know that Lewis Carroll (Alice’s author) is on the cover of Sgt. Pepper’s? Also, the Beatles were big into Buddhism then, so, therefore, it’s likely that Paul (the Walrus) has to be the living Buddha. Capiche?

I kind of regret being plunged back into the constant morphine haze. I makes me feel soulless (it’s kicking in right now). Have you been taking morphine, and if so, are you soulless? What color is your spirit guide and does he wear a bra? Are you wearing a bra?

Alex the Bastard Kurth just stopped by. I sold him five pills at \$2 a piece to get him outta my damn face and he acted like I was ripping him off. Ahhh! This has dissolved into fragments.

Love you,

the telephone is shooting bursts of steam spiraling up

between its nostrils, hooting, growling, lashing its

tail, nettled by the boss that’s underneath it.

the morphine is nervous, flitting from wall to wall

of the vein, tapping dusty wings against the

heart that feeds it.

the cigarettes have lost it, brooding, sulking, dashing

up with twisted neck, cackling throat,

stoic when they’re burning and screaming when the pain stops.

My ears are ringing.

My excuses are drugging the day.

My eyes are red and steaming, they have no

ghosts behind them.

August 6th, 2001

Mme.,

I broke down crying like three times today, i think I’m totally upset about my parents. I’ve been arguing with Andy all the time. That thing with my mom was just too much, you know?

My secret condescending thoughts are grinning, hiding in the ceiling fans because you’ve spotted them and given a good one two. They think you’re the dentist and (they haven’t been in quite awhile) are making sure to keep their mouths closed.

My thoughts on moments (the more upstanding, respectable thoughts who’re drinking wine in formal wear): I just meant that no matter how much weight a memory has, the event might not matter tomorrow. Moments don’t carry over because they turn into only memory, and what good is a memory if it has no place in the present? In fact, what good’s a memory if it <u>does</u> have a place in the present? if it has a place, all the accumulated sneezes and bandersnatch will be in the shape of the present for anyone to read, the memory is just...

a calculus book is great, right?

but if you don’t know calculus, you’ll never learn it from the book, and if, by chance, you DO know calculus, it’s really not that much use.

the morphine’s kicking in, too.

if only morphine was a hallucinogen. Can you imagine the flowers slowly winding their way up to the ceiling and falling down like arms or trees straight into your chest.

and then you’d have flowers in your chest.

i think i’m retracting from the world for a while. It’s getting to the point where i’m angry at everyone, just hurtling forward with teeth bared to prove that I’M RIGHT! It seems like the only option when everyone else is obviously wrong. seriously, it seems like most of the people i’m close to have flawed veins, and i’m so determined not to end up like them that i’m just being stubborn and forceful, mentally violent, you know? the point being that i need to step back from the world a foot or two, until <u>i’m peaceful</u>.

it’s so odd. both of my parents revolt me. Not in an immediate, you’re nothing kind of way, just a sort of slow, whole psychic rejection.

My mother is absolutely miserable, stupid, and dependent, to be blithe about it. She won’t compromise a conversation in the favor of another person an inch, even if she knows nothing about the subject and the other person has evidence.

I DON’T KNOW I DON’T KNOW I DON’T KNOW.

that’s not true, because i don’t hate my mom and it’s horrible of me to call her stupid; i just don’t wanna be like her. she can’t function independently.

and i’m not going to start on my dad. he’s happy at the expense of the destruction of another human being.

I DON’T WANNA BE LIKE THEM, but I’m so... raging, that I’m blinding myself, just in different ways.

\~~

apologies for that, I forgot I was writing for a while, and I try not to read over these letters, so it probably makes little sense.

this letter may (and/or may not) be one large fragment sentence.

LOVE IS NOT A CONTRACT.

I love you,

p.s. I’ll write again tomorrow.

I wrote this a long time ago and just found it at my work. It’s patchy and turns to shit after the first stanza, but you’re in it.

I measure life in milligrams.

(there is a girl with eyes so black the

heroin rings can’t dance beneath her basement,

her feet shimmer summer dresses and her

needles always stamp the same inscription:

LOVE, 100 mgs)

Five years ago it was pot warrens

twisting eyes on spring evenings,

with the smoke closet where the

secret addicts sat,

powder trailing tears like snot from

shining eyes.

angel lines ran at angles parallel to

concrete roses, plastic hearts.

I wrote it down and

polished silver numbers in the aftermath.

Now there’s Lauren.

Heaven dimmed to neutral markers,

scarlet light bulbs and brown crayolas.

There was blood on her back when I traced flesh letters,

fading in daylight and flaking away.

Never measure love in milligrams.

END

remember when i wrote that on your back? anyways, keep all this writing i’m sending you together, you have the only copies of most of it and i might want/be able to edit and make them good someday.

love,

\~~

August 12th, 2001

my mother is telling my sister what a vicious person my father is.

(behind me is a picture)

[image: Macintosh HD:Users:ctrueme1:Desktop:AtLwM:atlwm scans:images 7.jpeg]

can you believe this?

they thought they’d be together forever and stayed in love for 23 years.

now my mother is an obnoxious drunk and my father tells himself stories to make pretend he’s happy.

i thought i could rise above them, but it was all just pride fizzle.

i didn’t even know my parents weren’t invincible until i turned fourteen. I had no friends but my parents or only fleeting and half... my social incompetence until i was nine. i didn’t even learn how to function aesthetically normally in social situations until... late 16.

and i realize that my introversion, introspection... grasping at

being justified

was just pretend, my parents are both broken.

i fear for the afterlife.

p.s. sorry the other pages are illegible. i love you too.

maybe if i let the fire rip and shred the morning towels i can write a word or two that dries the skin or

catches eyes.

No one is special, and i think the world would be more beautiful if we knew it, special is a complicated structure of masturbating to naked pictures of things we were born with.

Towers of Babel toppling and breaking off in fractals of the language a god gave us.

a God

God

no nourishment and starving you said, i say we make an effigy of the body and hang it on walls in public places for passersby to rape and spit on, i say i have no God because of choice, i say that every splinter slap and tribulation-

is just my fault.

in the next life we’ll all be such shriveled blinded little creatures, feeding on the natural spirit and too goddamned afraid of *anything* *better than ourselves* to look up put of the misery and find a divine force

i say all puppy dogs should die.

i say morphine and cocaine.

i say i staked everything on finding the fountain of spiritual youth where words spill out of my hand like forgotten rocks

and maybe mountains.

*and i lost hardcore.*

i say that even now i’m tearing apart the soul of this jabberish, and soon i’ll be staring at it or writing from an adulterated spot of the mind.

Lauren, you are awfully far away and i’m afraid of ghosts and fathers and the cyclops, and maybe God and Buddha, most especially Walruses and *living.*

i do not want to shoot myself in the head or die at thirty from arterial sclerosis or yell at my mother

*or become an addict*

i want to write, but i’ve elevated writing to a position of moral validity, which is a conception i can’t live up to.

but what good does it do?

BE STRONG LIKE CYCLOPS!!!

at midnight my father’s ghost comes bleeding, screaming vengeance, “be strong, be strong,” and i shatter all the little villages and murder mad Mercutio... Hamlet complex.

the rain trickled down the caves and yellow things slept, waiting for the sun to camouflage, not a single daisy woke from snoring to see the pirates STEAL THE PEANUTBUTTER.

\~~

i think i’ve destroyed my writing ability. i think i’ve been subconsciously plotting against it all along, just waiting to find the perfect button to place beneath the waking mind’s foot.

August 14th, 2001

[image: Macintosh HD:Users:ctrueme1:Desktop:AtLwM:atlwm scans:images 9.jpeg]

my head is floating away and i love you and i’m getting silly jubilant

like i was fourteen and making out for the first time in a ferris wheel.

tomorrow and i’ll shoot myself or just stare in the mirror with

bullets in my hand,

forgetting all about your totem head and tadpole eyes,

but this evening is forever and can carry moments over.

August 17th, 2001

Madame,

I apologize for the clarity of my last letter, I was on morphine and coke at the time, and felt rushed. I’ll interpret it for you when I reach Louisiana, speaking of which, I need someone to pick me up from the bus station. I had finals yesterday and they went great. I got A+s in both my classes, think I had the best grade in philosophy.

The Doors of Perception is one of the most interesting books I’ve ever read. Some of his theories are extremely crack-brained, while others really hit home.

do you think the lines:

“I know, for Death comes for me

From regions of the blest afar,

Where there is nothing to deceive,

Hath left his iron gate ajar,

And rays of truth you cannot see

Are flashing thro’ Eternity.”

are Huxley’s trickles of cutting beauty from the deeper reality? Poe would certainly fit the archetype he described as “having a valve to the incommunicable world.” i think so.

i’m still smoking, as you may have guessed, and still addicted (<u>kind of</u>) to morphine and everquest (very). i can’t wait to see you on friday.

keep writing, it’s an unspeakable pleasure to get a letter every day.

yours in love,

August 20th, 2001

“People on zoloft are no fun.”

-Kemel Zaldivar AKA Uncle Smack

Prescription happy pills allow people to ignore the fact that they’re still drugging themselves, because it’s socially acceptable.
