Lauren,

i’ve been reading the House of Leaves. it’s a beautiful book. it cuts right to the quick, again and again.

“Who has never killed an hour? Not casually or without thought, but carefully: a premeditated murder of minutes. The violence comes from a combination of giving up, not caring, and a resignation that getting past is all you can hope to accomplish. So you kill the hour. You do not work, you do not read, you do not daydream. If you sleep it is not because you need to sleep. And when at last it is over, there is no evidence, no weapon, no blood, and no body. The only clue might be the shadows beneath your eyes or a terribly thin line near the corner of your mouth indicating something has been suffered, that in the privacy of your life you have lost something and the loss is too empty to share.”

It’s full of things like this. i wish i could write them all down right here, so they could come to you from my hand. So maybe we could intrude on that impenetrable sphere of personal experience a bit. So we could share it somehow.

This book is extremely sad. It is premeditatedly, uniformly, sad. i don’t know how it manages to be so beautiful. it’s a book about nothing and about itself. nothing. a little life trickles into the empty spots and fills it. i was just reading a part, a very melancholy part...

it made me want to believe in things. created such an utter emptiness of belief that a little part of *me* had to expand and melt and drip down into the empty spots, filling and slowly igniting embers and torn ideals.

i do not believe in things. there’s a little black spot that doesn’t believe in love. or God.

after a cigarette break at a Greyhound station, the moment is gone. but... maybe certain spots in the timeline are suspended. maybe certain stars point out the shape of the sky. that’s what i *really* wanted to share. possibly a little bubble of brightness, encapsulated from the encroaching night.

a little spark of immortality that denies the irrevocable nature of yesterday and a shifting, intangible past. maybe a little hope against a future of ending up like my parents, or yours, or a different construct of imagined constellations altogether.

ochre.

blood.

i don’t want to be pubescent, or shiny-eyed sentimental. so i won’t slip in an i love you. except maybe at the end. i definitely won’t continue on in this vein of thought. i just wanted to give you a moment. to make it or find it.

just wanted to step above the timeline for a bit. look down. draw bridges in the water. shapes in the clay.

with love,

Act 2

fed up with the impatience, i retrieve the bottle from its hiding place in full daylight. The little blue pills do not *look* like antibiotics. one smug smile as i pull down the shades and decimate the sunset with my headphones. transform quiet, brittle reserve into wide-toothed predatory spirit.

i’ve been considering striking up a conversation with the man next to me. it might be easier for him now that he’s got me marked as an addict. i feel like making up stories.

several years ago my family and i were on the People Mover (useless useless) being touristy. there was a wild boy next to us, unkempt around the eyes. his nails were black and he carried a skateboard. He struck up a conversation with my dad as if it were the most natural thing in the world, already having judged reaction and not waiting for any of the cues the meek feed on.

first words out of his mouth were that he’d been kicked out of his house, had taken up skateboarding and inhabiting the shadows of clubs. He didn’t need sleep. something about his frankness was... very charming. i want to steal it from him, spouting little platitudes about a broken home in sideways glances, mad tongue in cheek optimism.

i’m going home to my damn family.

Act 3

3 days without sleep. 2 without food. 4 days of too many pills, too little rest. at least, that’s what i’ll tell the stranger i feel the need to talk to. i feel like Kerouac.

my kind of girl

my kind of girlsoul

3 days extending into weeks pouring into past months and heating, rising into a future lifetime of too many pills. it doesn’t matter.

my jaw hurts. i can’t stop trembling. i feel better than i have in god only knows how many fabricated lengths. i will smile at someone today.

i

am in love.

I feel like some kind of borders are breaking down. maybe i am soon to be colorless and shapeless, floating through the air like your eyelashes. They’re beautiful, Lauren. I want to tell all the people I love them, yes, I do love them. I want to be honest, bring a smile then a tear to my face, cheek, hand as it’s swept away.

it may be the lack of sleep, but i feel like something has rejuvenated me along the way. the beatles. Zampano. Lauren’s fingers. reality, the crushing weight seems to have lost its hold. it just doesn’t matter.

i found it one time. prone to prophetic whisperings and visionary aspirations am I. too many shrooms, I pushed my mind all night, running headlong at unimaginable speeds to find the fabric beneath it all, the folded corduroy pleats around and beneath- the written word, conversation.

reality, what is it? I pushed and pushed, all night pushing, and found it at the end. lying motionless on the couch, staring at the fading sparks of power. tears began to stream down my face. not tears of joy, or blissful tears of discovery, but tears of broken, torn loss.

there was nothing.

i had pushed aside the door of perception, opened my eyes, and found a maw of absolute, stark hunger. nothing. i think that’s when i stopped writing anything worthwhile or three-dimensional.

all that was left: mumbling pride constructs. Gods of smoke and crumbling Babel. it just doesn’t matter now. so what if there’s nothing? i’ll make more of it. make a nothing so stark and lonely the heart bursts to fill it. is more full because of it.

nothing. nothing. nothing.

it doesn’t matter.

September 15th, 2001

Lauren,

i feel like a preemptive indian giver, sending you all these things before i have a copy. it’s due to laziness. but for a short period sometime in the distant future, all this writing is yours to keep forever.

love you very much,

it must be the first day of autumn.

spring jumps by, then, tired, it lays down and grows fat and bloated, its tears drying and browning into the blades of summer.

summer blinds the eye, lying viperous in its sheath, poison streaming down its tongue, dripping in two rivulets, washing the trees and sky, until they rust and finally melt away.

and then, the first day of autumn. in the morning, one notes the chill and rejoices at the coming of jacket weather, the prospect of a fashion change to furs, feathers, quilts. the day passes indoors, too silent to stir the windows or eyelashes.

then evening comes. you were going to play a video game. you were going to read a book. you were going to call your girlfriend or write a letter. but none of these things can kill the minutes. you find yourself outside.

the noises of the neighborhood are the same but for a breeze. you might not even notice it at first, might only feel the twinges of some unseen childhood memory stirring underneath the ice. you dismiss it. you smoke a cigarette on the rock outside your home.

and then, for a moment, everything stops. no one is outside. no car doors are slamming. the smoke eases out of your lips silently. the sky is gray and granite and impassive, its eyes too large to pick you out and gobble you up (not immediately), but chuckling. Christ! that godawful laughter.

chuckling all the time because you have forgotten it, and it’s been waiting and waiting, patient as the wind that wears away a cliff face, but too black and cold and uncaring to do anything but give you a slight fondle, a moment’s glimpse, before sending you screaming and gibbering back to the oh-so-temporarily warm little backwater of your dreamland.

and you realize it’s *always* been there. every time you touched her cheek. every time you pulled yourself together. every time you shrugged off your goddamned father cutting his throat and smiled through your mother’s shaking hand. it’s been there, catching the backdraft and falling longer and harder against the background.

a weep and then a scream and then throat clutching silence wells up from your stomach, splashing across your stoppered mouth to spill out in a drop of blood from your nose. and still, you would weep if you only thought you would remember why tomorrow. not even this can touch a chisel to the absolute mountain of dead silence.

what an *empty* wind is blowing through me.

you go inside, you write it down so you can forget, you let the words settle down like debris and ashes. they’re just words. they’ll blow away and rot. just like the pictures and the memories and the dried rose she gave you seven months ago on a Tuesday. just like the memory of the first day of autumn, and of the great abyss.

all that’s falling is you, alone, fluttering apart like paper bats.

so you shut the book. you burn it. every page. you smoke another cigarette. then two. you obliterate its memory by counting to thirty and slowly walking away. winter will come, and snow to hide the sky.

END

October 21st, 2:03am

It’s raining. It’s been raining for days, nonstop. The skies are black all day. All the flowers are dead. Autumn should be beautiful, if cold and mirthless, but the bark is gray and rotting, the leaves have all flown off to a better place. We haven’t eaten in days; it’s hard to get around in the outside world when the water’s so deep and the wind is so cold. There are snakes in the water. Even when I try to brave the whirlpool, they sneak around the toes, crawl up the legs, spin around and around and hiss like white noise, static serpents in the sea of TV sparks. like dying acid. They spin and hiss, confuse ad frighten, until I can’t remember where or who I am, why it’s necessary to go get cigarettes and cheap conversation, till i swim, sobbing and wet, back to the house. If this goes on much longer, I won’t be able to hold my breath enough to find the air pockets or the upstairs. I’m crouching now and scribbling, huddled on my sister’s bed (which is the only thing that keeps its head up) staring out the foggy sliver of glass that shows how gray the world is.

It’s raining in my mind. I think I’ve already drowned and this is the eternal dream. My washed out, pale, and sodden spirit will wander it forever.

\*\*\*

The Bob Dylan concert is soon; I think I’m gonna end up going alone. I would crawl out of a hospital bed and go naked, made-up to look like a black guy in a crowd full of Klukkers, just to see Bob Dylan.

everything’s dead, life springs up from the wastes, then expansive civilizations. The race that inhabits the planet is wise, and builds fleet upon fleet of machines of order to instill life into the blasted waste.

Thousands of planes fly constantly over areas of destruction, sucking up bombs and fire and explosion into a compact metal container, and then into their belly. Later, these metal containers are transported to factories, where tireless citizens work day and night to dismantle these horrible devices so they may never be used again. There are teams of specialists whose sole purpose is to cleverly hide these dangerous chemicals and raw materials in the earth, where none may find them.

Thousands of factories are filtering pollutants from the air. Trained healers with advanced technology, marching around and sucking bullets and wounds out of bodies to suffuse them with life.

How much better would it be that way? You die. You grow old and miserable. You have your mid-life crisis. You finally manage to cram your wife’s ungrateful brats back into her stomach. Years of suffering, the time comes to get unmarried and forget you ever knew her. You grow young and healthy. You drink. It cures nausea. You sink into the insecurity of adolescence. Then the blurry fuzziness of a warm childhood. And the goal at the end of it all is the womb. I could deal with that.

Do you hate doctors as much as I do? That’s because they’re fucking Nazis. they sit in white rooms waiting for their patients to bring them healthy, or at least, sewn up, people. The doctors then proceed to pick out stitches, put in faulty organs, replace bullets, and on and on. A whole slew of nasty little tricks.

Everything would make so much more sense if it went backwards. which is why i think we’re in the wrong phase of universal expansion/contraction.

And you know how civilization sprung up randomly in six or seven different places? that’s because it shrank that way. like water drying up, from a puddle to scattered spots. And the whole race is conspiring to create two perfect specimens. much more sense.

i have to go to sleep, i’m runnin’ on nothin’.

love you,

“quirky”

identity - 1. a condition of being a specified person or thing

For the better part of my life, I’ve had an mutated form of hypochondria. Throughout high school, my best friend, Andy, insisted that I was confident, and he was worthless pond-muck. Soon, this idea slithered into my ear and I started showing symptoms of confidence. It was an innocent thing, at first. I wasn’t convinced, but considered the possibility of the dormant confidence virus lurking beneath a childhood spent picking my nose in the corner. So I got a second opinion. And a third. Every giggling, adolescent chicken of a girl and half-stoned sophomore said the same thing. I was confident.

It didn’t end there. My list of previously unknown virtues grew daily. This plant was on crack, and the bigger it got, the less stable ground an accusation needed to take root in my mind. Second opinions soon turned into vague rumors. Even these were quietly discarded as my bustling topography became capable of supporting itself. I had discovered, simply put, that I was pretty great. Every time Andy said anything about his state of muckiness, I told him to be confident. I could afford such largesse; I was reassured of my place every day.

I was happy in my plastic world, too doped to look at the telltale signs of its falsity. Or, more realistically, I thought I was good enough at my game to keep winning forever. The critical flaw in my logic was thinking that everyone else had been playing the same game as me. They hadn’t. I’d been trying to resurrect Christ with an umbrella and an electric dildo. It had seemed so rational when I thought everyone else shared my vision. Somewhere along the line, I’d been told that I, personally, could create nirvana. I will need years of counseling and hard drug habits to find out who’s fault this is. Everyone else was just going on with their lives, trying to find pants that fit.

Andrew grew up. He stopped cutting himself and rolling in mud. Most frightening of all, he was confident. The kind of confidence you buy fresh at the fruit market, devoid of Formica scent and taste. My father moved out. It spat in the face of all my poetic depth, knowledge of human suffering, compassion or understanding. It even scratched off things I had taken as givens: patience, civility, control.

People conceded. I shook my head in disbelief, a speck of foam dangling from my lip. This was not the way it was supposed to be. It took little time for me to realize that shadows and moths inhabited my world. I left quickly, head down, vegetation shriveling in the distance. The first, piercing lesson of real life was that I am a follower, no matter how many times I’ve been told otherwise.

I am not confident. This came as a quick second. I was still looking in the refrigerator for cats, checking the toilet for my car keys, wondering how the hell I ended up so *nervous*.

My acting career was over, and there were no longer such simple explanations for things as vengeful gods, bastard half-brothers or tragic hubris. The existence of earth-trodden personality blemishes was only slightly less unbalancing than might have been waking up one morning with fewer legs and arms than I went to sleep with. I imagine standing in front of the mirror for long hours, shell-shocked numb and wondering why none of my pants or shirts fit.

I realized, then, that I *was* a one-legged man. I realized that I was a one-armed man, and probable perpetrator of all sorts of zany crimes. “It was the one-armed man what killed Peggy,” or “It was the one-armed man what passed out kibble on Halloween.” I realized I had no alibi for October 31st. I was frantic for new clothing, or a philosophic cloth that would let me run about naked in a barrel.

~

Believe it or not, I’ve started taking measurements. You have no idea how hard it is to find one-limbed clothing stores. The reassessment is... much different than the game. In the morning, it’s too bright; I have trouble glancing at my palm without wincing. Stark relief, telling detail, no phantom limbs to hide behind. But I’d get lonely if I stopped looking.

(I’ve chewed too much bubble gum in my life, swallowed a lot of it, too. Better spit this piece out and try to take up a more productive oral fixation, like smoking or biting nails.)

I make every dotted mark on my bare skin, rolling on the chalkboard when I’m finished. It reads like this:

God is the secretary.

i have square corners

circles of six-sides, into which oblivion pounds faces.

> i am the one who talks too loud, who gets excited and forgets to listen to the other person.

i am the one who spits when he talks.

> i am the one who attempts to explain why Chuck Berry is the anti-christ, and means it.
>
> i am the one who’s afraid to take his car to the mechanic; an oil change raises uncomfortable questions about masculinity.
>
> i am the one who traps fish in the air, flapping them in the cruel question mark of his hand gestures.

i am the one who feels tears welling over misunderstandings.

i am the one who forces shadow-measuring contests.

> i am the one who ***<u>still</u>*** gets nervous when a person refuses to play.
>
> i am the one who sometimes pretends his best friend’s father is his own.

i am the one who drives over baby seats.

> i am the one who gets too high; who barks, wide-eyed, about shooting guns into the Sahara desert while naked.
>
> i am the one who goes to a jazz concert with his grandma the next day, brushing seeds and stems from his smoke stained sweatshirt as he tries to distinguish seizure meds from clarinet.
>
> i am the one who exaggerates(only when there’s room for backpedaling).

i am the one who gets insecure and picks fights.

i am the one who looks at mirrors. and spoons.

i am the one who is short, skittish and temporally obnoxious.

My measurements make me feel like a freak; I put off my trip to the tailor for days. This morning, I paced across the living room, mustering courage. It seems silly, now, as the tailor shakes his head and chuckles, “You’re not the first.” He scribbles out a ritalin script and hands it to me, admonishing me to take it until it’s all gone, even if I start to feel better. After stopping by the pharmacy and heading home, I unfold the instruction manual and scan the short list.

1\) Put on your new bowtie at midnight.

2\) Snort your prescription off the dining room table.

3\) Write an impromptu essay on the word, “quirky”.

After staring at it for a few moments, I shrug and blink.

It fits.

\*

\-

you know, chic, it won’t always be this easy. there will be a time when the personalities we reserve for our families come out, and maybe we’re annoying, maybe we don’t even like each other, if we grate too much. i would compromise myself, i would bend and suffer injustices...

i would persevere when love chemicals run low.

what would you do when it stops being fun? what about poverty? at least three people who should know have told me that love can’t last through poverty.

my mind is full, but not uneasy, just full.

my father stayed home at night

when i stumbled to the shore and watched the

sun beneath the moon

the last time we talked i

gave you everything

but i never gave you anything i

just slowly processed time

i just metered everything to rhyme and said

“it was enough.”

so you left me and i

wondered why and

where and

got desperate and started making up stories,

saying it was pirates or

the nightlife in Denver.

but it was only me.

just the way i tied my shoes and

said i was going to the party store.

now, i’m trying to apologize,

the right way,

trying not to muster tears or bow my head

i’m trying to remember *you*, and

not the way i smile in the mirror.

forgive me?

i even smoked the cigarette that

mama jesus gave me while she reprimanded satan.

it tasted like lemons and burnt my throat.

i took my pills and started coffee,

pulled out all the stops and

sat beneath the table.

waiting for the treasure.

praying for internal rhythm,

but not the way one prays to God.

not the way I do, at least.

just fingers crossed, in the spirit you appreciate,

nervous, superstitious like you,

not thinking about the logic.

or repeat words.

listening to Danzig.

not writing to Lauren.

i’ll take this table when it breaks and dies,

pretend to be an ornament

so it would be unnatural if i didn’t shriek

and cough when i parked and it was

by the roadside.

i’ll just bring a blanket and picnic there,

buy the land when i’m 70 and

build a summer cottage.

REMEMBER me!

i’m like a lover,

you can’t just turn your back because i

didn’t capitalize I.

try and have a little confidence, i’ll stop

overcompensating, giving speeches in

the rain.

but pacing? in the moonlight? smoking

cigarettes and churning?

dream journal

12-06-01

The telling of this will take some time. -some sort of monastery, nuns to be hidden from, a man who was to be shot and a bell. he was tied down, i painted him somehow, while the nuns were gone, covering him in sticky gray goo. this was a prank for the benefit of someone. the hired gun, or, perhaps, government man who was to shoot him came in in the middle of my deed. he said something to the effect of, “do you know how much trouble it causes me to shoot a man in public?” and i had just quadrupled his load, because he would now have to shoot myself and my two friends. transition.

came to my friend, outside of his (or my?) white car. i told him what had happened just as the man who was to shoot us rode up on horseback. there was someone else there, an old friend of mine, a girl. the man got in the car. we all did. the general feeling was one of going on a long and adventurous road trip, not to our deaths.

time shift. unsurety.

a\) i was told to do something, i took the car door off (my father’s? a priest’s?) the car and brought it over to our car. the man said we could use it if our door got scratched up. i said that our door would certainly get scratched up before this was over, and the replacement door, too. i thought i owed the door’s owner a nice, unharmed door, at the very least,. it was obviously someone i respected. i put the door back.

b\) the man was having me do some sort of errand for him. i believe i was painting sheets of plywood blue, just along one of their thin edges. somewhere along the way, my task switched to carving a stick. my stick was ramshackle and rundown and frightening all at once.

i was standing at the edge of a forest while i was doing this. every once in awhile, i would complete part of the stick and toss a piece into the forest. each time i did so, the noise emitting from the forest would change. it was distant, background noise, but ominous. i remember only that it started out as something like animal noise, but by the time i had finished the stick it was a voice, calling, singsong, to have the hearer brought into the forest. “i want to break your bones, i want you to come in and never come out,” etc.. i was not, however, afraid. it seemed perfectly natural in the dream.

shortly thereafter, i needed to go into the forest. i had dropped some small object over the lip of the hill. the forest was in a large, steep valley, with a great lake in the center. i set off down the incline, but it soon grew too steep. i fell, grabbing at the grass in an attempt to slow my fall, but hit the ground and died. that was of no consequence. it seems i had become immortal, regenerating at the bottom of the hill.

i called up something to the man (who i was doing chores for), then looked around the valley. on one side, a bear. on the other, sean and another member of the Magic nerds.

he was going to lead me out of the forest. he seemed to think that i was gonna be a funny guy, and did an impression of how i would react to his proffered help. “gee, i *could* have Sean lead me out of the forest, but i think, instead, i’ll go see Mr. Bear. i think *he* knows the way out of the forest.” saying this, he and the other nerd promptly found bears, who ate them. this was the funniest thing i had ever seen, and my laughter woke me, asking Andrew if he couldn’t see the funny events of my dream on a computer screen. then i wrote this.

end

Lauren,

Andy ran his dad’s car over sixty ft. of curb tonight. wasn’t paying attention, found himself heading straight for the concrete barrier where Lapeer splits into Opdyke, swerved and slid over the curb. it’s really bothering me, the whole Andy thing. he’s a horrible fucking driver, but he gets ultra defensive when i say anything about driving, like do this or don’t do that. makes me feel like i’m walking on glass, on top of being moderately freaked out when he drives on the highway anyways. if he weren’t Andy, i would tell him to piss off and find his own damn ride to school. but he is Andy.

i realize that rock and roll has taken the place of the mother. it offers compassion, when needed. it offers warm, fuzzy love. it offers the blue ache of nostalgia. something to cry to. it feeds the emotions when we’re hungry. Everything a mother should do, and it’s there all the time.

it’s true. all of it.

chica, i miss you. have you ever considered what it is to miss someone? it almost seems like, to me, that it’s... not an emotion easily felt unless the missed object hears. i’ve never really felt that kind of loss or ache acutely unless it was being sent to someone. i don’t know if this makes any sense. you don’t feel it because you need to feel loss or loneliness. you feel it so the other person can know you miss them.

that seems almost coherent. barring my ultra atrocious handwriting, worse tonight that normal.

lots of love,

see you soon,

December 13th, 2001

My Dearest,

i’m out of notebook paper, so i’m writing this on the back of old history notes. my history notebook was full a long time ago, i’ve made my way up the back half of it. my history final is this coming Thursday, one question requires wading through 100 years of Roman history, or about 1/2 a notebook. holy Yazu.

Lauren, i’m driven by a subtle arrogance and a desire to... be or have something worthwhile and meaningful in life. to do something. i have no idea where it came from, nor any idea how to attain it. which way to go? to be harsh and unyielding, to walk with unbent back beneath the sun, while it burns away anything base, or to travel quiet trails, quiet workings, while the moon watches. not making a decision will eat away at all the things i value about myself, leave me bitter and unsure. but i don’t feel bold enough to make a decision.

there’s a special place for words on paper, how they can be more graceful and evocative than anything spoken. there’s also a place in the mind that envisions what words on paper can be, and a giant gap between the possibility and the reality. any delay between conception and action is shattering. it destroys, not only what the words could have been, but some of the truth behind the original thought..

~

Unfortunately, the record stops there. Lauren returned these letters in the mail after ending the relationship (as an act of benediction and a favor, not out of spite). I began typing them in 2002 shortly after I got clean; I was trying to sort through the last few years. I got very quickly to the point you see now, but could go no further. The project began to drag. I was not yet ready to look myself in the face. Especially as the record neared those crucial moments when my world finally shattered fully, it was unbearable to be face to face with my own selfishness and lunacy, my own mad cycle of death and sin. There was too much sadness still.

Much later, the project still untouched (although plans continued to soar), I threw out the letters, the box, the drawings—the whole shot. Probably 1/3 of the letters remained to be typed, and there were a number of drawings, photographs, pictures, and postcards that I had before planned to include as part of this notebook. The letters that did not get typed were those that covered the most crucial—the saddest and most eventful—months. I know why I did it, but I will not say. Only that at the time it was important: my life was moving on.

So there is an indelible blackout at the most crucial point of the narrative, at the event-nexus of my life. I will say this, only briefly: life continued much as it had. I spiraled deeper. I visited New Orleans. There was a shattering falling-out. We continued to write and pretend although everything had been broken. I sunk deeper in my depression and madness. I began getting into car accidents and having near-miss encounters with the law. One in particular near the end of winter I think had an especial effect on Lauren: I passed out at the wheel, Andy sleeping beside me, and ran into a fire hydrant. It was not long before Lauren called to say that she thought we should quit. Our relationship was already little more then an empty outline, but I was devastated nonetheless. It was the emblem of my aloneness.

Now I felt I had nothing left. I continued to write some letters, but they were both elliptical and filled with resentment and anger. These too fell off. The drugs got much worse. I began experimenting with the needle. This all happened very quickly. By September of 2002 (less than a year from where these letters break off) my cycle had intensified to a frantic peak and then finally ended in a visit to rehab. I only needed one. This is where the record picks up again, but in the form of poems and scribblings, and in particular with one long poetic project which began in the Winter semester. Over the course of two years and infinite revisions and mutations, I quit working on it. It is as follows, perhaps I will finish it one day. To the best of my estimation, it is the most direct descendant of the self-narrative that begins in the above letters, although in more explicitly creative form.

Since the letters to L diminished and trailed off somewhere between the months of April and September (although even then there was an occasional email), I suppose there would have been a fundamental void even if I had not thrown out the box of letters, especially at those crucial moments, maybe the month or two of vital (mortifying) activity. I was not writing much. I was numbed and stunned out of expression. So the void remains. I will sort through my papers, and fill in the period between the end of these letters (December 2001) and rehab (September 2002) as best as I can, followed by the first and following drafts of the Rebekah project, miscellany, and letters to C

.

**M**

**9/17/05**

[image: Macintosh HD:Users:ctrueme1:Desktop:AtLwM:atlwm scans:images 26.jpeg]

Louisiana. Lauren's kitchen. Silver ashtray on the stove where her mother and I perpetually stub out butts. With the fan on low, smoke washes out in beautiful waves. Hundreds of tiny, deadly waterfalls. 2am. First one up this morning, last one awake tonight. Smoking in the kitchen and blowing rings into the abyss.

Always the last one up--I've put it down to genes. Uncle Bob was some hotshot--one of Nixon's physicians. Mom says he never took more than four hours of sleep in his adult life.

Of course, he also swallowed a bottle of valium on the anniversary of his divorce, then blew his brains out.

So here I am. Smoking. Waiting for the dogs to bark or Lauren's lamp to click on. I bend down, face low and close to the counter, trying to get all the smoke into the suction of the fan. I count three butts in the ashtray. Paula must dump the ashtray every couple of hours--I see her smoking all the time, but there are never more than a few butts.

All the ashes and dirt and filters are squished on the left side of the tray, the side nearest the fan. They look like metal flakes. Magnetized.

I stub my butt out on the right side of the tray. Stand up.

I fill the empty spots until sleep.

12/26/01 -- somewhere between Louisville and Montgomery

Scribbled down while a stranger reads. He offered me his terrible teenage poetry with no shame.

too many things from the past have been paraded in front of me in the last two days. too many things i'd thought had faded. but i still know my poems by heart. there are still finger-runnels on the edges of my book. my reading level is up. my compassion level is down.

i feel like the only thing i've actually lost is progress. i gave up "immutable forward motion."

Socrates spoke of death as simply an unknown. Showing cowardice or immorality to escape it is one of the greatest causes of human evil--they do a certain evil to escape a possible good.

that's how i've lived--clinging to the familiarity of a stagnant mediocrity that i know--choosing the certain purgatory over stepping out into unknown air.

So. what to do? push off, i guess, take my chances in unknown waters. i think i started pandering to people's opinions too much. let their critiques warp my great big brain, bend it in every direction at once--arriving at mushy writing.

who could have guessed?

a solemn vow--or as close to solemn as i can get with this great big, cluttered, catastrophic computer for a brain. i will stop and record the words when they come. i will pull over to write, i will drive home so i can have the necessary quiet, i will pull out my book in the most embarrassing of situations and scribble in it.

i want the Quiet now. the calm that comes in a bus full of strangers (or anyone, i guess). early dawn or late night when the lights are out, when birds peek our from our brain and make nests there--and for a little bit, we feel like majestic, noble, silent creatures.

beautiful. i can still write in the dark. darkness brings the communion of hand and page, like the deepest, coolest pools of shadow hanging from your eyelashes. darkness lying in wait to devour the heavy-footed, the incautious.

but no danger to me--my peace.

the greyhound gets closer to home. anxiety builds--all the petty arguments rush back in, the complacency, the failures. i wonder... if i'll hang on to the seeming peace of mind, the sense of destination i found in Louisiana. Mostly, i miss Lauren, and am afraid to send her the letter i wrote because it's too uncovered, too naked. i want a fix to the issue, but i don't have one. nothing in the letter addressing the difficulty of finding a fix.

not the flickering thousands within it

in all things, in writing most of all: honesty. build the walls that funnel the voices, the echo chamber to shoot the bullet of song up and shatter the spheres of heaven. have courage--and above all stubborn persistence. pray to the god your heart knows, not the one they feed you.

the hardest part: never, ever reread. the words become idols, little statues of truth that destroy the living Word. emblems, mementos, debris--this is not the life of words. setting them down on paper is only the outward act--the more vital act is their inscription on the soul, carving and carving and crafting a living word there, a spring of water that won't dry up. carve the poem in body and mind--violently, if necessary. this above all things. don't be deceived by the lie of *artifacts.* poems just the crumbling cities and petrified curiosities--the Logos once walked here, the Poem has passed this way.

1\. Her fingers walk the keys with precision. She pauses to tune her voice to F, then settles her glasses lower on the nose and begins the piece again.

2\. His foot taps as he rings the bell a third time, then checks the address on the pizza box. He glances at his watch and jogs back to the car.

# ix. Amnesia

# ix. Amnesia 

**march 2002—sept. 2002**

[image]

\[longhair / stoned looking photo\]

Light. Blackness. Yellow blur. Blackness. My eyes peel open again. I can almost make out my hand. The rest slowly resolves. I’m sitting at a half-sanded and ancient table, papers scattered across its back like scales, head slowly jostling back and forth on an unsteady spine. A blanket’s draped around my sunken shoulders. Hapless, naked hairy tree-trunks are rooted in the floor that quivers in a forty-degree morning far beneath me. A memory flails, then gently falls apart in broken pixels. My eyelids are soft and cold and wet when they settle across skin; I let them linger on the bottom for a long, long blink. Something fights weakly in the darkness there, twitches vaguely and shudders until it’s still.

Tense. Seize. Ugly orange vision bursts into life. The summer. Cotton dresses. A bottle. Sweat drying on her forehead. Revolving doors. I try to hold my head together, but my hands are tatters. Tears seep out between the scattered gashes in their shielding. The memory slips back into the deep, dark blissful shadows that kill in one breath. Northern ice. I cringe from the smell of whiskey and realize I’m taking a drink. Jesus Christ. It starts to rain. Perceptions sting my ears, my skin. There are sleeping bodies on the floor. I can hear two people fucking through razor-thin walls. Just where the fuck am I? I sit still. Inhale. Exhale. The sound of air being pulled into lung holds its own sort of rawness. I think I’m falling. A desperate trance closes over red eyes. Glazed and dreaming. I wonder faintly, before I go, just who the fuck I am.

They ignored it for as long as they could, but the night was heavy, sweating. Each time they thought they’d left it behind it snickered from the startled shadows of their plastered smiles. It perched on branches, draping low to scrape against their dreams.

It waited in corners of ceilings, in heavy spots behind their back, in the distance between their laughter. It crushed air tight to lungs and smothered bodies in torn sheets.

They’d fallen into a circle by 4:00 in the morning. Three of them, jittering and lifeless, noses cracked by powdered iron that shifted in their heads to the tugging of a great magnet, bits of it trailing behind as clumps converged, bringing Rob to Jesse, Zack to Rob, Jesse to them both, until they stuttered into gasping orbit around a talk of what was. The night was too lonely to let them talk about anything else. Zack sat to the side, radiating skepticism. Jesse defended while facing Rob.

Jesse always defended against skepticism. It was simple; Jesse had faith. Jesse had *always* had faith. When his world was younger, Jesse was bursting to touch people, ecstatically jubilant to feel out the edges of their humanity or dip fingers into night whispers of conversation. He’d lie on the floor after a birthday party and turn, over and over in eager hands, the awed hush of bright-eyed, pigtailed, or freckled angels peeking out from newborn voices awkwardly croaking through the shadows around him. His rush was headlong bare-feet on a path as empty and clear as glass lips, wet, sparkling, October’s finger screaming across the crystal, howling at and battering shut the eyes of summer’s senseless, silly slumber. There were things in the world that were there to be had, things that hummed like fire and called to all men and were waiting, feckless, wild, true, and untamed, to be taken by unshaking hands. Jesse knew there were real things because he read them in books.

Zachariah, however, was a bullfrog. He was always skeptical. Zack had *always* been skeptical. Zack had skinny lips that recoiled from his Cheshire teeth, trembling in the trees, invisible and as far away as they could stretch, clinging to the branches of a circumstantial smile. He gestured his hands in torturously slow arcs, which traced gelatinous eddies in the air. He rarely talked, and when he did he aimed at closure. He normally struck. He’d been doing nothing but watching, that night, eyes bulging from foxholes in his skull, following the darting rhythm of conversation with unblinking eyes that belonged above sharp teeth. There was caution there, too, crisp bits of terror that spoke of enemies inside his den, a backward glance between sinew and bone to peer at the resonating darkness inside. Neither Advil, aspirin, or cat tranquilizer had been able to still his head since dinner.

Rob made a comment. Jesse’s shoulders swung forward in a screaming lean that threatened to send him tumbling into his hands. He braced himself on the edge of the table, which sent shivers up his aggravated voice. “Yeah, yeah, I know what you’re sayin’,” he nodded his head enthusiastically, then paused. “But uh… I dunno though. I don’t think it actually lets you *get* anywhere, you know? Just uh…” his hand fluttered in the air beside him, darting and hovering around a question mark. “Just uh, it let’s you do some crazy shit with your head. Like uh… it really does let you get places, just not the right way,” he cocked his head to the side and offered a quizzical nod. “Here. It lets you bend your head around to places you can’t get to naturally without a lot of practice. Prayer maybe, you know? Monks and shit.”

Rob scrunched his nose up to meet the edges of skin drooping to its bridge. “I always do soul-searching on drugs. You can get to that place. Where everything’s, like, perfect,” he drew the last syllable out. “It’s very Zen.”

Jesse recoiled from these words, arching his eyebrow and forming a small ‘o’ of protest. “That’s not-… I mean, that’s not what I was saying. I was trying to…” he leaned back on his heels and ran a hand across his eyes. “OK.” He drew a breath, then pressed in towards his audience. He exhaled slowly, then spoke, “not Zen. You get there and it’s not right, you know? Yeah, you can get to crazy places, but you don’t belong there. Maybe you can balance crazy-like, get a crystal of what’s what. But your head doesn’t match up, you know?” A note of zeal crept into his voice. His eyes turned starwards. “You’re in a place that people work their whole lives to get to. You’re dirty, small. Patch-worked and shit. I think it might actually hurt you in the long-run.”

Silence was in the room for a drawn out breath. It pressed down, making Rob turn his head. Jesse spoke in slippered tones. He whispered across the carpet, stopping to kneel and lie a secret at the doorstep of his friends. He hummed, “I got there once,” flattened his palms. “Shroom night, ‘member? Was goin’ through this whole brain-flexing kick. I dunno how to say it. Like, pushing, you know? All night I pushed and pushed at the edges. I think I even preyed and shit. I was set on getting through, getting… the place. You know.” Rob nodded. Zack hesitated, then dropped his chin in a yes. “I was lyin’ on the couch. Tryin’ to find out what was underneath.” Jesse stopped for a moment, started again, “my brain. Reality and shit, not the couch.” Jesse frowned. “I got there. A wrestling special was on. We weren’t watching it or anything, it was just on. Surreal. I was layin’ there, watchin’ the tracers but not really seein’ cuz of pushing. And I got there. Tears were just streamin’ down my face,” he ran his hand down his face, moving his fingers in a mock patter of rain. “It was empty and shit, man. Just… empty. No music underneath, you know? Just dead silence. And cold. That’s what it was man. That’s *all* it was, what was real. Still makes me feel empty.” Jesse shook himself and rubbed his arms. “They’re just drugs man. No Zen.” Rob was silent.

Zack had been stone, and now he tapped a finger to crack the shell. The stillness crumbled away. He spoke from a dead place, “I used to do acid. I used to do acid all the time. I used to soul-search, too.” He met Jesse’s eyes. “I found a lot of horrible shit there. Nothing but pain.” Frost plumes curled around his nostrils. He shrugged and gave a revolting grin, “So I stopped looking.” His grin attached to Jesse’s startled sympathy or pain. It grew toothier and black. “What?” he sneered. “You’ve never been in the midst of it and fallen in love? Never been perfect there? … never thought the rest was just soul-shredding agony?” His smile slipped. “That’s the peak. After that you’re broken, so you wait to do acid again. I used to have my calendar marked. Every three days.” The concrete slowly reformed and took its seat.

The talk trailed off after that. They fell out of the circle before the sun rose, elastic restlessness unraveled, end of magic marked by the receding night. Soon, one snore sawed through Venetian blinds, rattling them and tossing about glimpses of the outside. One slept silently, impassive, not dreaming. One lay awake, face pale and unblinking, dappled gray with shadows. Tears streamed down his face. “There’s more,” he whispered. Rest was lost waiting for the words ‘the end’ to scroll across the horizon with a recurring promise of normality, of substance. Jesse waited for an eternity in the ghostly, lifeless prison of pre-dawn light.

“old junkie”

Spiders crawl the length of his lazy veins and swarm like vision without breath, black dots back-dropping yellowed flesh. His height would be impressive if it wasn’t drawn in on itself, hunched and waiting to protect from unseen blows, guarding precious breath. His skin is shadowed, vacant, clinging to his face without ardor and falling down his body, parting and stretching around ribs before it settles in a stagnant pool around his feet. It’s grey beneath the glassy eyes of a doll, which swivel pointlessly from left to right and see little. A beak of a nose perches on petulant mouth, takes its shade from towering cheekbones. He distantly sucks on cheeks when his face is still, or puffs them out like pebbled grapefruit. They are hollows that eat the light when he talks, slowly, deliberately, words dripping from his lips like an untimed faucet. His speech is edgeless as it breeches the ear, soft and uncommanding like all the old, old junkies.

He takes his time because he knows there’s nowhere to go. Never has been. The track marks follow suit, marching ponderously up each arm, tracing the path of old scars that nestle in elbows, above wrists, along bicep that seems to be attached to the bone by nothing but heroin, marking guideposts over those covered by age spots or simply faded, like burning pinpricks in the night sky after the star’s imploded and the light’s traveled so far, twenty, thirty, forty years across vacuum to reach our eyes. They sleep in wasting stomach, brittle legs, everywhere on a body that shakes in the wind; they are nails in rotting timber.

His teeth are white-edged and defiant of his living death, the only bright spots in the world. They peak from his mouth, sometimes, when he talks about the past, thing’s he’s done or women he’s had. He talks a lot about places, old, old places. Ancient places that he reads about in his old, old books, all of it as ghostly and strange as him when he rocks back and forth slightly to whisper it. It’s hard to believe he’s ever done anything but shamble to the corner bar, or sit in his chair, collecting years while he quietly shoots up.

Dare I say I met her? It was more that her presence unfurled, or that the veil that hung before her image in the mind was violently ripped aside to reveal her - impossible, unreachable, - *there*. An image - coming in the back door of the house behind Andy, glancing into the large kitchen with the long table underneath the window, stacked with sliced ham, chicken wings, carrot sticks, pasta salads. Two adults with beers chatting at the far end of the room at the threshold hallway between the kids' bedrooms and the living room. The view of the large backyard scattered with people and kids playing tag, two men in the act of throwing a football, but silenced by the glass. Down the stairs lined with shoes, emerging into the basement with iron supports and the washing machine and drier at the foot of the stairs, walking into the living room, behind Andy still, slightly nervous but holding my own beneath my new costume (All through middle school I'd worn khakis and dully striped shirts which I hated; I was just dipping my feet in the pool of black, metal, and boots, the style that segues into piercings and body art as soon as humanly possible. But I was just starting, and found a whole new self there, along with the drugs, and the grin, and the penchant for impersonating Hunter S. Thompson and british folk and oddly amalgamated creations of my own; so I was wearing black and Airwalks and maybe some black fingernail polish and a spiked bracelet, or something, beneath which facade I thought, for a time, my nervousness was invisible or absent).

An image: Emily like a performer in front on her friends, four or five of them. They all watched her - she was it, it was true, she was telling a terrible joke with that attitude that makes you sure it doesn’t matter what joke she tells, in fact it’s better if the joke is terrible - it’s my jovial angel dearthing, my down-deep from the death of laughter that sings this song to you, and you’ll like it and me so watch out -

she, the only one in black - all the rest of the earth in earth tones and pink - with this ripped black skirt with patches of purple fabric. I knew right then it was her costume too, along with that laugh that chimed out from her solar plexus in a redemptive rain of sound like a rush of wind-blown bells. She was right on, dark down out of a dream of mine I had recently had (or maybe one I hadn't yet had). Yet all in all, there was nothing terrifyingly special about her. I mean, she was not homely, but not - you know - a supermodel, there was just this olive-toned glow in her cheeks, a particular sparkle, a way she had of looking off into the distance, this gurgle down in her voice. (I taped a picture of her in my poem book where it stuck for years - this is really what I'm describing - her picture in my book, which is a far more familiar sight to me than her flesh and bone face, which, for all I'm concerned, is the one that's origami - that picture, and flashes of laughter or solar flares of moments that burst into life - flint striking powder in the iron-aching chamber of memory.)

and she turns from her friends and her face is like this shining, radiant bell that sounds clearly and calmly through the room and freezes everything in its instant to alight, a translucent clarity that pierces the room and all of Time itself, or whatever. Everything gels and slowly resumes, flowing infinitesimally back into motion until it snaps and she’s speaking -

(she deflates, spent. disappointed with her protagonist). Man. Nobble is like, confused and, disappointed, he’s so confused he - you know - practiced, hard he - you know - put his heart into it. Glum, man. Just plain glum. But Hobble is the man of the hour, and Nobble is, in a way, happy for him, and so he goes to congratulate him and he says to himself, “You know, I’ll just try harder next year. For the gun to go off (we’re all eating this up). And they’re in the stalls super tense and they - BANG! the gun goes off and they - BAM! - out the stalls like an incredible shot of, you know, *lightning*, or whatever, and they’re running, running, goin’ super-fast they’re running, pulling out in the lead and then they’re - neck and neck, so it’s - Hobble-Nobble, Hobble-Nobble, Hobble-Nobble - and just - at the last second Hobble - pulls ahead. (all the breath gushes out of her). And that’s that. Nobble’s, you know, getting old, he knows, and so he thinks that - man - that was his best chance and he’s given it, all he’s got, man, and he’s - gosh - he’s staring into this great gaping abyss he’s like - ultra-depressed he’s like - this is the end. (she pauses). The end the end the end the end (an ominous echo). And he looks over at Hobble - in his moment of glory, with the flowers and the, you know, the prize, and he knows he’ll never (she sniffles, she riding this intensely ridiculous but real wave of emotion) be quite the - (gulp) the horse that - Hobble (her voice chokes up around her words) - and so he goes to the stables. And he sits down, and he doesn’t know what to do - he thinks “There’s only one way - out of - this” and he gets his pen, and composes a long and heartfelt sort of letter where he says to his brother - “Dear Hobble, you were the best sort of brother that a horse could hope to have. I love you very much, I never want you to think that this is your fault. I am weak. I just can’t go on.” And he signs it “May the Best Horse Win, / Your Brother, / Nobble.” And he leaves it in his dressing room and gets this rope, which he ties in a noose and ties it to the rafter, and he gets up on a stool, and puts the noose around his neck, - but just then this dog comes in, a friend of Nobble’s who hangs around the stables, and he looks at Nobble and says “Nobble, man, what are you doing?” and Nobble looks at him with utter shame in his eyes and, gathering his words, he says, (and she says this part swiftly, with the most precise and deftly executed anti-climacticism) “Holy crap a talking dog!”

the strange bursting of their voices over the sand of our ears and we sat there smiling defensively and they asked us some questions - "what you doing in there, lone rangers" (mustachioed bastard) - and he, certainly, joking, knowing now that he had no idea who we were or cared, that he probably supposed we were up to whatever and just trying to make small talk - and everything's happening so quickly

and me "making butter."

and there's this sense, on that drug, that there's this rhythm to everything, some plan that has been jotted down on a napkin somewhere in the cosmos for this very moment - notes that had been written long ago and now the fingers - the stiffened fingers draw the bow of the cello - that is to say, that there is some script we were assigned and that that - is the thing that we must find and come - into attunement with and then - when that final chord is struck and it vibrates out - into the room in an action - whether it makes sense or not some - indelible gong in the aether will babble - bang - bark - blare - blow - boom - burst - buzz - crackle - chatter - clack - clang - clank - clap - clatter - clink - crash - creak - detonate - echo - emit - explode - hum - jabber - jangle - jar - moan - murmur - patter - play - rattle - reflect - resonate - resound - reverberate - ring - roar - rumble - shout - shriek - shrill - sing - slam - smash - snort - squawk - thud - thump - thunder - toot - trumpet - vibrate - whine - whisper - into place in the jigsaw puzzle of the ear. and so you do odd things on hypnotics because you think they're preordained and predestined.

which is probably why emily begins to sway back and forth on the table, rocking her self gently and singing "we're rockin' the boat" and the laughter in the room builds, and andy insists on the coffee-machine and i say it was the one-armed man -

and that's when Terry (andy's aunt, emily's mom) wanders in and sees the group of people and, i thought, some part of her seeing what's going on with us but not - in her state - being able to deal with it starts drunkenly burbling about politics and blaming the Republicans (that way that drunks have of putting what they really feel out there in a manner that instantly dismisses itself as absurdity and inconsequence) for everything - me not seeing that she was too drunk to really see that Emily was sitting on the table and rocking back and forth, back and forth, singing sing-songedly in a sing-song "rockin' the boat, rockin' the boat - don't fall off the boat, we're rocking the boat" - and that innocent flash in her eyes (her not knowing at all what she looks like (infinitely innocent and astounding and rife with hilarity and gut-wrenching piano strings) "oh *hi* mom" in an elongated song and she repeats "oh *hi* mom how are you?" and terry the same "oh *hi* emily - oh *hi* emily how are you?"

"oh *hi* andrew. oh *hi* andrew how are you?" and this room seems to be the place for those who like to watch people do their thing, because drunken Terry is having the same effect on the room that the group of us did, gathering attention, going on in her drunken drawl, building laughter. andy tugs emily on the shoulder and says "emily, we should go outside now." and emily looks at him and then at her mom and smiles and says alright, and we start toward the stairs (even though there's a door that leads outside less than 15 feet away) and we make our labyrinthine odyssey up the shoe-stuffed stairway and emerge in the kitchen, passing by the door to the outside, all of us stumbling past the table and stopping at the mouth to the family room. we're trying to figure something out, some problem that has us perplexed and andy is animatedly slaloming in the cosmic logic of hypnotics, trying to bring his light to the situation and we're standing by the potted plant on the small book case.

i say to emily "was that alright?"

-what?

-that.

-the?

-with your mom.

-what about it.

-(andy) you were sitting on the table.

-so?

-and singing "rockin' the boat, we're rockin' the boat." (pause) you looked really high.

and the plant tips, one of us has knocked it over but waves of nescience still buffet us, they're rockin' the boat and none of us can tell who knocked it over, so we all are staring at this plant, on its side, dirt spilling out in an arc of black plant-blood.

we stare at it. Not knowing what to do, we stare at it. There's been some terrible rip in the fabric of destiny. Confusion wells up like blood from a paper-thin cut. I look at Emily who looks at Andy. Andy stares at the plant which looks at all of us. Emily looks at me and I look at Andy. Andy looks at Emily and she shrugs. I shrug.

I say "What do we do?"

He says "We've gotta fix it."

"How?" she says.

"How." I say. It hangs in the air.

How how how how how how.

"Did you hear that?"

"What?"

"He said how."

"Who?"

"How."

there, in the family room. someone from the party is all alone on the chair with the footrest out. He's been so still we didn't see him, but we see that he's there, vaguely conscious, looking miserable. His great gurgles have become the how that we heard. He's very overweight - not the happy-go-lucky kind like our friend Biggy Smalls in the basement, with the two girls on his arms - but here he is, absolutely trashed, half a pint of vodka in his hands, red-eyed, wearing his abjection on his sleeves like an emblem. Here he is, trying to do, which is what happens when the party wears off, and you're all alone. Which I wasn't yet, and we weren't, yet - we were just getting started. And there was this guy in the chair who we hadn't seen, but who had been drunkenly watching us for a while, drinking his drink, lips lined with hate and dripping revulsion from every pimply, middle-aged pore.

These people are littered everywhere, like calm blue reminders of Death. One or two who are near the Truth Within Lies and so cannot help but radiate the Ugliness of their living deaths, in their skin, in their bodies, in their terrible eyes - a reminder that we're all just biding time (those of us in Lies) - that look that has been abandoned, that's clawed down through the dirt of the swamp to find the mushy crap at the bottom of the pond which is their deplorable Self. All of our miserable Selves, there in that chair - burping, obviously wanting to puke, zit-lined, alone -

alone.

and here he appears in the midst of that sound that rips across the cloth of reality, that missed note that seems to tells us "something is wrong with Destiny" (but really is just the drugs beginning to fade). An omen, apparently. Some sordid road marker, some impenetrable augur from God. We all looked at each other. We knew.

"He's *alive"* Andy says.

"He couldn't be" Emily echoes.

"It's an otter" I suggest.

he’s very drunk and very belligerent, and we get out of there quickly when he starts to try to wobble up. emily and i went to her room, just to sit there while she showed me some of her things, and this is how we ditched Andy - it had been just some small image. after that we headed out the garage, and nate's in the driveway with a beer and he says to me "some guy has got acid, man" and his speech is slurring and dissolving in a puddle, which i should have gone for in a minute but there was emily on my arm and we were both sort of alone now in the Cimmerian shade of late-at-night and so i just smiled, all the hilarity gone from earlier, no more disco gnomes just quiet and timorous and shy with emily there on my arm and my heart thumping away inside my lungs and something that tastes a little like vomit, an admixture of the powder draining down my sinuses (which is wearing off) and the intense emotional high of emily, in the back of my mouth. so i light a cigarette and say something like "that's great" but there's some tension now, which is hard for nathan to bear on the acid and so he wanders off shortly, and i'm left with emily in the driveway and we both want to get out of here, away from prying eyes.

Now Emily and I were attached at the hip. It was late and cold and blue, and a moist air draped its body over our shoulders, over our naked faces, over our palely clasped hands that tangled their pathetic fingers together. Everything now is veiled by a hyperborean mist like my nervous core that trembles in the darkness. Her face is softened, too, drained of its mask, looking up with soft little glowing eyes from the cup of my arms where she huddles, and I huddle above her, as much a refugee as a refuge. There can be no words between us, now. We're in the open space between the forest and the house; we have no idea where to go, what to do; we are so confused and lost in the darkness and we are just sort of standing there, words disappearing, faltering, freezing into our cold blue fingers which inseparably connect us; and the lights, except for the incessant porch light, were out in the house; and the noises, which were eternal in their clamor what seemed like moments ago, from the woods, noises of voices and acoustic guitars and shouts and songs, had quieted from their roar to a simmer, a soft simmer that promised to keep silent watch until morning.

We were both very sad, now, because softnesses are born in sadness, our home on the horizon, and because the viscera of our touch proclaimed its impermanence, in fact its wretchedness in the night. Soft words strained out, trying not to touch the brittle glass that encased us.

I say Us and We, but there was really just me. Remembering this is remembering the most Loneliness of experience that could be - that most horrible aloneness which persists when bodies are near one another - oh, that terrible Absence. That’s how it was as we touched each other and I stroked her cheek and - and, in truth, I have no clue what she felt, what she was thinking, only that I was completely alone, and so I assumed she must have been too. That’s how it was as we went across the back lawn and, dark now, pushed aside the branches to the tree fort and (those terrible branches like skeletal arms clawing) walked up the path to the birch-white fort in its somber clearing and clambered up there, into the fort where there were sleeping bodies, and onto the roof where two or three of them sat and we, or I, so awkward and nervous, wondering what they thought of our union, Doug’s friends, one or two of them with a bong which we hit and Emily hit and the hits rasped into our lungs and the stars were enormous above us and the sky was entirely black, black black black black black black black with these intensely bright pins that pierced it, pins that showed pinhole glimpses into some World besides this one, and silence reigned and soon the two friends left and Emily, who had been silent, and I were alone and we went down into the tree fort and we lay down to go to sleep but I kissed her and she kissed me back but it was so cold and we touched each other, then, or, rather, I touched her, and I was so nervous, I thought, I’m not doing this right, but I couldn’t say that against the wall of silence and so there we sat for what must have been an hour and Emily finally said “you can stop” and she said “you want to go inside?” which i did and we wandered there together and everything had been shattered, was already shattered always before this was just the bitter everything the loss of words and we went into Doug’s room and lay down on his bed and I just held her, knowing that it wasn’t enough and that there would never, ever be any substitute, any breech across that impossible wall and we lay there with me yearning and open and barren inside with her next to me and just huddling there, hoping it would never end and that time would stop and we would be forgotten there, left behind in some cinematic sphere where there was just this stasis that never, ever had to face the light of morning but then i drift -

and, in the morning, with the light streaming through - (how familiar, this sight, this lamentable, piercing refrain - the light of the morning streaming in to display the foolishness, the unlastingness of the night - i woke up slowly, with those worms clawing around in my chest and Emily gone, which is the only way she could have been, and it was over before it started which it never had, and there i was i climbed out of bed to find andy and smoke, and he had slept upstairs and he seemed sort of happy about emily and me but I was cold, and he said that last night some people had mistaken me for him and so they thought that andy was making out with his cousin - but here we were, back to the same old dynamics and i was looking for emily who was, i thought, avoiding me, and all of this I locked up in a dark, dark room with that terrible Child, myself.

There was a promise made, in meeting her. I waited for its fulfillment for years. It never came. The promise of her eyes, the promise of her mouth, the promise of her bloodstained fingers. It never came. God! That moment! That deferred burst of clarity, of connectedness, the *fulfillment of the Promise -*

Never.

And it never would. Was never meant to. Was always some abomination, some sad-faced deformation of unwedded birth. Something *impossible*. For years I waited for that moment to *mean* something, to be more than a random string of consequence. But it never coalesced, it violently refused to be. Nothing could consummate what never was. Some terrible, mutant symphony had been begun; its awful chords had been unveiled, but there was no conductor, no composer; no one to draw it to a close.

Looking backwards, I stare into the abyss. Where Emily was, an absence. Where I was, a shadow. She never existed. I do not exist. The events in my life took place on some stage composed of shadows while I hid in the empty orchestra pit watching wraiths perform those acts, sing those songs, mouth those words, on a stage whose meaning, whose form was incomprehensible to me. Yet I stared and slunk and wondered at the audience "Do they see this? Are they less alone than this silence / that rings in my ears?" This was all precisely most terrible due to its startling lack of froth, or terror, or great gnashing of teeth, or even substance. I had no good reason to weep, no reason to be taken seriously, yet I was absolutely empty inside, and bankrupt, and becoming more so every day as my credit stretched so thin. I wept over a night and a day where nothing had happened, which was the only reason I had for weeping, which was the singular reason, which begged for a reason, which had none, which wept. That day, that emily, that event - really less than palimpsest, beneath which my burning spirit bucked and heaved. Or, rather, reverse that. The emptiness is the ghost-gray letter that peers through the text of the event. Any event. That one. Another. Take your pick. I could have as easily narrated a trip to the grocery store, where I had my eyes on some freaking turkey, or reduced-price meat, or the ripest ripe cantaloupe, and some terrible housewife beat me to it, and there I am - bankrupt, with the whir of the automatically activated mist salivating cold-crisped vegetables, weeping, ripped by tears that shake me like a ragdoll and - the only thing - that holds me up - the cart.

Take your pick.

–M, 8/17/05

you noticed me

in a dream rose up in front of me

old graybeard, yes,

from desire.

Her leg was more beautiful than sex. And then I was onstage playing the drums for an audience of beautiful little orphan girls.

Flash back in time to the night before:

The earth was swallowing two giants, taking them back to their home. I read through my letters to L. In retrospect--how could I have been surprised? Here she is, a doctor's daughter, upper-middleclass-bound high-achiever--and I’m sending her an explicit record of my descent into abject addiction, crime, etc. Even I, narcissist that I am, was bored with the final chunk of letters--the spectacle of self-destruction was so... *banal*. Redundant.

Happy today, but need more meetings.

to bed now. bed.

**an unorganized array of thoughts**

organized by Richard Welsh

Self-concept: a phrase that causes me to tremble slightly, turn my face, perhaps draw knees to chest and rock, to flail for spinning lullabies. Possibly too personal of a definition. The book says, “...an organized collection of beliefs about the self.” Organized?! I cry and beat my fists against the wall.

Looking through the mirror, I see a chain of diminishing mes: infinite worlds of minute clarity, flashing before me and screaming truth! and truth! and truth!, lulling me to acceptance before being dashed to shards by the next vision, the next me, faster and faster until my eyes are scattered across the bathroom floor. Skewed windows that show me nothing. The book says, “... the term possible selves refers to one’s conception about the kind of person one might become in the future.”

I am prone to long-windedness and tacky verbal flare. This is most evident when I am faced with looking at or disclosing myself. Nestled in some words, some of the time, is what I want to say.

Point 1: My self-concept is in a state of confusion. My idea of who I am is reduced to a narrow vision of days and minutes. I do not know who I was. I do not know who I will be, and any glimpses of the present are fleeting, at best.

Will this thought, this writing, become a pointless wander? I seem to know that I started with something to communicate. Webster’s dictionary tells me that to wander is to have no permanent residence; to be nomadic. I began with a destination. Something tells me I will get there, will communicate. Thank God I wander; I would not be happy with a residence built here and now.

Let’s think about this over a cigarette. Perhaps a little brainstorming will help. I know I am a writer. I know I was a drug user. I know I am an addict. I know I became so terrified and convoluted and hidden from myself that I could only disclose myself in nonsensical gibberish. I know much of that still remains. I know I sincerely prey that neither formality nor timeliness factor too heavily in grading. I know I am academically gifted. I know I am emotionally stunted. I have a vague impression that emotional intelligence is far less set in stone than IQ. I know I am a shame-based person. At this moment, I am blessed with some sense of the depth of my ignorance. I know this makes growth possible.

Often in the past, I have taken to the odd practice of basing self-concept on the ways others have wronged me. A twisted validation process. Movie theater in my mind, playing over and over, from every imaginable angle, the exact manner in which the pitcher had thrown the ball into my face. Growing shock, appalled refusal. I was right, I was right, I was right, until I was frothing over an accident. Most importantly, my attention was as far as possible from my actual self.

My self-concept has been broken by sensitivity to reality. It was very easy to base my self-perceptions on the actions and mistakes of others. Finding an accurate viewpoint, some medium between god and dog... tentative.

I grieve over loss of perfect world and perfect self, fanciful as they may have been. I grieve over acceptance of reality. Truthfully, it’s not as bad as I often imagine. It’s not too late to get my life started and to do something helpful with it. My inventory of personal experience will enrich me someday. Have you ever opened a book to the last page and read it before starting? I’m still at the beginning of a journey. Acceptance allows me to start where I’m at: the beginning.

I find myself wandering into a residence, a new formula, a conclusion. Others’ words, my words, “We found we were neither as terrible, nor as wonderful as we had perceived.” Robert Zimmerman, “I was so much older then, I’m younger than that now.” I stand precariously aware of my own truth and depth (still afraid to look down). I am a young man who is not, thankfully, perfect. Sometimes the simplest admissions are the hardest. What an odd thought, that by letting my flaws go, by knowing and accepting them, I may work autonomously against them. Or something. Arrogant to a tee, and finished.

The mood is tight across the throat, keen against the chest. We tremble as our heart flutters in its grip. The wave is crashing, rolling along against veins, through neural nets; behind my eyes two stars are sparking.  
It all unfurls in the body like the petals of a deep curling spider, crisp and red and stiff like a finger. Unclenching in every vein. To the toes.  
Great wave crashing on the shore, all along in the sand where we searched - who thought, this diamond mind of glass and splinters, long forgotten rocks on the sea - rattling and rumbling beneath the surface of the earth like a great beast in slumber, we on its skin and the whole world undulating with our trespasses.  
The sky breaks.  
The monster crashes through its flesh.  
Memory is long and dreams are deeper; it screams betrayal and its yawning is all of life, the breaking tide is free and all rivers rush to fill the vacuum.  
And we, all falling through this tunnel.

5/9/03 1:08am

Lauren,

Ok, so I lied. I will write a letter--even if you haven't returned the last. Why do I always want to complain to you? Spout out all my melancholy. Perhaps there's no one else who would understand; or maybe my complaints are groundless, and no one else would humor them. Or perhaps I hope to win you back through pity.

I'm waiting for a typewriter I bought on ebay. I'm convinced it will transform my writing. This, of course, is hyperbole, but I *do* find that the compositional medium has a surprising influence on the writing itself. Almost all the poems I consider worthwhile (at least, in the last month) have been typed. Paper just doesn't do it, anymore. But typewriters are better. This one is an old-fashioned manual Smith & Corona--I only hope the ribbon is fresh.

Ebay is a drug. I'll sell the world--every electronic device I see, my first thought is, "Sell it on ebay!" The fact that none of these devices are mine rarely muddles the purity of the impulse.

Sometimes I sit in terror of getting high--like it will sneak into my house like a thief and physically compel me. Night terrors. Dreams of poisonous spiders injecting heroin-as-venom in my arm. But instead I'm writing a letter, tonight. and I'm learning to play the guitar--I've tried to pick it up several times with no persistence.

Und now I vill be destroying vorld vit scary paw.

I should sleep, now--but I don't know what happens when I sleep. Only ominous memories float back. So I don't know what happens but I'm not entirely sure it's good and sometimes I wish I could avoid it.

I am so angry at the page, right now. I want to ride a Greyhound bus.

You know, and what do I know, but it sounded sorta like what the hopelessly liberal call a stereotype. Like the poor woke up one morning and decided they were tired of having food in the refrigerator, and so they let their fingers do the walking and scheduled an interview at the appropriate government agency and went in and filled out paperwork as thick as your neck and waited 6-8 weeks for the paperwork to be lost so they could go in and fill it out again and wait for their poor card to come in the mail—

Jeremy RE: psychiatric industry play (correspondence), 6/19/03

prozac is not-so-good, i think. but i tend to be superstitious.

i have been getting your political emails, and i emailed my senator/representatives about the epa amendment. they replied, too, which i was kinda surprised about. they're probably automated. stabenowski was much more avid about her position anti-it than was levin.

as to the play - most definitely - i appreciate any input, and can use some of your thoughts.

particularly, i'm having trouble knowing why person B is there. he almost seems unnecessary. what role does person B play, and should he be there at all? i don't want just a space-filler.

the play itself is a critique of the mental healthcare industry. i want the healthcare industry to be represented in the doctor. the main char. is more human. she's looking for a fix, goes to the doctor. spirals out of control with the meds.

also, i was thinking, why not have just one actor playing the parts of the various pills? such that the same actor would play the part of Ritalin, Prozac, and so on. and the idea is for there to be one lead Prozac with whom she develops a relationship, and several crony Prozacs to go out into the audience and sit with people and hug them and tell them how special they are--wearing, of course, giant, fuzzy-comfortable bright-orange fur costumes. the audience/stage would be linked that way. their attention wouldn't be on the Prozac on the stage, or the Prozac in the audience, but on the simultaneity between the lead actress's experience and their own.

let me know,

matt
