6/2/03

Douglas,

There’s something new, Doug. Something new. Slam? Performance art? I don’t know what to call it. Spoken word, maybe. It carries more power and sheer connection than anything on a page, and isn’t that what I’m doing this for? I’m so excited and full of life to be doing something like this, I got a book called the spoken word revolution this weekend, along with an audio CD. I fell into it *immediately.* I’ve only been doing half my poems, up to this point. Not half my poems like, half of the poems I write, but half my poems like only half of what they are, the same way a play on paper isn’t really a play. A play exists in its *production.*

Aye. Is there *any* way you can get audio Cds? You would love this, Doug, you would love it. I feel like this is what I’m good at, what I’m supposed to do, for now. I don’t know, maybe I’m just on a natural high, but Hastos Christos. It’s *living* art, yes yes.

My family is good, but my sister is constantly sick. Always moving from one cold to the next. Sometimes I don’t know, Doug. Did you hear that Matt Mondon’s autistic brother died from a respiratory infection? I worry sometimes, which is totally irrational, but sometimes I feel like mourning for my sister even though she’s here. Does that make any sense?

I think some of what I’m experiencing might be just life coming back, just the emotions coming back and - I almost started crying in the car this morning, just for *being* there. I would not trade this life for anything, Douglas.

I miss you. There are many times when I’m doing something, particularly at readings or plays or, stuff like that, and I say to myself, “Doug would love this.” How are you? How is your recovery? I hope you’re alive, Doug, it’s amazing. So much! There’s so much, I thought this program was supposed to work like a drug, a cure-all, a cure-all for every emotion and circumstance I’m uncomfortable with but BAH! That’s bullshit, we just feel. When there’s something we don’t understand, or don’t like, we just feel it, accept it. That’s life. The pain as much as the joy.

I’m just ranting, raving, this letter is a long free write and I’m ok with that. I’m not even going to read back over it.

When can I come visit?

Yours sincerely,

Matt

(performance poem), 6/2/03

So I walked into the first day of my college class jittering, an honor student and proud to be strung out, I- I- I— I said proud to be an honor student. I sat down at the desk all jittering and ratta-tatta and tappin’ my feet and carving astrological symbols in my arm and unabashedly, yes, unabashedly I am not *ashamed* to recite charles bukowski poems at the top of my voice under my breath like (mumble mumble rant rant rave).

And the teacher came in all white hair and aristocratic glasses, and he blah blah blah and started his lecture and me just ratta-tatta and tappin’ my feet. He asked for introductions, tell us a little bit about yourself he said and I thought, “Yeah, sure, yeah yeah, sure I’ll tell him a little bit *about* myself, I’ll tell him a little bit about myself *and* the revolution, I’ll tell him a little bit about myself *and* the revolution.”

So this, this thing, this introduction thing it went around the room in a convoluted snake train of blah blah blahs and whatshisname and whatshername, all, “hi, my favorite *book,*” and, “hi, my favorite *movie*,” and “hi, I’m an internal *medicine* major,” and I thought to myself, “Yeah, oh yeah they’ve got charm but when it comes to my turn I’m gonna tell them a little bit *about* myself, I’m gonna tell a little bit about myself *and* the revolution.”

So these introductions, they went around in a convoluted snake train of blah blah blahs and whatshisname and whatshername and I just ratta-tatta tapped my feet and carved astrological symbols into my arm and muttered charles bukowski poems at the top of my voice under my breath and—una*shamed* to be an honor student, I said una*shamed* to be strung out and I—just waited

For my turn.

It came. The class

Hushed.

My moment was here I

had something very *important*

To say, I was going to tell them

a little bit *about* myself, I was going to tell them

a little bit about myself *and* the revolution, a little bit

about myself *and* the revolution—The class

Hushed.

I looked at everyone in the mirror from my crystal island, eyes streaming, all jittering and ratta tatta and tapping my feet, astrological symbols bleeding. And now that it was here, now that the time was here I-I-I I couldn’t quite *remember* what it was I had to say—

My turn came. The class

Hushed.

So I took a deep breath, I let out a red-rimmed sigh, I couldn’t quite

*remember* what it was I had to say but I knew it was something important and so I just—

And everyone was *staring* at me and everyone was waiting for me to tell them a little bit *about* myself, everyone waiting for me to blah blah blah and what’s my favorite *book* and what’s my favorite *movie* and everyone was just *staring* at me and I and my-my-my my *composure*, and everyone was just *waiting* for me to blah blah blah and I-I-I I knew I had to say something *fast* and so I—

I just opened my mouth, “High-powered stimulants are *everywhere* these days,” the class

Hushed.

And I was really starting to feel the pressure I knew I had to tell them a little bit *about* myself I knew I had something very *important* to say but I couldn’t quite, I couldn’t quite put my finger on it and so I ratta tatta tapped my feet and watched my astrological symbols bleed and just—“I hope you don’t mind,” took out my smokes and ran my fingers through my hair—the class

Hushed.

and so I tried again I opened my mouth I said, “It’s like, it’s like -- high-powered stimulants are *everywhere* these days, everywhere these days. It’s like high-powered stimulants are *everywhere* these days. Do you know what I’m saying? Do you, do you know what I’m saying? It’s like, it’s like, ecstasy is remapping the DNA of an entire generation and high-powered stimulants are *everywhere* these days,” the class

Hushed.

I was starting to feel a sort of tense vibe in the air, just a little tense vibe in the air and it looked like they were freezing up like mannequins in a dead-dear headlight, and they stared at me with this sort of blank and terrified look, just this *look,* this *look* and I knew they were waiting for me to tell them a little bit *about* myself but I didn’t quite know what to *do* and I didn’t quite know what to *say*, and they were all just sitting there and *waiting* and so I just, I just took a desperate drag and let my symbols drip and I-I-I I just couldn’t I just couldn’t stop and I just opened my mouth and—

**“*HEY!” ***I yelled. The class

Hushed—and I just,

***“What is everyone STARING at!?”*** – I screamed. The class

Hushed.

“Forgive me,” I said, I said, “it’s—insidious, it’s, it’s like a fresh-water snake is sinking into our brainwaves and I don’t—I *don’t,* no I don’t really think you know what I mean, no I don’t really think you know what I’m saying but it’s not that hard to see. You *might,* you might just see if you took the time to drop off your aristocratic glasses and look, if you just took the time to look—” and I ratta tatta jumped outta my seat and flew to the windows and threw them as wide as they went and—

I turned to them,

I spread my arms—

“*See?!*” I said.

I just spread my arms like Moses,

“Just look at the *size* of that ocean!”

“It’s all around,” I said, “on every corner, if you’d just look, if you’d just, if you’d just look around you might, you just might see what I’m trying to say because high-powered stimulants are *everywhere* these days, it’s like high-powered stimulants are everywhere these days.” The class

Hushed.

Shortly after I dropped out of school and took the long and winding road directly nowhere, sex and drugs and destitution. I knew what I was saying but I don’t, no I don’t really think

They did.

I do know, that somewhere along the way, behind the starry sky of stimulants and black eyes reflecting the light of a dying sun,

My *turn* came. The whole *earth*

Hushed.

They’re all

singing in their cars, America, and I-I-I

I know my turn came. The whole *earth*

Hushed.

My turn came and I,

I knew I had something important to say but I-I-I-

I could only spread my arms like Moses,

and say, “just look—

just look at the size of that *ocean*.”

My turn came, but I couldn’t quite remember what I had to say.

5/31/03

Mme Juleff,

Ah. It’s very late—4:00. In the AM. I don’t think I have to be up at any particular time tomorrow. I saw a really terrible play tonight. I was forced to. THR 1010. Take my worst drug rantings—the very worst—run them through a shredder, and put them on stage. The most frustrating part was that the production itself was quite good. Someone put time and effort into the stage design, the special effects. The actors were also good. But Hastos Christos—the writing.

I won’t spend too much time complaining. I have six pages in which to vent, due sometime… sometime. I got nine months clean today! I’m happy for myself, good job Matt. Actually, I’m full of self-pity. But you know what? By the time I get around to writing letters at never-o-clock, not having slept in seventeen billion eons, I am *normally* full of self-pity and delirium and all those other typical characteristics of disintegrating brains.

I’m so sorry to hear about your mom. As to the chemo: I have to be honest - I don’t remember many details about the physical effects of what my mom went through. I know she was sick, and lost her hair, and very upset. One thing I do remember, very clearly, is that I really wanted to fix her. So much so, in fact, that I would get angry at her when she wouldn’t let me fix her. It didn’t matter that I couldn’t fix her, that no one could—that was just the hurtful delusion cooked up by my sense of powerlessness.

School’s going well - I’m signing up for Honor’s English. I don’t know. It’s not so important to me, anymore. I want to do well, but mostly just to avoid the chaos. I’m not going to learn to write at a *university*. I’m just going to have the opportunity to do what I would be doing anyways. For a grade. Eventually for a receipt—er, degree.

Oh well. I got a laptop yesterday. I got a chunk of debt yesterday, too.

Fuck fuck fuck. I’m going to Cuba. I’m learning to play the tuba.

I sometimes wonder what the point is, because my perceptions are so far off. Terry says it’s like binoculars - it’s a *self-perception* problem. When I do something right, I look at the binoculars through the big end so it looks small and far away. And when I do something wrong I flip them around so it’s all I can see. And when I think like that, there will never be enough.

Did you know that agnosticism rocks your socks off?

You can find it by the plastic baseball diamond on the back rack of the NASDAQ.

Did you catch that?

I’ve been listening to KRS-One. He’s droppin droppin droppin science droppin history with a holy leap of style and intelligency.

And I know.

How do I know?

And I know because of KRS-One.

Forgive me for sending the poem below.

I have to latch on and write whether it’s appropriate or not.

The world is going to end, Lauren. Soon. Right after my performance art.

All sincerity,

Matt

\[nonsense saga\]

\*

the airways

\[10 Jul 2003\|**12:26am**\]

a strash of long filaments of hair in water,  
bleeding twist of chromosomes on ice  
fluttering over tension in the wrist  
as enamel chatters on the roadside and  
dread dogs whine in the firmament  
of Train Station and on midnight benches  
crawling from underneath  
perverted murmurs of hope  
and exclamations of violence  
in receding tide of saltwater  
shells beneath our feet for days and days  
until we fall inside our silence and sink  
and sink  
and sink.  
  
this is a vision of peace  
for the airways of America.

**\[insert typed letters to C—early relationship\]**

*still life*

vibrate.

sit on edge of bed stare at nothing.

wake up, fall out door and stab cigarette into mouth, claw coffee out of beans and light cigarette to start car. vibrate. rattling green Escort flies down I-75 towards sun, leaves trail of ashes and bread crumbs. park two miles from University in cold shadow of Moon where spots are free and meters continuously die twenty-four hours a day. cross bridge. light cigarette. rush through campus, hooded hijab girls in Office, which is not an office but a worn spot for two or three on concrete ledge by pigeonholes and ashes. haze of smoke cubicle wall invisible between passerby and interior. stop, talk, ask the time and realize eight minutes ahead of schedule so smoke, spend singing and speaking in the office, make business gestures and meaningless small remarks about the nature of man and nothing. and. three minutes into interview they say i vibrate but are too late because i already dash off to class. vibrate green and blue and shimmer karmic energy. tap feet and take notes and shake in hand and neck. distracted by muscle tremors until it's time to leave and smoke and back to office for company fieldtrip. two hooded hijabs and company clown in company car which is Sandals. to restaurant, to lunch, to ever-after to good health. talk hours about addiction/love/living/nature of man and absolutely/nothing, sometimes/God. spill energy all barren, naked on table and talk disinterestedly and lap it up with scissors. step on it and seize the day dissected. spin in fingers like snow globe and spit back out until whole cycle breaks down and i break down and do nothing but sit and cry and stare and sing while whole world rustles about with books in arms outside rusty sheen of company window and rain, which begins to pour into fifth cup of coffee.  
  
and the day is made of lima beans. and i am already chuffing away to the next station of cigarettes and nothing, small square small of light on back of hand in the dimmest snow in Fantasia, walking. waiting. for the sun to set and vibrate away in cold Underneath of horizon and Shadow, wondering whether Winter will come and everything can die in peace in the cold blue dark of Underneath. stepping on feet, one in front of another until the motor cracks and i am off to infrastructures of pale white light that crumble in Insomnia.  
  
light cigarette. vibrate. sit on edge of bed and stare at nothing, waiting to trace small scratches of birds that sing in the window.  
  
sing.  
  
sleep.

**the final letter.**

Ah Lauren,

I am fully prepared to spill the whole story onto this page whether it is a good use of ink (computer code) or not. Is this a violent act? It may be.

So. First of all, let me start by proving to you that I am an upstanding, driven member of society.

Ahem.

I’m taking honors classes (just english honors) , directed studies about performance based work (next semester), at the top of my class in ancient greek, studying linguistics, and, recovering from the wreckage, a steadily rising 3.62. My lowest grade is also in my easiest class - it seems so fucking pointless.

Violence on the page, self-mutilations, but we’ll attempt to get around to something healing. Redeeming. going through…. what? pain?

My keyboard just shut down for a few minutes. I still don’t know how to type.

I am having a hard time getting honest with myself, maybe. In any case, God is… shaking me? I really don’t know what’s happening. I may be grieving. I have never grieved for any of these things (anything).

There must be a solution.

There is. I’m sure.

Let me start over. I am tired, I’ve had three hours of sleep a night for the last two days, and I really have learned the lesson, at this point, not to make decisions when I’m tired. I get frustrated at myself because I’m not functioning at peak and my emotions are all out of wack, then sort of… push the knife in.

I gave an open-talk last night - I plot and plan and scheme things to say, but something new always comes out. God shakes the truth out of me, and sometimes I’m ashamed and embarrassed and afraid.

-break-

and now for a completely different mindset. my mood is like michigan weather, and I’ve been outside so my fingers are clumsy and hard to write with. C was here. we went for a run. a walk, really, but we had a nice talk. that’s very confusing. I go through fear at many different times in the day, and sometimes it feels like it’s so much that I’m going to stop, freeze, like it will destroy me. but I just keep going, and I’ve found that i get through (triumphant arches, and all that jazz) even with the fear, and that is one of the hardest (most valuable) lessons I’m learning.

I will go to sleep shortly - it’s 1 and I’m going to be a wreck tomorrow. I’m working at home instead senior care, I do nights, 10 hour shifts, three days a week and, when I’m not too tired from abusing my sleeping schedule earlier in the week (case in point), I can get a lot of studying done.

-break-

the next day. early morning. someplace on the moon.

aha. I started piano lessons again this saturday - most of it’s still there, but reading notes is rough. practice practice - I’ve been thinking about doing this for a long time, and it feels good to go for it. untied strings, loose ends - time for a push.

I have a counseling appointment with jeanne today. I haven’t seen her in a long time, but I’m going through some new things and feeling, in general, displaced. I feel like I’ve been growing, growing for a long time, and, after seeing the results, getting the reward for the effort, am leveling off, but I have to go forward unless I want to go backwards. so it’s time for another push. honestly, I’m a little scared of the boundaries, particularly boundaries on writing because I am more vulnerable there. but… I know I have something to write about. I’ll push through the boundaries, draw a line and keep it. tooth and nail, all that noise.

this is a letter to you for hope. am I about to step on a soapbox? I don’t know. there’s just something hopeful about letters, to me. or can be. an unleashing when I allow myself to be open with another person, unable to see their reaction, knowing that this letter will sail across centuries and land with you and a piece of matt is there, somewhere far-off, unguarded, unsafe.

it’s okay as long as I don’t start editing.

when I get that feeling, in the pit of my stomach, like the writing will stop, my first reaction is to panic and start writing whatever comes to my head, as if simply writing is the cure. but I’ve found the only way is to follow the thread down and see what’s making it tick. follow it down with the words. does that make sense? these are not things I can work out by thinking, and they’re not things that scrambling around on the page will help. I’ll get sediment and dead weight.

but to follow it down carefully, ask for courage, plot it out…

potential.

what will we be, then? career people? what's the point?

Did you ever read that adrienne rich poem, diving into the wreck? it’s something like that.

I’ll put the last thing I wrote on the end of this - it’s one of those once in a year types, and I hope you like it. It was good to write.

thanks for the letter - I give you permission to write a prompt reply.

was that funny? it was meant to be. I appreciate being able to write (and get) letters, and I miss you as well and look forward to your reply.

sincerity,

matt

The subway rattles

in its sheath,

gray windows sway

between aisles. Rebekah

lets her head sink

to chest and presses

window to brow,

bleeds sweat, “It’s really

quite blue / this December,”

she says

to no one in particular,

fingers trapped

around the pressed

petals deep

in her pockets.

The man

across from her

uncomfortable, shifts

in his skull, mutters

the crazy,

shakes the bag

for quarters.

23rd avenue and

Rebekah departs, leaving

oil and skin

on window. The man

draws into himself and reads

the Times, not seeing the letters

at all / and dreaming.

postcard from L, 7/9/03

You write to me

and distant and suggestive,

like the rain.

You talk about all the

casual things, family

and school and Salvation,

(I can see you, waving

unfocused, dreaming of

a far-off shadow.)

I don’t know why,

but I know

we might not believe

in quite

the same way.

I am torn

between hanging my head

in shame

or shaking it.

When we were in love I

was Underdressed.

You were the good girl and

I was just fine with that.

You were just fine with that, too.

I want you to know that I

gave up

that life,

and it wasn’t for you.

But sometimes

I wish

it had been

for you.

I see

stark Revelations. John

must have felt like this on

one day

or another.

I shred the letter and

smoke cigarettes

until the night burns away and

Dawn rises

like sullen

red

match tips on

gray

striker

sky.

looking for the words,

I rummaged through my pockets, credit cards, expired gift certificates, the refrigerator, dirty closets, the newspaper,

but only coupons fell out.

locked myself in my room and turned out all the lights and prayed and meditated and scratched foreign symbols and burned my notepad and started over, threw myself out the window to count stars and question the man-in-the-moon and stumble through midnight streets,

got serious and studied dendrochronology for eight years at Harvard writing dissertations on the importance of your life, got discouraged by the bureaucracy and dropped out,

pawned textbooks bought bus tickets for a new frontier, to near or far and went there, stretched out like an empty hand across back roads, barrooms, empty hotels dead theaters New York, teetering husks of buildings, friendly small towns where no one knew your name,

across the ocean to Tibet to monasteries to hidden wisdom to Nirvana,

beyond,

to the supermarket looking for a gift to give you.

returned empty, beaten,

ashamed to have nothing,

waited in the blistering cold beside a Greyhound and scraped tongue on the frost, begged bargained threatened the night sky to surrender! surrender it’s words for you or forever be cast into darkness,

it threw back only echoes so I wrote them down in the snow and blew ashes all over the letters until they melted and flew to you,

but I knew it wasn’t enough.

Rode home seven hours in the rain to the doorstep, dripping, barely more then travel dust and rung the bell to hand you a ragged shred of paper, smeared ink,

which read only “Happy birthday,” and

“Thanks.

For everything.”

Somewhere in the silence-

white light,

in blackness,

motes, on smoke

# xiv. More than the Ink of December

# xiv. more / then the ink / of December

xiv\. more than the ink / of December

[image]

September 12th, 2003

C,

I'm writing you a letter in the middle of the night. i'm at work. i don't know what to say. i'm in a funk. this part of the letter will not make it to you. maybe none will. i'm facing inner silence. shutdown. meltdown. quarantine. that icky feeling that means i will not put one word to paper until it leaves. or, at least, i will not feel good about one word put to paper until it leaves, and i will avoid, like the plague, attempting to write anything with a preplanned destination, such as a poem intended to expunge the emotion or, oddly enough, a letter attempting to reply to or include emotional content.

so this, appearing in front of my eyes, is an enigma. the real problem has absolutely nothing to do with the words that come out, but with the way i feel about myself right now.

i sometimes want to just stop, stop, stop writing, stop journaling (because this resembles, more than anything else, a journal), stop trying to work it out, stop beating the dead dog with a stick.

i appreciate your letter - it means a lot to me. much more than the letter, it's important to me that you be able to have a happy life, and (Jesus, I cannot stand myself today)

This has become just a waddling penguin of a self-pity session, indeed.

pour moi, pur moi

mares eat oats

and does eat oats,

and little lambs eat ivy.

how important is intellectual compatibility in a relationship? (Now you're really not getting this letter.) i write all kinds of letters i never send.

I'm calling katie bontinen, age-be-damned.

i think maybe what you're looking for an out from nick.

yes, yes, let's (seeing how as this is a private jam session) do away with the polite little lies to ourselves. carla, i sincerely doubt you have these feelings for me in more than a fanciful way.

Unless i misread the poem? what? let's be direct, here, we're both adults:

smoking stinks. eat yer yams. don't lie to the television. grow up to be a doctor or else. the garbage man is watching. prescription for sorry, prescription for guilt, prescription for better-than and lackey. help the world. your wealth puts you in a position of guilt. eat your cheerios. mind your bleachers. pave the stadium. buy astro turf for mother's day. write big, write well, write now and write a letter.

note to self: calling in to work to tell them that no sane person can work those hours would have saved you as much money as you're making by doing it.

\*

*i.*

camera shutters

waver and drop

into dream where:

Many white bodies, iridescent robes, shaved heads,

a piano key escalator shrinking to a pinprick in the eye's

dilation.

I click:

tuxedo leg crossed

pad white, pen cocked just so like a weapon.

radio waves over each head in angel wreaths,

binary thoughts heave between thin silica wires

which stretch / / and // / // /

it's the time between dawn in the gray mist I

click. with eyes open dream:

the Empty into which all vision filters.

*ii.*

in the living room meanwhile I:

stand up. sitstand. stand up sit

down. stand. touch the chair leg check watch digital

nerves on tight,

restless patter of hands, call friends family refrigerator door slam click open crunch slam

check for the dog, dark bugs on the window night light is buzzing while no

one is home.

There is a blank spot gnawing.

Stand silhouetted and hope out open window.

gasping for antelopes, i leave the house

touching the letter / pad stamps on the soft feet wait

for the mailman midnight cars rush vacantly one or

two

per

hour.

watch the rain fall on the leaves,

meander wind fingers,

watch for the mailman.

grab chalk.

stencil equations on concrete lawn grass

as green as her eyes.

lost in nails,

chew pencil, realize the vacant.

Raw emotions more

than the ink of December.

Check for casual winter thorns and look both ways before crossing.

Trees rush by.

*iii.*

the string in the labyrinth leads to this moment;

a breaking place,

let all recorders record it.

the horizon is dimmer in

verted, placed in the hand's cup.

drink blood drink type / writer

fluid, feel

the inkjet's smooth return and the carriage's

satisfied crash.

it feels good to be alive. i wonder, should i go on, and let you know who i am, or keep it safe because of fear, and i know which way to jump. real human beings are crazy - i think about this, when i judge others (which i do.). my dad was talking about teddy roosevelt (spelling?), today. this man declared war on south america while the white house administration was away and he was the secretary of the navy, and when they got back they had to undeclare war on south america. and this man became the president. real human beings are really crazy, and i remember that when i find myself judging others or trying to see myself as something besides a real human being.

and i think about that william carlos williams poem "... sure, love is cruel, and selfish, and obtuse (at least, blinded by the light, young love is)" and i wonder. and i think, of course our love is cruel, and selfish, and obtuse, and then i ask myself how much am i willing to let a poem dictate my life. or how much am i willing to let anyone else dictate my life? i'm the only one who has to look in the mirror.

*the bridge*

I’m sitting in the empty parking lot of the Chinese restaurant with faded red roofing. Jim’s or Joe’s, Chinese/American cuisine for the whole family. A big sprawl of quartz bits and gravel and hairline fractured concrete at the edge of commerce. The city’s excuse for a forest directly in line of headlights: ragged leaves half-naked, brambles, the empty infinite of train tracks and a whistle in the distance.

Strange midnight rumblings.

A bedraggled clearing rests just past branches, weeping arms, the matted carpet of beer bottles and rain and wet, wet leaves which float on the pavement like oil.

I haven’t been here in many lifetimes. Two or three. I carry no contraband this time but still wait for the siren. I wanted to come in the day – the bright white, write about hallmark cards and wax poetic. It’s dark now, like before. Always dark: I’ve never seen this place clearly.

I can’t stop smoking. Hovering ghosts of the long-dead appear in the tar stains in my windows. They flit always at the edge of vision. They are looking for something, telling me something, but the wind eats their voice, the groaning semis eat their voice. Nighttime whispers which don’t exist eat their voice.

Ghosts always speak more clearly at night, in the forest, on railroad tracks which stretch forever like memory and sentences. Faced with a question, the limitless possibilities of the spirit produce nothing.

I hesitate. I tap my pen.

I will have to face myself.

Armed with Winstons, I leave the car unlocked in its clutter of coffee cups (which is not unlike the past). The door clicks. The trees tear at my jacket. The walk isn’t as long as I remember. My heart murmurs, only the ghosts and these Winstons and me. I’m in the clearing; it’s raining; I feel I should have some say in the matter.

I clamber up loose rocks, shift under soles and huff in the lung, final burst and vision crests, breaks free in the ridge of the city’s metal spine. Clear path through muscle, sinew, choppy tufts of foliage, the spreading capillary streets laid out in a descending splash of blood and life - the calcium covering. Main nerve for drifters, wanderers, the homeless find their way to its vertebrae.

Make my way to the bridge. Shopping cart in the rusty river next to vacant swan’s nest gone somewhere for winter. The bridge perched between present and past. These tracks were on the way home from work and it was always sunny. It was always soft time in the falling afternoon in low traffic in low water and the trickle of the fishing line. From this vantage, I see cars lumbering by, distant lights.

I need to find something. I need to hear what these ghosts are saying.

The wind rips through everything in its way and drags the clinging things behind. I am in the eye of the hurricane, but blind. It’s cold. My fingers itch. I brought Sharon here once and we took morphine and watched the river and the slow ache of the sky’s endorphins.

I threw up; we left.

I don’t know if I have the courage to claw through these branches; they’re very cold. I brought Lauren here in the summer and we laid in the grass and heard songs in our head. I felt forever and she, in my memory, danced.

Someone has taken the railing down. John got too high and fell off Halloween. Bled and didn’t understand the bottom. Countless falling thoughts, throwing thoughts. The memory of them. This bridge is silent memory. It was never the center, but always lurked at the conscious edge. It was a meeting place.

I meet here again, but no one else this time. They are in jail or scattered, dead to a different life than mine. I have to meet the person I never met before.

Whispers. Fog.

A satellite blinks and it’s just as good as a star. I make a wish. My clumsy paint arcs are still on the bridge’s stomach. Rough logs punch through the river like bones through its skin.

Again someday, maybe ten years.

I read poems here and wrote them. Made many plans to train jump and travel and hitchhike to Happy Destination. Threw rocks at the intermittent monster which ricocheted like the fumbling of intention.

I danced on these tracks with countless bottles and left them shattered in the engine. I chased these tracks to dark corners, to Nichols, to the doctor for more. Chased these tracks that never end trying to steal their home. Became broken and saw God in the supermarket on the horizon.

It’s getting too dark to write. My words wander over the notepad, dip down into the bottomless and lose their form. I have come too far to make the same mistakes; I’ve never met these ghosts to their face.

They settle down on the tracks, sit next to me. Slip into the still river and my murmuring heart. Matt Carter, where have you gone? Why have you never made good on your word to live life like you mean it? The doctor told me I have a real heart murmur; I really should quit smoking.

You, ghosts. This bridge is not for me. I have a new home. I write letters all day long, letters on the wind, the pages are the leaves of me and it is fall. I let the wind blow them near and far, letters about redemption and hope and the shedding of you. I am humbled by life - I have never been given anything so simple, like birch bark my skin strips free for the winter. I am not afraid of you. Wind comes every year and we keep on living.

Do you hear me, wind?

Do you hear me, ghosts?

I have won over the night, I have been through and come back with a candle.

Dear Young Lover,

I love you

and want to be with you always.

Dear Ghosts,

come with me where I’m going. Your long-dead are the bones of future revivals. This bridge has a home in me. Its spine is mine, its wind is mine. Its past is mine, I claim it.

This is the meeting place, the person I never met.

I see my face

shifting

in the water.

Dearest Carla, (correspondence), 12/13/03

Saturday December 13th, 2003, 10:45 pm

Dearest Carla,

I'm writing you a letter with my own fingers because it feels right.

I want to express something, but I don't know how.

deeper than all the surface things, deeper than any butterflies of emotion, is the simple knowledge that I am yours and you are mine, and there is safety there, and love.

I have the TV turned on, but the volume all the way down. just for company. ticking clocks are a familiar sound, alone at night. I want to be comfortable in my own skin - that sounds like a deep freedom. I won't know until it gets late, but I think I'm closer to that than I was three weeks ago, or whenever the last time I worked with Mr. Cryderman. it was very hard to be... still. that's the goal. I just went outside for a cigarette - alone in the cold. i lit the cigarette, paced up and down the concrete floor of the walkway between apartments, then stood on the ledge and watched the night. Halfway through the cigarette, a man came out of another apartment and repeated the same set of actions. he didn't notice me, but I watched him stand on the opposite ledge - he walked the same way, too. slow. measured. it's good to know... it made me feel not alone. he was just a person i'd never met, and probably never will, but our reaction to the night was the same. it made me feel human.

i felt forced, and rough, last night. i want to be gentle.

when i look at my hands, at my fingers, at the scabs from hangnails, I know I am still self-destructive. I want more peace.

ticking clocks and thin electrical buzzing.

will you still love me when I'm taking 18 credit hours? it might be harder. I still have lots of decisions to make, concerning the rest of my education. should i go to grad school right away? start working? take a year off and travel? I refuse to settle for a white collar until I've been to Europe. (I may, at some level, refuse to settle for a white collar at all. my system might reject it violently.)

there are books to write, places to visit, languages to learn.

i look forward to seeing you tomorrow.

Yours in love,

\*\*8 (unfinished lyrical essay)

this notebook and i, we’re learning a new language. i think i knew it, at one time. much of the vocabulary is familiar and a lot of the sounds are familiar - some words bring back memories of other times.

This language was a part of me, once; I think I’m sure. My heart is heavy; it’s very important that I learn it, so I can speak to you.

I’ve been living in this country for years. I don’t know the language; sometimes I feel so isolated. The foreigners look dark and ominous, when I have no idea of their intent.

I suppose I must look the same - running around holding up pictures of their landmarks, carrying \*unreadable\* drawings of their cultural heroes in my wallet, spouting out insane mutterings which are meant to be their poetry.

I’m trying to make friends, but cultural gaps are so trying.

I was raised in a multilingual household. we spoke, not one language, but many.

I’ve written essays, in this language. An occasional song or two, but, with no direction, it’s hard to find my way home. Failing to practice the vocabulary, I constantly forget what’s important to these creatures.

My mother was one of them. My father too, but he’d shunned his heritage for the fast pace of the New World, the New Language. We all had to learn to speak it; we were told it was the only way to survive.

“The Old Country is not productive,” he always used to say. “Their economy will dry up, their customs will die. It is a matter of time.”

He may have been right, but I hold out hope for the preservation of a proud tradition.

It’s been my dream, since as long as I can remember, to map the Old Language. To preserve it in some form. To find a way to share what had been so important to my childhood.

I’ve met a girl who lives here. She wears flowers in her hair. We go for walks.

The Human Tongue.

Marriage is purely a function of the state, in the new country. But here, there are possibilities. We talk for hours in the Old Tongue. Sometimes I forget the words and miscommunicate. I may try to tell her she has pretty eyelashes and end up asking why the toilet is wet.

But the Old Tongue is a part of this place's bones. The ground refuses to hear my stuttering.

I have found a home here. It can’t last forever... but who knows? They don’t believe in death. They have no word for it, here.

Oh, I’m exaggerating. It’s not quite so glamorous or mythical. The chickens still fart. I am still a foreigner. But... I am home.

I draw gigantic word diagrams on all the walls. I’m working on the dictionary. It seems less important. now. I might just go for a walk.

The Human Tongue.

Will these mutterings make it through to the reader?

I wish I had the words, but there are no dictionaries, here.

ii\.

this notebook and I, we’re learning a new language.

it is sometimes vulgar, strange

(to our thinking) concerned

with flapping the tongue.

it requires

a guttural throat

and a great deal of patience -

it is a mother tongue ancestral

to them all, I see

its odd pauses

in most of ours,

can hear it

beneath the thick surface

of casual conversation.

What strange fish

it takes

to learn this speech; we’ve had

many false starts. 6 billion

characters, and not a single word

for death (the heart is always beating

in its verbs, it is a hopeful tongue,

and vibrant.)

Tense pages bruise my fingers

every night, but i return

again and again,

spiral-eyed and

filled with purpose - we must make it

home

to the Human Tongue.

We must find our way, these books

cannot keep tight

their secrets.

I’ve met a girl

who speaks it.

She wears

flowers

in her hair.

Moon, do you know this language?

Will you come down

from your perch

and speak it?

Sky - your stars are arranged

# xv. I'm Writing a Long Poem, Muse

# xv. I’m writing a Long Poem, Muse

HONORS OPTION PROPOSAL

Matthew xxxx

phone: 248.673.2130

ENG 5860, Fall 2003

Major: English

Rank: sophomore

email: aj2906@wayne.edu

The course assignments in **ENG 5860: Topics in Creative Writing** include reading a wide-range of texts, discussion, and regular writing assignments related to the reading material or a particular problem presented therein. These culminate in a final project of at least twenty pages, which may be in any genre or many.

In addition to regular classwork, my project for the honors option will be a long poem of 30-40 pages which pays particular attention to the work of A. R. Ammons in such texts as *Garbage* (personal reading), and makes use of the experimental style of Viktor Shklovsky. It will assess problems political and social in nature, including, but not limited to, the deep roots of the Christian vision of the Apocalypse in Western culture, and how it affects the individual at the levels of identity and emotion. It will also ponder “the linguistic complexity of the innovative work under the sign of Shklovsky’s Russian term *skaz,*” as outlined in the course syllabus.

10/03

O Muse,

O Muse who does not suck,

O Muse who is not less than Big,

whose shoe is so large that I

am not fit to be a burr

in its lace,

please spit your dewy

pigment

on my page, fountain

your brilliance

like vomit

on a cold morning after.

Muse?

hello?

Muse!

Just whose psychological hamper

do you think you inhabit? Don’t make me

get the spanker. I’ll come in there by golly,

and don’t think I won’t.

Argyles! Quantum farthing! I deserve

entertainment! get your act together,

get a job, make the money or else!

or else.

*soft touch*

sprayed across a doorframe

your

laughter

is the pathway

to truth.

cicadas

bend

like the tense

brush bristles,

their whispers

escaping

your wind.

*mumbles*

Down in deep lungs rattling around

I-75 attached to a cigarette in

green metal ashtray burning towards

a destination I’m happy

to forget,

lozenge in a throat like the frog

stuck to the roof of the sky

*tracks in the mud*

in a prepared grave of

paper, phonemes

mark the eerie passage of long-

unrealized behemoths

who hulked

through the swamp of living Sound and may once

rise again

in the carbon-date

of structure.

ii\.

My voice must be filtered through the

red beam of the satellite, projected

into mass minds, a great gaping

wound in the flesh of the vocal tracts.

I have arrived, audience, transfigured

by the iridescent hands of the radio, the tremor

of waves collecting in the pistons

of the synapse. I pool there

like a thick oil, coagulating in defensive

maneuvers, metallic squadrons

of antibodies ripping free from the nipples

of the mother ship. Do you hear

what I’m saying, audience?

the gears are twisting switches.

we were unclamped from the

spring of fingers red, elite, fingers

raw from the scratch of their century -

uncurled like tight petals or

retractable teeth in the mouth

of the cannon

by technology -

O arcing of cinematics, squinting

eye of the camera, you unopened

yourself to the sunlight, gave

grasping hands to the silent masses,

made them quiver in the headlights of

vespers, neon matins, electric

hours of reckoning sucked

into the keyboard of dream -

flesh in the steam of the

steamer, red coals in the husk

of tobacco, filters came with

nicotine transfigurations: the engines

of Insomnia have

been turning.

the dot of satellite

revolts in the sky. when the Near

is now, the charge of time

is slipping and

batteries

will suffer the consequences.

ii\.

an unseen threat to

democracy or such and such,

and decency in everyplace, et

cetera, et cetera.

Lo! (the terror)

the young men must march

while we stay and watch,

and stroke our oblong, our bright pink,

our post-modern nuclear tomahawks.

\*

I’m writing a Long Poem,

Muse. Feel free to address me; I send letters

everywhere, to all kinds of

anyone who will write me back love

nothing more than getting

letters in the mail.

Yes, I will cut some of this out.

Please stop, Muse. Be beautiful, Text.

Muse, I’m addressing you! take

your fingers out of your ears. I don’t pay you

to do nothing all day.

\*

Draped like a

nightgown on the floor of the bedroom, I take

a soft step towards the mirror. Cut throat mutters

proverbial nothings on the notebook.

What is it I have that you want, dear hammer?

Wouldn’t it be just as appeasing for you to leave me

on the floor in a rumpled structure of

disappointment, prayers, unanswered cell

phone calls? Which is ringing, please, I break

again I shut the drawer.

I will

not leave unfinished beginnings. You have

the power of will-bending. I bend to you,

I break -

the cloth of the world is burning, I will not

stop bleeding until you speak.

I shut my wrists and light a cigarette.

\*\*

I’m in a windup toy car puttering

through the ancient city Brain:

I stop the motor and get out, gaze

apprehensively at the towers of

sky and civilization. this must have taken

centuries to build.

but the city is abandoned.

I stand, smoke

a cigarette on the roadside

stutter with inaction. I finish

with a long drag, flick

the cigarette long and far,

and even further, knowing

it’s all in the wrist,.

i chuff away to the future,

leaving the cigarette in a frozen arc

through the evening air of Manhattan

until the next letter,

E,

I did get your note - I believe I even started writing a return letter, but it's lost somewhere in a stack of notebooks, which I've been filling up very quickly. Scattered around the desk somewhere.

I'm reading your letter. I feel like it's time for a smoke break too, but can't take my laptop outside. I mean, I guess I could, but it would be an inordinate amount of work just to smoke while I write. I will have a desk with an ashtray, someday, E, and then they'll all be sorry. They'll *all* be sorry. "No smoking" signs in classrooms - how do they expect smokers to learn? It's discrimination - we, as smokers, have much less time in which to learn things than your ordinary person on the street. And still they make it harder for us.

Apartheid!

Social injustice!

I feel like that a lot, too (like i'm not where i'm supposed to be with my life, like i need to change, heaping all kinds of guilt on myself for where i'm at) and then i use guilt as a sort of weapon to make myself change. do you do that? it never works. ever.

or so much so and so on.

time for a cigarette break.

back. you know what? i only smoke in my letters with other smokers. very communal. or, at least, i only let other smokers know when i'm going for a cigarette. we smokers stick together, and you can't stop us. right now, at the north pole, around the red and white candy cane barber pole and snow and ice for miles and miles, sheets of it, and all you can see is white and snow--and a group of smokers huddled around a lighter.

wearing no mittens.

And so now. what to talk about? i'm preparing to order subs (after this letter.) and then we will eat them and turn on the music and sing (and dance) and play a board game or something. but the important part is the singing and the dancing. my sister has been listening to the violent femmes and the stray cats.

i don't know about this memory thing, i always seem to come up with memories from using or near that period, but it's still fresh and vivid. i feel like i should be giving you memories of things that are going on now in my life, like by not sharing current memories i'm somehow saying that there's nothing going on in my life. but. i think maybe i just need to work through some of these memories before i move on.

when i was detoxing for the last time, it was fall, it was orange out, i was in the driveway. i was coming home, i don't know from where, i hadn't slept in several days. i thought i was dying. my memory is really fuzzy around this point, but i think i started crying in the driveway. i don't know. my sister was out there, sitting at her picnic table, digging in the dirt.

wow. looking back at this, trying to recall it, i realize how patchy memory really is. honestly, most of what i would be writing, some of what i've written, is filler, things i've made up that fit. i only have an impression and the bare bones of the experience and the emotion, which is odd for me, because most males have a very low emotional recall, but i guess that's what i do as a poet. or so much so and so on. in any case, the bare bones: i was broken in the driveway and my sister came and comforted me, and told me something to the effect of "it's going to be alright," although maybe not in those words. and that was very touching because i am her big brother and those are not normally the roles we play, she as the comforter and me as the comfortee.

so. i was thinking of that as i was thinking of memories to give you, but i didn't think i was going to give it to you because of the thing about looking for the right kind of memories. fresh ones.

i've included something i wrote about the bridge - i hope it will give you life like writing it gave me life. do you know the bridge? you do, don't you?

yes. you do.

well, there is the bridge. its bones. and my memory, which you're looking for.

so. to family night. happiest of birthdays. it was a pleasure seeing you and everyone else, and i appreciate being included in the celebration.

until next letter.

M

who do i write a letter to? i feel like a hand is reaching down

through my throat, my lungs, my stomach--to tightly grip the heart.

let them rip free from the foundations–

until they are dust and glass and ashes.

bliss comes quickly.

in the grave all things remain

and come again with morning.

Worms worry, the flesh of the skull is sinking. I have a great gaping void of the eye, the black heart of the song with prismatic fire lapping, the edge of the palm is seared like a conscience. I use their imagery; I know their symbols.

The ambiguity of a pronoun on paper.

Tall robes in spider webs stuck like a bunny. Twitching ears.

A soft cotton tail.

Spread-eagled in the silence of matter, internal vacuum, God and his Spiders come creeping, spread-eagled in the silence of the steeple - matted against the spire of church bells and the deep wrenching gong of the tomb. It tolls the day and the hour.

October is gray.

Somewhere the tense rivulet of steel is stretched across a web of metal wires. my back is flat against the mesh – the spider steps and I feel vibration along every inch of the structure.

The deepsounding gong marks the day,

The bell of the tomb marks the hour.

October is gray.

# xvi. A Transfiguration

# xvi. a transfiguration

a guide for the perplexed, 4/22/04

Dr. Aguirre,

A guide to the poem for you and for me. Where to start?

The spatial mapping, I have discovered, is vague because it seems that the reader’s first assumption is to think of the map as spatial. This assumption is fundamentally wrongheaded. The deal is that the map is not specifically spatial, but rather a spatial map of spiritual or affective states. Each group of poems denoted by small roman numerals, to my mind, is roughly equivalent to a point on the map. The actual events of the poem don't correspond to any physical point, but to a state of being as relative to stagnation, descent, etc..

Secondly (i feel like i'm grabbing at straws, here) Scott Hollifield brought up a good point about the invocation:

> "...the invocation is stunning, but ... perhaps over-defined by its predecessors. Follow me for a moment: We're summoning a 7th century Christian bard, in a Homeric style, invoking Penelope, Virgil, modern industry and depersonalization, theoretical physics, Islam, fin de siècle pastoral, and spiritual desolation. While all of these ideas are for the most part touched upon in the body of the piece, we never get a clear sense (even in the abstract) how all these things are collected into shrinking space, pressurized, and exploded into Revelation."

The invocation was simply, at the time, a plea for the inner forces to be funneled through the instruments of poetry: an earnest need to be filtered through the substance of what all these touch on. The reference to Mohamadden angels was not a reference to Islam, but rather to Ginsberg's "Howl". I guess it was a plea for the poem to take its place. I don't know if that helps or not, or makes the invocation any more or less appropriate, or how... I guess I feel like I have no responsibility to deal with the specific names/concepts in the body because I was not shooting at them, specifically, but rather at their spirit, their redemptive value, their poetry.

Secondly second, something that I haven't entirely digested yet, nor was I holding up as a frame of reference when pounding out the latest structure (neglectful of me), is the struggle between order and chaos, day and night. There are recurring motifs of day and night as specific entities in the poem: night as a time of passion, emotion, longing, undefined borders, gray space: a place lacking time or substance, held up against the day, specifically first daybreak, the sun on the horizon (which, by the way, comes from the Greek word for limits - terribly fitting): a time of borders, restraints, definition---

There is a constant struggle within the poem (and in my life, I imagine) to bring the viscera of the night into the day - to capture it, to trap it, to crystallize it - to pin it to the sky like a sick dead bug for all to see and science to profit from -- to hold it still inside the horizon, to give it definition and borders and boundaries so that it can be examined. So. Check it out when you're reading. I haven't checked thoroughly, but i imagine this representation is fairly constant in the poem, and in some ways the poem could be charted as this journey - the struggle to bring the night into the day, and eventual success - the energy of the night --

A classmate suggested that it was the energy of the night that destroyed the day. Or should be, and I tend to agree. So, how to clarify that ... the energy of the night spilling out, breaking its confinement - destroying, culminating in the shatter - the destruction that has to come before a new thing - the clearing away of the old debris - the forest fire which brings new life --- hopefully, in part IV, the integrated voice. Notions of time are all tied up with day and night, maybe just another way of talking about definition or its lack - part III ends with the moment crucified on a clock - "eternity moored in the thunder / electron splits on the cool radial / quartz, millions eyes stretch in / finite, in chains. / / a breaking place.. / / rain."

The third and fourth parts feel particularly unfinished and in some parts corny to me. I don't know exactly what is missing from this for the finished product, the full fruition - Rebekah completely drops out of the already sketchy plotline, in IV, but i think that's fitting to it. In fact, I'm not sure how i feel about IV mentioning Ichabod. Stay? Go? Also, the "points along the map" indicated by small roman numerals are *much* less helpful, much less defined, much less meaningful as distinctions in III and, especially, IV.

I don't know if any of this is helpful to you as a guide or as an insight, but here it is. Your critical / theoretical / practical eyes, I hope, I expect, will be extremely helpful to me in this.

Looking forward to working with you on this project,

Matt
