'the colors I sing,

the...'

ii\.

He is tired -

he's been

for weeks

underslept

and forsaken.

he wanders the fields -

by his dreams

at the last

overtaken.

sun breaks

and he is / clay angel,

stretched out

at the feet

of the desert,

skewered, exuberant, tangled –

*ii. a Trailer Park Altar*

the opaque sphere swallows like teeth of a bird.

the tense scribbling of stairs in the canister

of heaven, raking tense / bristles the sky.

the cigarette shifts hands. it’s uncomfortable,

muttering, using / the same words.

three raps in quick succession.

the nest twigs burn in blue

sulfur flashes and the misspellings of Egg

hatch thin things in the uneasy

light of the trailer park. Dark shifting

of stars uncovers blankets and haphazard

housewives (hair of snakes, hair of

delirium) tremens into the pale concrete

of the moon and sink / in its tranquility,

the Mad Jealous Husband sleeps heavy the

trench of the bottle’s bottom restless on

the feet of the couch, TV static grimly

announces the nothing of the hour. I watch

from the tree and spit / the flak

of the cannon, atom bombs on the dilated

Time of horizon. these housewives / are the

undead heels of the night; I wait as they clamber

the ziggurat, voices / joined together

the chant / on the stack of the altar

*i.*

Adonai,

come softly, quickly,

burning through the branches.

midnight looms like

monolith.

your sad

sulfuric face groans

in the clock tower,

pinned to the square

by its feet.

the horsemen

wake

in the alley.

you stretch,

where you proceed by the second

into dark shadow death,

gears

ticking

the incalculable.

*i.*

Ichabod's ghost, like a spider

in the pale web of sky scrapers,

his voice in the scuttle

beneath midnight ashes.

in alley trash heaps, the burning

bar of wrist which bleeds

while he reads the signs

in the stars

and neon masses.

the horsemen approach

and he watches,

tuxedo

tails rest

in trailer park dirt

accumulating dust

and red static.

*i.*

Rebekah waits at the bridge

for morning to break

on the wet tracks.

she picks her way

over shards of glass

to the water

where she watches her face

with the dying Star.

"You are a flower in the night, perched

on a thousand lips,

a thousand ledges: everywhere

the light lands, I see your folded face.

If I could gather you,

to burn in the mouth of the hand's cup,

reach you with a hint of the hand's speech.."

and, unwilled, an arm snakes

into the water where it shatters,

where it shatters glass reflections, Rebekah gasping -

"what is the-"

the train replies in tin distance,

penetrating skyline; Grim monster

rattling momentum on gathered

splotches of gray hills spilled in distance,

whistle trilled in distance,

whale song whisper filling distance.

Single eyed cyclops of neon stumbles

through the wine-dark tracks, growing

blind in the night and

painful in watering eardrums.

"Oh morning come, oh -"

*ii.*

Ichabod ferments in the shed for days  
without vodka, drinking cold lifeless light of  
Ketel Drum, of five-o-clock, counting pitch-black  
minutes in a bitter ambition to suicide, hiding  
the desperate left-hand from the right, encompassed  
by inspiration at midnight unhanging  
shotgun from rack: a last-ditch  
madness across parliament steps puking  
bullets at heaven, rattling redemption  
on neighbors’ lawns fear  
finally gone, knowing somehow  
intuitively that God  
is unprepared  
for a showdown.

*\**

tossed about on the concrete,

rent by the city's aqueducts in

two,

in two,

underneath sky groping

at braille dots in blackness,

i swallow

several stars

while waiting.

*iii.*

beyond redemption arcing / the circle’s inner edge  
the circuit’s lip limbs / tangled, the thrust of anxiety  
  
a hesitation. all is lost for looking and an eye  
tears to the earth in / heaven’s vacuum, a spacesuit  
  
crumbles seals / hiss to be broken, for shame the vision  
curls itself in cracks / the pressure presses, pressurizes a  
  
flurry of lips thousands / of the scurrying leg: judgment  
falls / on the fallen wings / of Babel.

language is lost.

*i.*

The world stops.

A breath in the window

settles itself on the branch,

she reaches

for the handle

and the world

rips itself

into shreds.

She holds her breath.

*i.*

one day, i’m sure,

your face will return to me,

unknown for a decade in dream.

a thousand years,

no further.

your slightest whisper walks back to me.

*ii.*

Darkness descends on the anthill of twisted limbs and wind  
from the mountain howls (titanium mountain, nuclear  
  
mountain, mountain made of the sun) – the splintered  
ground groans with the birth of new fissures, capillary  
  
cracks spread and the thin hand of mutters  
asserts itself in the strangle, a groan of unnamed  
  
earth gears strain to stretch through the heaving  
iron, ore of steel, silver, quartz unsettles itself  
  
from the ashen mantle of Earth – somewhere  
on the shifting continents soot / bleeds into the meteor,  
  
smoldering springs from soil and smears / in hollows of eyes,  
the unnamed / stir a restless / gathering of motion, the sun  
  
screams free, snaps / the pink tendons of sky,  
a new night / is born and the firmament / howls with suffering.  
  
a green cicada / waits in the window, we brace  
ourselves for the coming flood of plastic / sheets huddle  
in the sweat of the bedroom anthrax / will crown the Messiah.

i tread softly  
on the soft carpet, nervously  
asserting the windows, making sure

that the plants  
have been watered.

*i.*

Rebekah

in the boiler red

with sweat streaks,

chained to the tracks back

bent with blood, hands

gasping the sky retaliating

the cold gears which crush

and the symbols

that turn

in the stars.

a flash

of gunpowder and the igneous

shadows

dissipate; a horizon

dimpled

with thunder.

*i.*

camera shutters

waver and drop

into dream where:

Many white bodies, iridescent robes, shaved heads,

a piano key escalator shrinking to a pinprick in the eye's

dilation.

I click:

tuxedo leg crossed

pad white, pen cocked just so like a weapon.

radio waves over each head in angel wreaths,

binary thoughts heave between thin silica wires

which stretch / / and // / // /

it's the time between dawn in the gray mist I

click. with eyes open dream:

the Empty into which all vision filters.

*ii.*

in the living room meanwhile I:

stand up. sitstand. stand up sit

down. stand. touch the chair leg check watch digital

nerves on tight,

restless patter of hands, call friends family refrigerator door slam click open crunch slam

check for the dog, dark bugs on the window night light is buzzing while no

one is home.

There is a blank spot gnawing.

Stand silhouetted and hope out open window.

gasping for antelopes, i leave the house

touching the letter / pad stamps on the soft feet wait

for the mailman midnight cars rush vacantly one or

two

per

hour.

watch the rain fall on the leaves,

meander wind fingers,

watch for the mailman.

grab chalk.

stencil equations on concrete lawn grass

as green as her eyes.

lost in nails,

chew pencil, realize the vacant.

Raw emotions more

than the ink of December.

Check for casual winter thorns and look both ways before crossing.

Trees rush by.

*iii.*

the string in the labyrinth leads to this moment;

a breaking place,

let all recorders record it.

the horizon is dimmer in

verted, placed in the hand's cup.

drink blood drink type / writer

fluid, feel

the inkjet's smooth return and the carriage's

satisfied crash.

This *clock*

is a breaking place, crucified

in its center -

check watch, the arms

spread wide eternity moored in the thunder

electron

splits on the cool radial quartz,

millions eyes stretch in

finite,

in chains.

A breaking place.

Rain.

IV\. a)poka/luyiv

1\. laying bear, making naked

2\. a disclosure of truth, instruction

a\. concerning things before unknown

b\. used of events by which things or states or persons hitherto withdrawn from view are made visible to all

2\. manifestation, appearance

*i.*

you knew all along the way

was cold and broken,

the stage is dusty all the actors

shiver, pale.

you knew and knew and feet

are broken, bloody,

knew and ran and won and

broke the shadows of the morning.

you knew and won, now go,

now run.

*ii.*

i drive all night

for dandelions.

*iii.*

Tomorrow the lie.

Today waits

in license plates.

I believe we will rise at the end,

victorious

and broken.

*iv.* *at least, blinded by the light...*

destroy goddamned fairytale love it  
cannibal, it

rapist,

stealing fingers from

the hand-in-hand, the human

error -

despicable poem i

claim you.

to wrench the sad

statistics from you;

a living

sacrifice to every

burnt flower / bed,

grow the rose,

find thorns,

string bitter necklace flesh -

feel blood

feel beating,

dig with the shovel,

resurrect bones,  
build

triumphant arches with bodies

meshed.

forever.

build.

*i.*

I push

through the machinery,

like a miner with my silly

hard hat

in the gargantuan

elevator

shafts

of the mind.

drilling,

while the whole world

is dying

for lack

of this oil,

for the breath

of this fuel and the calm

dark flower

in pressure.

I reach

and redeem,

by any necessary

means,

by the violent drill

or the desperate,

on the slick flesh

of the beast,

many stratums

reach

miles up,

deep,

there can be

no surrender

to silence - many

miles tower, many

wide but not

so impossibly

thick.

the only way

is through.

others

have found

their way

to the center, but

it must be

always

renewed.

by any means -

the violent drill,

the desperate,

i drive

to the center

because the calm flower's

absence

would gray

all the colors

of morning.

*i.*

this is our transformation: in the midst of the fire

burning eyes unblemished,

angels of the fall, angels of ashes, angels unnamed,,

this is the value: that we, continuing, redeem

beyond redemption: salvaging the even

ashes of the fall. Diving through the wreckage:

our glory: firm in the knowledge: all lost,

and the point of salvageability, well-past -

screaming defiance at the architects, the ashes -

in the sad face of the night,

lighting our damn candles’ all.

i am simply saying

the important thing / is how we walk / through the fire.

take this: a single atom, split, can cause

a dearth, destruction, or spin

a million blenders.

there may be nothing

particularly / magnanimous

about it. but.

tomorrow,

when the sun, bubbling,

thrusts itself, grunting, thick

through the shell

of the sky -

then, by God, we’ll see the aftermath.

you underestimate

the will to survive

under pressure.

this, *this,* the redeeming value (breathless):

a bag of bones, animated atoms,

*i.*

your heights  
have their distance,  
voice has its silence.  
(your leaves have their season)  
  
there is no noise in your thunder;  
your softest  
rustle brings me to tears.  
seven years  
in the wind,  
there has been no time between.  
  
in your shadows i am blinded  
by the brightest light;  
your night  
has never known darkness.  
  
i owe you everything you won't take.  
your single penny  
has its prisons.  
  
in your breath i am born,  
(and die there) your whisper  
is all of things that shatter me.  
  
when i knew nothing,  
you were the one

who swallowed everything after.

you were the last one

to know the first inch of me.

*i.*

carve out a good life for children / grit your teeth and

bear it, find something / decent for god’s sake in this

forsaken, find a smile even / with gray teeth, make

a worthwhile, shake your fist, stand against /

tell stories about / dog heaven, remember how

grandma laughed, get a good job find a good

neighborhood or build / a garden in the bad one,

hold onto pictures, and picture books, find an

album if you don’t have one write / poems

when you don’t have any money put / poems

in the gifts when you do, tell / stories

(the same ones) again and again, laugh

every time, go fishing let the / big one go don’t

take self so seriously.

*i.*

we sing

the same simple song

of self,

the same revelation

of character.

the same story,

your story,

mine.

simply put - starting at morning,

(yesterday morning) with birdsong

burning

in the window,

i forged -\\

look, - a nothing-story, a never-there -/

for a day, a long night,

always (I’m laughing)

beginning again

with birdsong.

will you please

please

listen:

it’s no sin

to forget again,

begin again,

with birdsong.

write.

*ii.*

all the birds chirped songs

no longer caught in headlights.

he woke from his dream,

a pleasant dream,

a fiction.

it was, of course,

a spring, and not the

winter he’d imagined.

he took

long breaths

to recollect the night and

willfully

forget.

Ichabod,

with birdsong

in red eyes and

nightmares in the pillow,

forget your sleep and

breathe..

*i.*

drink blood from the cup

until your lips are full,

and red,

and stained with roses.

and the rain releases in face-tracing torrent.

until the wires snap, and behind your eyes

is livid, lashing,

until the current hums electrical,

and thrashing.

until the symbols crash symphonic,

the full lips tremble;

drink wine from the veins until life expires,



# xvii. Footnotes to Heaven

# xvii. footnotes to Heaven 

(poem), 12/15/03

Carla (correspondence), 12/27/03

Carla,

you're amazing, dear. i have your picture on my printer, and i'm afraid it's consuming too much time. i keep talking to it and, (tell no one) smiling at it.

this room must get clean! but... i don't know if it will. i don't know what the future holds except books, and you.

-break - shower:

carla, thank you for being a friend. thank you for giving me the space to trust you, and for trusting me. you know, in a way, you *have* accepted me, and helped me get closer to self-acceptance. i hope our friendship continues to grow.

i was thinking about something i said on the phone, when you were talking about stealing, when you first told me, and i said something to the effect of "i won't be with a convict" or a felon, or something like that, something to that effect. i want you to know that i don't feel like that, and i don't feel it was right for me to say that or put conditions on who you are or who i'm okay with you being. i would, of course, like to hold you accountable for your struggles (triumphs and failures), as i would like you to hold me accountable, but... it's not right for me to put conditions on you.

i will finish tristessa tonight, and you may read it. i really had forgotten what a powerful intelligence jack kerouac is. i feel like i'm rediscovering the Beat generation - i had pushed them aside for awhile, because they are tied in inextricably with drug culture, but that does nothing to take away from the power of their message or their raw talent in writing. i was in the poetry section and i picked up a book of charles bukowski poems ( a Beat) and related to every one i read. he only got one poem, in the Norton anthology. "the only thing that matters / is how you walk / through the fire."

there are calluses forming on the ends of my fingers, which means i can't feel it when i'm picking my nose.

record that; i want it on my tombstone.

the neighbors are back over, which means it's time to unfold presents.

i will see you in digital fingers on the cellphone tonight.

yours in love,

(journal entry), 12/27/03

the last thing i want to do right now is write. so i will. journaling is maybe... second to last, on the list. the thing that seems like it would be the most difficult, right now, is something creative. trying to dredge a poem up. working on dreaded skits. so... maybe these are the things i should be doing. i will journal, first, and see what it brings up, see what is underneath, and ask for guidance in what to do next. a tenth step? what have i done right and wrong today?

i woke feeling extra guilty about carla, seeped into everything, feeling dismal. one thing i did right was read the book on relationships, and write a positive letter, talking about some things i've been meaning to for a long time and, in general, letting her know that i love her, clearing up for myself, as well, my feelings. i really care about her too much to let ambivalence and fear destroy it: important to be firm and clear about my feelings: i love her, she is the girl i love more than any other, she is my friend, probably my best friend.

one thing i did right was going to mcdonald's - much better than sitting in my misery is trying to do something about it. better, even, than calling a sponsor or going to a meeting is going out and actually living this way of life, i.e. clearing up the wreckage of the past. one thing i did wrong was not go in to the store. no, she probably was not there. yes, i did ask an employee. however, that employee didn't know, so i left being unsure if i had ever actually planned on going in and doing it. it would have been best to go inside, just so i knew for myself what i planned on doing. try again tomorrow.

one thing i did wrong, or let myself feel, not being consciously aware of, was hypersensitivity to mom about the vacuum cleaner. it would have been best to pick up the coins. i was also hypersensitive with kairen, and i made a smart comment, but i did the right thing when i went back in and shared how i was feeling and tried to make it right.

good meeting.

good work.

how about now? writing here is a good thing. a good way to experience growth. i saw a vision of charles bukowski hovering over his desk, scratching his life, his self, his very being into sheaf and sheaf which flew away on eternity wind in fractals of Existence which knew he Was.

what works for rilke, in writing, may not work for me. it's important for me to remember that, no matter how many books i read on the subject, i must always find my own way through to the Eternal Heart. no one can come with me. it is a lonely journey, lugubrious, sad gloom cloaked. alone in the darkness. end journal i'm tired of writing for the sake of words scrawling, heart or none, life or nothing, the blood in the veins dripping, seeping into the pavement and staining everything, forever, there for the bones of the earth and countless passersby to see and know that they have seen the Real Red life. or nothing. sad sediment, murky, turbid - this is worse than nothing, then, at least the silence is a testament to sorrowful things.

\*\*

of tristessa, i wish he had left the second half out. i believe what he built in the first half was innocence, removal from world, depth - depth in innocence, depth in isolation, withdrawn, deep dark golden thoughts with the rustle of life far above on the surface. spiritual experience, vivid, full of colors. i feel his coming back robbed some of the innocence, showed us the Real Man and the Real Disorder. i preferred the illusion and the deep dark golden thoughts.

Dearest Carla, (correspondence), 1/1/04

Dearest Carla,

and you are my dearest. i am at work, trying not to watch tv, but i discovered long ago that tv always wins, when it comes to attention contests. destructive, it makes my brain feel like it's melting. the worst part is the feeling, the desire to rip away from it and do something else, and the inability to do so. i met frank today; he is nice. we have all kinds of snacks for the party tonight.

that was pretty good at anna's, last night. i often feel uncomfortable at anna's, i become very judgmental.

i was listening to nick's conversation with his girlfriend last night; i could hear her voice, when he told her he was in an apartment with three girls. i had the strange thought, that, in some perverted way, jealousy may be a way of expressing concern, care, and love. or need, at least, and then i thought, if i just let carla know how much i care for her, in my actions, on a consistent basis, there will be no need to resort to jealousy. but... i really don't know if that's a true thought or not. it was an interesting thought, and i'm sure the latter part (the advice to self) can't hurt.

it felt good to inventory some things last night; in a lot of ways, it's become something i do naturally (after some pain), or in my head, but it was good to write it out and see. there is always more to see, when it is written and in front of me. there are still some things, though, that i just can't quite put my finger on, and i have no idea how to inventory. they escape me. i have hope that, as much as my awareness of self opened up in the first year, it will open that much more in the second year (as long as i walk through the fire).

this is the ticking part, when the gears are turning, and it's my instinct to shut off, to stop writing, probably because something is rolling around inside, a real letter is about to start.

am i too involved in your recovery? i feel like, basically, i keep my hands out, but i am responding to something anna said, which i often find myself on the defensive about. i dunno. there are so many things that have gone on in my mind. for example, i was having a really minor disagreement with my mom today. it was really a small thing, and i took care of my part, basically, before i even acted on my part. which is a good switch. and i was turning my thoughts toward relationships, you (where they often go) and there was this feeling that i would never be able to function, in a marriage, this feeling that there could be no harmony, like rich was talking about, and i realized that it was because that's what i learned. in my home, watching my parents, i learned that minor disagreements can't be worked out, and that they will, in the end, rip and tear. i learned that these things are a big deal, and so i perceive them in that way. maybe. maybe it's a natural part of my perception that would have been there whether i learned it, or not. but it's coming to my attention that this is not true for everyone, nor does it have to be true for me. i am typing fast now. i was at the mt. zion center the other day, working on a commercial with josiah. we were in rich and tammy's office, and there was a small question that came up about an end tag, and how it should be. and they disagreed, and they clashed. i could feel tension, but later i realized that the tension was only in my mind, and not in reality. right in the midst of the tension, when i, in my mind, would have been turning to hopelessness, rich made a joke. tammy was right. he said, "tammy, you're so smart" a little sarcastically, sweetly sarcastic. and the tension broke, and i realized that the only place it had been was in my mind, because i have not had an example of how a healthy marriage can work. but i look to people like rich for hope, and his life is, in a way, hope. not even so much his words, but his *life* is hope, like ours. that's an apostolic ministry, where the ministry is simply the miracle god has done in a person's life, the ministry *is* their life.

i guess i'll wrap down. it seems like, the more i write, the more i have to write about. there really is, in this letter so far, pages and pages of things that need clarification, that need exploration. funny it should work that way, that the more we talk about, the more there is to talk about. so the only limit seems to be this page and how long i am willing to write for, and how deep i am willing to dig to get material to talk about, and how open i am willing to be, and how many of my thoughts and feelings i want to give. i encounter this same thing when writing creatively: the only limit is me, and my character, and my qualities. i was at work today, and i realized that i am lazy. i avoid physical work like the plague, and i'm sure this effects me in many negative ways, most clearly how i perceive myself, as being somehow exempt from working like the rest of us, and i realized that, if i want what god has for me, i'm going to have to be willing to work for it, but that He can and will take me the whole way, and that something as small as willingness to work, to do the whole job, to not shirk, to be willing to do physical labor, can carry through into all aspects of life. and quality of life.

i am willing to work for our relationship, and it strikes me sometimes that a relationship is not just pleasure (although there's just enough of that) and emotion, but also a big commitment which takes dedication and work.

-break-

12:10am. somewhere the start of a new year.

dearest, i see all these people making out, and i know i am missing your kiss. i don't like to miss out on memories. i was thinking about romance, in the hallway, while smoking, and the thought came to me that... romantic love will not hold a relationship together, but it *is* a part of a relationship. do you really want to go to new york? i am seriously planning on going on a trip; save your pennies. we will go, one way or another, if we put our minds to it. if we drive, i would like to check out cornell - it's in ithaca, NY. i looked at it on a map; it's basically en route.

i did, in the end, put the computer game in, but i haven't had an opportunity to play it much. almost all that's left for tonight is a little cleaning up, a few dishes, wipe down the counters. take the trash out to the dumpster in the morning. -- just got a text message from you -- everyone says happy new years -- From: Carla -- text messages build up awfully quickly.

i will keep this to a succinct two pages.

g'night love.

in my thoughts, prayers, dreams, etc..

Dear Carla, (correspondence), 2/4/04

Dear Carla,

it's very late, and i should be wrapping up the endless studying or sleeping, and i will, but i feel the need to write you. carla, i have to pour out my heart - i love you. it gets hard to go on, i catch in my throat. you've shown me something beautiful, and we have something beautiful together, and it's better than i thought was possible. god surprises me with the gifts he gives - they're never what i think, they're always beyond my expectations (and i have high ones, but they're often distant, stuffy dreams of prestige, which dull when set next to the things He puts in my life).

i love the ability we have to talk, to work things out, to share what's going on. i have that with you, i'm able to share.

this is short, because it's time for bed.

it means so much to wake up next to you.

yours,

M

carla,

i wanna get to the roots, the good roots that are under all the walls that my finicky conscious self puts up around me. the fears et cetera that keep me from you, from my self of you and write it here for your record, for your self of you, and me.

carla, i never knew what it was to love and then i met you and then i *still* didn't know what it was to love, but you made me want to know - and i still do. i want to ... love you. treat your right. give you good things. do better for you, do better for me for you, (and me.) so... what i'm saying is, and i really have to keep typing here even if i want to stop, even if i don't know what comes next and i'm afraid of it, because that's the only way i've learned to get honest sometimes. carla, i love, i want to spend my life with you. i'm learning new things that go along with love, new desires:

i want you to be independent - i don't want you to be dependent on me, i want you to be confident in yourself and your abilities. i guess that's the nature of this new thing i'm learning, this new love - i want you to be fully yourself, i don't want you to need me so badly that you are dependent, nor would i want to be in that situation, even if it kept us together. does that make sense? you've shown me, i've discovered, god's shown, something more important than just being together, than just surviving.

we are separate people, and we should be. what is it about that, about being full and complete in and of ourselves that makes love... that makes our coming together... more worthwhile? we can take the time to grow, to find ourselves because our being together is an act of the will, a choice, each day.

maybe that's the new thing: choice.

i choo-choo choose you.

et cetera.

Andy, (correspondence), 5/5/04

Andy,

This life shifts around under our feet, gives me vertigo; the last clank of the tracks before the coaster drops and the whole stomach lurches free from the body. I have an interesting defense against this: obsessive future-planning, scribbling disembodied equations determining drop vector in the corkscrew's inner loop. Plans are comfort objects more than something I take seriously and, despite the number of times destroyed, broken, or realigned, I am instant in coming up with new ones.

I don't know where you're at on the ride, right now, but I feel I have to write you quickly before you're gone to another.

The bottom is the place where we stop digging; that's to say that the where of the bottom is our *choice*, and it's a new beginning. A cornerstone. When I get caught, when the structure gets stale -- there's the bottom, the place I started at, with nothing left to lose (we're talking internally here, not existentially). The greatest gift is not to be chained up. Then we can live.

Miss you brother; my prayers are always with you.

Matt

carla (lyrical essay), 6/2/04

Firstly, I'd like to say that the girl is soft, and I'd choose her over goose-down each and any day. Secondly, allow me to commend the girl on her charm and sense of humor - a degree of sophistication which marks the barest occasion (particularly when, like an untrained intellectual, she wears her glasses and her Aspen scarf, red and wrapped around the neck like a fashion noose).

I love the girl because she's a mother, a hard-worker, a friend - my companion. I love the girl because I don't need to say anything important or grand (I still do); my jokes can be as dumb as anything and she doesn't mind. I don't think she wants anything particularly from me, or for me to *be* anything particularly (except me), for which I'm grateful. she shows me and I show her and we show each other how to be just human beings, not too much more or less.

Carla, no one's written a song for me, or cared to maybe. Of all the things, this is the one that I understand the most: making something for you, you making something for me. There's something incredibly special in that which means more to me than... than anything else. This started with a poem, and it couldn't have without it. I could trust your poem. This is the thing, Carla - that's the way *I* love; by making; by saying there what words won't can’t say.

Look at how far we've come from the uncertain and terrified beginning, how much we've grown as individuals and as a couple. The poem was a possibility which I accepted and continue to accept. I have never taken a more rewarding risk than believing that poem at face value.

When I draw close to you, there's nothing that can tear me away.

The power of our love shines blinding; small men turn away; nations revolt; the earth spins wildly. The future is perched on our love. Whole generations of racket and clamor wait in the wings for our outcome. Entire races hang uncertain.

There is hope in love, and our love only.

But, if not, it's at least very important to me.

Carla, no one's ever meant more to me than you. There's too little time to talk about fear. I love you. Please, live your life for me; be alive; be happy. Too little time to talk about fear.

open talk notes, 8/23/04

working with others:

the first thing a person who is using will tell you is that, they're alright. in fact, they're doing good. sure, they use once in a while, but it's not as much as i used to use before, or it's not as much as my friend so-and-so. they're so used to hearing from themselves and others "you need to quit that stuff " or "what's wrong with you?" that they've stopped telling the truth, because they don't know how to tell others that they *can't* quit. they don't know how to quit, they've tried to quit and they've been unable, they've tried to do something better, to do something different and they've failed.

if you're there for that person, if you're motivation is to love them, to share your hope and faith with them, to feed them, they may see something in you that they long for - that's hope. that's courage. that's love. they may even open up to you.

when people open up to that vulnerable place, where they're willing to say, "you know what, I got this outside person, but inside i'm kinda broken," and i'm able to open up to that vulnerable place and say, "you know what? you're okay, you're alright, and god loves you.", when i see that hurt little kid in another, and i'm able to tell them they're alright, then the hurt little kid inside *me* hears "you're alright". when i see another person make it, then i see me make it, and that's why seeing others make it is so *valuable.* some of the most precious moments of my life have been very simple, quiet, and otherwise forgettable moments, but i was able to tell someone else, "you're okay.".

\*1 Volta Prißnikof calls technological inscription the physical manifestation and extension of the intangible inner processes of perception itself. Perception itself he objectifies as an inscription tool of the metaphysical substance of the individual. We are, of course, familiar with the long-standing division, in Western thought, of physical and metaphysical, and that such philosophers as Husserl have, within the last century, resituated the relation between metaphysical essence and corporeal substance as one of lodging: the animate, willful soul inhabits the passive body like a feudal lord his castle: it is mere stone; at his beck and command. More recently, Schlenner employs the dual functionality of the metaphor in his rendering of the relationship between *perception* and metaphysical essence (perception as both inscriptional tool and inhabitation) and, thereby, through a complex reversal and extension of metaphor, relates technological inscription as both extension and tool of metaphysical essence, and also its manifest inhabitation.

See Schlenner's artful analysis is *Technological Bodies: Remediating Metaphysical Essence in the Networked World*.

# xviii. O, Jerusalem!

# xviii. O, Jerusalem!

the very first drafts of 'O, Jerusalem!' (poems), 1/16/06

i\. to all you who / hover / at the entrance to forever...

to all you beaten and bruised,

to all of you uncomfortable / in your own skin, squirming

in the pangs of midnight searching for / a way to kill / the neon--that is, the yellow consciousness / of the bright-lit / mind--

to all you uncomfortable in alleys, squirming in your porches under the empty / moon, waiting / for something, or nothing, or for / the sky to fall in the alley, so you can pluck it / up from the puddle and hang it / around your slender neck--

to all you searching for dissatisfaction, spurred on by an empty / center, unable / to rest you’re always / restless--

to all you searching for more, forever wanting more to burn up out of your middle, to come crashing / out of your lungs that eternal / spring of living / water you’ve been / waiting for / for an eternity, and longer--

to all you under the influence of Time, singing songs at the speed of light to try and crack the walls of your pathetic prison, death, your pathetic flower Naked Life in its eternal tender flesh, exposed to the knife of Midnight--

to all you who have lost the will to / fight, whose / teeth have been plucked / from your fickle skull / like the buds / of an opening / blossom--

to all of you who / hover / at the entrance to forever and / ashamedly / turn back

to wander the dusty halls of your / unending bedroom, waiting, for the night to end-- (which it doesn’t)

to all you forlorn and biting / your cracked blue lips in the mouth / of the bitter night that / cold-eyed / killer, Night, that senseless mother--

Night the consumer / of her children, Night whose / womb is an empty catacomb whose / name is the dust of the cellar, who has hardened / her dark old / heart that / dark old heart the moon, that dark old bulb that / centrifuge both / empty and electric--

to you whose laughter leads to nothing, whose / ecstasies well up like / blood from the infinite gash / of the midnight at your center, midnight that terrible lover,

Midnight when everyone is sleeping that / terrible hour of truth, Midnight you sad old / bag of bones you hopeless hustler--

Midnight you irascible liar--

Midnight you unreformable drunk, you sad old twisted frowner--

Midnight you damnable sayer of sooths always / predicting the future--

ii\. the last pale tears of music...

to all you who have held your breath in the hurtling dark of sadness, who have prowled its long black lanes in the numb hours, who have searched its deepest corners,

and found them lacking,

all you who have beaten your breast, who have torn the tattered sheets from your back to stand without warmth in the Barren,

who have clothed your self in ashes,

and emptied out the last pale tears of music, the last white notes of the morning, which rang into the silence like a hopeless spark in the infinite, mindless ocean,

to all you who drank that bitterness to its drops,

who ran yourself through with its daggers,

who staggered down the hallways of your longing,

bleary, and disheveled, and drunken,

rocking, and weeping, and raving,

and starving for a cure--

and then (and this is the impossible part) turned back,

to take up your mundane life in the daily day and grind and the infinite papers and paid your bills, and ate your peas, and wrote a wonderful note to your mother,

who turned your back on the infinite night to take up the limits of your sad and daily expression,

and transformed it, the beating endless metronome of

who made the movement of the infinite, to descend / into the infinitesimal sameness / of your unaltered and naked / day,

who got the mail, and went to the gym, and took / the car / to the carwash,

who saw nothing incommensurable / with this, this daily and / the ultimate infinite--

who transformed your endless infinite conception which could never / exist / into a moment of silence / at the dinner table, / who sang endless prayers at the Endless,

iii\. the blessed...

My history is inextricably tied with the history of the Beats and the Beatles. They were part of something to which I aspired. That is, some thing captured them that captured me also - which in the end consumed them. I followed the wake of a frozen historical moment, yet I was turned back from its center. I stared into its center, into the holes of a powder white skull - into the Obsidian nothingness in its sockets.

broken and threadbare,

bald, unveiled, unconcealed,

defenseless and barren,

Finally and once and for all unmasked in your unimpressive glory -

Be magnified.

Blessed are the unimpressive, who do not aim to impress,

blessed are those whose glory is the Lord’s,

Blessed are the joyful,

or those who follow in footsteps,

a thirsting after saintliness,

whose hearts are pure.

who do right.

whose Father is God.

whose spirit is meek.

welling up in the midst of its traffic

who stand abruptly in the muddy lips of the dirt,

in dirt’s dark mouth.

Selah.

O you who sing songs at the speed of light

to try and crack the walls of your pathetic prison, Death,

your pathetic flower, Naked Life, in its eternal tender flesh,

exposed to the knife of Midnight -

who have lost the will to fight,

whose teeth have been plucked from your fickle skull

like the buds of an opening blossom -

O you who hover / at the entrance to forever

and ashamedly turn back,

to wander the dusty halls of your unending bedroom,

waiting for the night to end (which it doesn’t)

O you forlorn,

and biting your cracked, blue lips in the mouth of the bitter night -

(Night, that cold-eyed killer,

Night, that senseless mother,

Night, the consumer of her children,

Night whose womb is an empty catacomb,

whose name is the dust of the cellar,

who has hardened her dark old heart,

that dark old heart the moon,

that dark old bulb,

that centrifuge, both empty and electric.)

O you holding your breath in the hurtling dark of sadness,

who prowl its long, black lanes in the numb hours,

who have searched its deepest corners,

and found them lacking,

you beating your breast,

who tear the tattered sheets from your back to stand without warmth in the Barren,

who have clothed your self in ashes,

and emptied out the last pale tears of music, the last white notes of the morning,

which rang into the silence like a hopeless spark in the infinite, mindless ocean,

O you drinking bitterness to its drops,

who run yourself through with its daggers,

who have staggered down the hallways of your longing,

bleary, and disheveled, and drunken,

rocking, and weeping, and raving,

and starving for a cure--

Selah.

Peace be to you.

May the good Lord bless and keep you,

May he restore all the moments you’ve lost,

that have slipped / through your impotent fingers,

May the good Lord be your redeemer,

may He redeem you completely,

may He pick you up from the median,

where you, cracked and torn, are lying, stretched out beyond the radius of your wreckage,

May He sing for you,

and redeem you,

and wrap you up in redemption,

May the good Lord pay for your trespasses,

Selah.

May the good Lord cover you,

may He cover up the sleeve that bears / your old, red heart,

may He cover you up in your barrenness,

May He cover you, vulnerable and threadbare,

may He cover your bald old head that cracks in the winter wind,

your old, uncovered hands that crack in the bitter winter,

that singe in the freezing snow,

(And You, O Lord, who are also unprotected,

and broken and threadbare,

and bald, and unveiled, and unconcealed,

defenseless and barren,

clothed in your poor old circumcision,

exposed and shorn and stripped,

made manifest and naked,

Finally and once and for all unmasked in your unimpressive glory -

be magnified.)

Blessèd, Blessèd, Blessèd.

Blessèd are the unimpressive, who do not aim to impress.

Blessèd are the joyful,

Blessèd are the lovers of God,

who love with their heart, and their mind, and their strength,

Blessèd are the Sons of the promise,

who wait on the promise,

who pray for the promise,

whose endless expectations ache with the promise,

Blessèd are the seekers of truth,

who buy it with blood,

and swear,

and never sell,

Blessèd are the sons of God in the earth,

and those in whom loss lives,

in whom the long forgotten perpetually breathes -

you mourners,

in whom these dry bones live,

and the valley jumps

and the dawn’s dim hope yet shimmers -

Blessèd be you.

Blessèd are those in the midst of the night,

around whom blackness presses like a thick black scab,

who stab at the infinite darkness with their frail, pathetic candles,

and, what’s more,

win out,

Blessèd be you, O exiles, not having a country,

O fugitives and outcasts, you cast off,

Blessèd be you,

belonging to none, wanted by none, received by the wind,

interlopers, intruders, outsiders,

refugees, aliens, strangers,

whose kingdom is Elsewhere,

whose name is an infinite longing,

and a thirsting after saintliness,

who turn back and back and back upon the empty evening,

who will not stop short of the eternal prize, that inexpressible,

Blessèd are the pure of heart,

whose hearts are pure.

and the makers of peace,

whose peace is full.

Blessèd are those who thirst after righteousness,

whose longing is right action.

and the meek in spirit,

whose spirits are meek.

and the broken,

whose weakness is strength,

in whose shards is power perfected.

O morning star, sing!

sing softly! sing soft sweetnesses!

sing softly in the ears of Your numberless children!

in the ears of Your numberless sons and daughters!

in the ears of Your infinite orphans in the earth!

whose hearts beat and are broken

for the infinite succor of Your touches

sing, O morning star! sing! sing!

Dear Mr. xxxx,

The Program in Comparative Literature has reviewed your application for admission for graduate study, and we are very impressed by your record of excellence and the match between your scholarly interests and the Program’s strengths. We are happy to recommend your admission to the Horace H. Rackham School of Graduate Studies to begin graduate studies with us in Fall 2006.

It also gives me great pleasure to inform you that you have been selected to receive a Comparative Literature Program Fellowship. The Program in Comparative Literature is a five-year Ph.D. program, and the Program Fellowship is part of a five-year plan of support. Please be aware that this package is contingent on progress towards your degree, satisfactory teaching performance, as well as adhering to the Policy on Academic and Professional Integrity.

<u>Year 1</u>. Your stipend will be \$14,000/year plus tuition and registration fees. (A year is defined as fall and winter terms, September through April.) Insurance is not part of the fellowship package in the first year. This year is service free, and you will be expected to complete three courses successfully each term.

<u>Year 2</u>. You will be hired as a Graduate Student Instructor (GSI), and we will supplement your salary to bring you to the \$14,000 level. Such an appointment carries a tuition waiver and health insurance eligibility. You will be expected to successfully complete three courses each term. By the end of this second academic year you must have satisfied all language requirements and have begun preparation for your preliminary examination, which may be taken as early as winter term.

<u>Year 3</u>. You will be hired as a Graduate Student Instructor (GSI), and we will supplement your salary to bring you to the \$14,000 level Such an appointment carries a tuition waiver and health insurance eligibility. By the beginning of your third year you will be expected to take your prelim and achieve Candidacy. During winter term of this year you will be expected to complete your topics paper.

<u>Year 4</u>. You will be appointed as a GSI as specified above.

<u>Year 5</u>. You will have the opportunity to compete for a variety of fellowships and grants that, if awarded, will release you from teaching. You will also have the option of continuing to teach, in which case we will supplement your salary to bring you to the \$14,000 level. In either case you will receive a full tuition waiver and insurance coverage.

In addition, you are eligible for \$2000 in summer funding two times in the course of your graduate studies. Additional summer funding is available for successful proposals.

If you are an international student, please note that you may be required to attend an International Graduate Student Instructor training workshop. Students who have attended or are attending an undergraduate school where the primary language of instruction is English may be exempted from this requirement. Please also note that beginning in Fall 2006, the University of Michigan will require certain entering international students to be screened for tuberculosis (TB). Screening will be offered free on campus and a TB infection would not jeopardize a student’s visa status. A word or two about job placement: although jobs continue to be in short supply, Comparative Literature at Michigan has a strong record of placement for the last five years, placing 66% of our candidates by the second year in their job search. Our graduates have taken tenure-track positions at American University, Arizona State, Buffalo University, Cornell, University of Florida, University of Illinois, Pennsylvania State University, Princeton (twice), and Williams College, among others.

We have enclosed information that might be of interest to you. Please contact us with any questions you may have. We also encourage you to arrange a visit to Michigan, and we have a fund available to subsidize your travel expenses. There are many faculty and students here who would love to meet you.

The Rackham Graduate School may contact you to ask for additional materials. They will also send your final admission letter, and preliminary visa documents if you are an international student. Be sure to notify us whether you accept or decline our offer (on April 15th we have to offer the fellowship to another candidate if we have not heard from you). With congratulations and best wishes, we hope you will accept our offer and join us here at the University of Michigan.

Sincerely yours,

Tobin Siebers

Director, Program in Comparative Literature

Dear Lord,

most of the time I don’t understand life, or my place in it, neither. I got thinkin’ thoughts, some times, that think me up in a tree, lookin down, not knowing how I’m gon’to git down from this here tree. I get stuck up here in this tree that ma thoughts take me to, this upside-down, don’t understand nuthin ‘bout life tree, what I’m stuck up in now, lookin’ down, not knowin’ how t’ git home. And Ah thinks to mahself, “ain’t nuthin’ in life but this terrible, lonely tree, and me stuck up in it.” Just me and the moon, most times, so lonely and cold up here wit’ no blankets. We be spendin’ most our time together, lately, just spending our solitude time together up in this tree, thinkin’, wonderin’ how we’s gon t’git down, and, if we gits down, what we goin’ t’do with our lives.

Most things in mah life ain’t perfect. I don’t do nuthin’ perfect, and my momma can attest. I got this job, and sometimes I sleep, when times I ain’t s’posed to be doin’ no sleepin’. I got me a girl, and she’s a real steal, one thing at least been goin’ good in mah life, but I ain’t been seein’ her so much, lately, cuz of spendin’ so much time wit’ the moon. Sometimes I spend so much time, up in mah tree, thinkin’ ’bout mah girl, and life, and what it means to be livin’ life up in this tree, and spendin’ so much time up here all lonesome wit’ the moon, that I be forgettin’ what mah girl even looks like, and I be spendin so much time wit’ the moon, dat I begins to see mah girl’s face in that lonesome face o’ the moon, so dat I even begins to think that the moon be mah girl, and that I never had no girl in the beginning, and that’s it’s always been just me and this moon, up here lonely, thinkin bout life, and what we’d do with it if we wuz t’git down outta here.

Sometimes I been tryin’ t’come down outta mah tree, but thing is, ain’t no place in this world for me, cuz I’m kinda some lonesome kinda guy, wit’ no home or family, even though my momma might hit me upside the head, for sayin’ such. Momma always been real good t’me, always been tryin teach me ‘bout industry, and the ways o’ the world, and getting’ ahead in it. But Ah ain’t done no good thing wit her teachin’s, ‘cept to go back to sleep, and so, “Oh momma.”

Sometimes some things, though, comes up outta this blackness I got inside o’ me. The blackness, I mean, this lonesomeness, and this strange sorta sense that I ain’t kinda nobody but some lonesome kinda guy, wit’ no home or family or nothin’ on this entire earth -- that black lonesome, I mean, that I been tellin’ you ‘bout. Sometimes somethin’ comes up outta that black, like the bubbles poppin’ on some sea-monster liftin' its head to the top o’ the frothy sea, been downstairs underneath for thousands o’ years, or like some flower pushin’ up, up, up outta earth -- some flower kinda which you never seen, but been waitin’ somewhere, black and beautiful and ebony, and outto this world, some kinda strange blossom been waitin’ somewhere under mah surface, gestatin’, bloomin’ its earthy bloom, waitin to push its dark and strange shape up outto the earth since time began, and when it gets up outto there, it’s gonn t'change some things. That’s the kinda thing that sometimes I be feelin be comin’ up outta my black, like the black is some kinda thing that you be sendin’ me, Lord, and I can’t do nothin’ but sit back, in my tree, soakin’ up your strange kinda lonesome sunlight, waitin’ for this strange flower to break it’s way outta me, grown by you, sweet Jesus, that’s gonna change mah world forever.

Sometimes I be thinkin, thinkin, bout the way things are, and I know that this lonesome you send is like some kinda rain from heaven. I’m goin t’soak it up Lord, much as I can, and let that flower bloom, Lord, your sweet gift, that’s gin’t’change the world forever.

THE LORD doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel. He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds. He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names. Great is our Lord, and of great power…

Psalm 147: 2-5

*O, Jerusalem!*

Cry and howl, and howl and cry, O sons of dirt, who spring from the dirt, and live in the dirt, and finally return to the dirt. Thy sin is a jet-black pit before me, and thy blood a brackish ash. My gaunt arms groan with gashes, and cringe with the crash of your glass as I gather your scattered pieces. You are splinters in the embrace of your Maker, and shard in the flesh of your Strong One.

I fed thee; you cursed me; you spat in the face of my servants, and hardened your icy hearts. I spoke to you; you closed your ear; I appeared to you; you shut your eyes; I reached for you, you turned aside your shoulder, shutting yourself. My name was the shame of your scarlet lips.

Murder! Murder! Murder! ye endless specters of Judah! Murder, thou ghosts of the infinite Letter! Murder, thou scavengers of the Sign! who chew and grind, and grind and chew the marrow, of the splintered bones of thy first-borns;

O ye worshippers of Babylon, who devours her children whole; Babylon, thou cold-eyed killer, thou senseless mother, whose womb is an empty catacomb; Babylon, whose name is the dust of the cellar; Babylon, who hardens her dark old heart, that dark old heart the moon; that dark old bulb, both empty and electric; Babylon thou insatiable engine, thou limitless yawning maw; Babylon, thou gasping mouth of maelstrom, thou bottomless, thou gaping grave!

O, ye sons of dirt! who spring from the dirt, and live in the dirt, and finally return to the dirt: your sin is a jet-black pit before me, and your blood a brackish ash; your eyes are a sick miasma, and your razor-teeth are brown with blood; What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? What mean ye that ye tear apart my dear ones, and drink the blood of the broken? What mean ye that ye spit in the face of my simpletons, and laugh behind their backs? What mean ye?

O Jerusalem thou empty skull, thou infinite gaunt Golgotha; how often I would have gathered thee in my empty arms, and washed thee with my endless tears, and bandaged thy dull-yellow bruises; how often I would have held thee; but ye would not. Selah.

O Jerusalem thou wounded, how often I would have gathered thee, like stars from thy bone-white burials; how often I would have digged thee from thy ragged grave of the sky; how often I would have plucked thee from thy ashes, like asphodels from the dirty train-tracks; how often I would have held thee; but ye would not. Selah.

O Jerusalem thou asphodel, whose gray head groans beneath granite sky, and whose dusty arms quake weakly: today I declare, it will not be long: I shall tear thee from thy terrain, and uproot thee, and thy dirt shall be no more;

O Jerusalem thou broken flower: today I declare, it will not be long: I shall pluck thee from thy rocky bed, and redeem thee, and thy dirt shall be transformed; I shall pluck thee from thy dolorous doldrums of dirt, and change thy mud into rivers of living water; I shall press thy ugly petals, with their pale, pink skin, between the pages of my limitless book; and thy name shall be changed to Infinite, and Endless. Selah.

O, thou broken-hearted, who are beaten to pieces day and night; and O, thou cracked-in-half; thou eggshell shards like an infinite, calcium ash;

O, thou citizens of silence, who live in silence, and die in silence, and breath it in like a mantra;

and O, thou hesitant, who hover at the entrance to forever, only to ashamedly turn back, to wander the halls of your unending bedroom, waiting for the night to end (which it never does);

and O, thou forlorn; who bite thy cracked, blue lips in the mouth of the bitter night; and O, thou desolate mothers, who collapse at the knock of thy longing; O! thou shatter-hearted, thou made of an infinite jaggedness; O! thou sorrow-mouthed, who could snap in half at any second;

O, thou weepers over endlessness, who rock in the hallways of thy Bedlam; and O, thou mourners, who hold thy breath in the hurtling dark of Sadness; who have prowled its long, black lanes in the numb hours; who have searched its deepest corners, and found them lacking;

O, thou hearers, who hear the call that calls you beyond yourself, and the shattering Voice at the window; and O, thou deaf, for whom the Voice is a sickly fire, with no heat;

O, ye faces scarred with endless tears! O, ye millions of Christs in the ruff! O, ye countless lost Elijahs, habiting the caverns, of the deserts, of the mindlessness of space and time! and O ye who have wrestled this sad, human skin; and the Lord of Flies in the night; and O! you who tear apart your hapless hair; and O! you bastards of the sky;

and O, you who sing songs at the speed of light, to try and crack the walls of thy pathetic prison, Death; and of thy pathetic flower, Naked Life; in its eternal tender-flesh, exposed to the knife of Midnight;

and O, you who drink bitterness to its dregs; who run thyself through with its daggers; who stagger down the hallways of thy longing; bleary, and disheveled, and drunken; rocking, and weeping, and raving; and starving for a cure;

and O, you who tear the tatt’red sheets from thy back, to stand without warmth in the Barren; who have clothed thyself in ashes, and emptied out thy last pale tears of music, those last white notes of the morning; which rang into the silence like a hopeless spark into the infinite, mindless ocean;

and O! thou beggars of the dirt, who spring from the dirt, and live in the dirt; who stuff thy mouths full of mouthfuls of dirt, finally to return to the dirt; and O, you who stand abruptly in the muddy lips of dirt, in dirt’s dark mouth! who may yet rise in the rose-fire morning: a blinding phoenix of the eternal dirt;

O dreamers! hopers! broken!

mourners! pris’ners! weary!

O! O! O!

O Jerusalem thou asphodel, whose gray head groans beneath granite sky, and whose dusty arms quake weakly: thy god will tear thee from thy terrain, and thy ugly bed of cigarette butts, and of bottles scattered haplessly around the radius of thy halo-wreathed head; and thy impossible smoke-blue hair; and thy thorny crown of longing;

O Jerusalem thou broken flower: thy god will pluck thee from thy rocky bed, and redeem thee; thy god will pluck thee from thy dolorous doldrums of dirt, and change thy mud into rivers of living water; thy god will press thy petals, with their pale, pink skin, between the pages of his limitless book; and change thy name to Infinite and Endless. Thy god will press thy petals into his invisible and pulsing center, where thy heart will pound with His forever. Selah

The Lord will cradle thee in thy brokenness, and gather thee up in thy endless pieces; the Lord will bless and keep thee, and restore all the moments you have lost, which have slipped through thine impotent fingers;

The Lord will be thy redeemer, and redeem thee completely; The Lord will pick thee up from the median, where you, cracked and torn, are lying, stretched out beyond the radius of thy wreckage; The Lord will sing for thee, and redeem thee, and wrap thee up in redemption; the Lord will pay the price for thy trespasses;

The Lord will cover thee, and the sleeve that bears thy blood-red heart; the Lord will cover thee up in thy barrenness, vulnerable and threadbare; the Lord will cover thy bald, old head, that cracks in the winter wind; and thy scarred, uncovered hands, that crack in the bitter winter, and singe in the freezing snow. The Lord will cradle thee in thy brokenness.

O remnant, you left behind in the wreckage; O, thou lost and shattered in the desolate black of Babylon; O, thou seed-shards buried in the shadows at the base of the tower: Pluck thyself from the dirt, O asphodel; pluck thyself from the dirt, thou battered blossom, infinite and glowing; Arise, thou splendorous ashen halo. Awake, thou strange, white creature in the pale remains of morning, and thou amaranthine element! Feed thy flame, thou strain of starlight in the embroiled chords of dawn! And burn with light, thou candle amongst the cacophony of darkness!

you have not yet seen yourself, nor the shape of your latter glory: O happy shapeable matter! O bodily hope transmogrified! O speck of flesh so fragile, and orange-white hope so brilliant! O petal of flame! Ariel, Ariel, O Eternity my lover!

Awake, thou bones; arise! the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments! Shake thyself from the dust, O Jerusalem! and loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion, O prisoner of dust! Awake, O empty-handed! arise, O captives of Canker Babylon; shake off thy dust! Awake, thou bones! Arise!

Burn with light, you Christ! and with unquenchable fire, O precious Name, O Jesus; who have been, like us, unprotected; and broken and threadbare; and bald, unveiled, unconcealed; and defenseless and barren, clothed only in your poor old circumcision; and exposed, and shorn, and stripped; made manifest and naked; finally and once and for all unmasked in your unimpressive glory: be magnified.

Sing, O morning star; O morning star, sing! sing in the ears of Your dear ones, and in the ears of Your numberless children; sing in the ears of Your infinite orphans, whose hearts beat and are broken for the infinite succor of Your touches; sing soft sweetnesses in the

spirits of the seekers; sing soft sweetnesses in the songs of those redeemed; sing, O morning star; O morning star, sing! sing! sing!

Arise, thou heavy-hearted! the Lord illumine thy leaden center with His otherworldly alchemy, until your lifeless metal turn golden!

Golden! you exiles in the earth, who have no country; Golden! you fugitives and outcasts, belonging to none, wanted by none, and received by the lonesome wind; Golden! you interlopers, intruders, outsiders; refugees, aliens, strangers; whose kingdom is Elsewhere; whose name is an infinite longing, and a thirsting after saintliness! who turn back and back and back upon the empty evening, and will not stop short of that eternal country, a city with foundations, whose builder and maker is God;

Blessèd are those in the midst of the night, around whom darkness presses like a thick, black scab; who stab at the infinite shadow with their frail, pathetic candles and, what’s more, win out;

Blessèd! Blessèd! Blessèd! Blessèd thy terrible crown of nails! Blessèd thy blood-stained back! Blessèd thy unbathed glory! Blessèd! Blessèd! Blessèd! Blessèd thy soft-white hair! Blessèd thy infinite laughter! Blessèd thy face in the morning! Blessèd! Blessèd! Blessèd!

Blessèd are the lovers of God, who love with their heart, and their mind, and their strength. Blessèd the seekers of truth, who buy it with blood, and swear, and never sell;

Blessèd are the sons of the Promise, who wait on the promise, who pray for the promise, whose endless expectations ache with the promise;

Blessèd are the sons of God in the earth, in whom loss lives; in whom the long forgotten perpetually breathes: you mourners, in whom these dry bones live, and the valley jumps, and the dawn’s dim hope yet shimmers;

Blessèd those bought back from the brink of Ba’al’s blackish lips! Blessèd those rescued from the ruddy ranks of legion, and those snatched back from the sheer cliffs of Sheol. Blessèd ambassadors from the pit; blessèd penitent diplomats, whose names are Redeemed, and Glory, and Jehovah’s Salvation!

Blessèd your servant, a pillar of flame; and the lion of Judah at daybreak.

Blessèd the broken, in whose shards is your power perfected;

Blessèd the pure, and the empty, and the clean. Blessèd the lowly and meek.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He has anointed me to appoint to them that mourn in Zion, to give them beauty for ashes, and the oil of joy for mourning, to repeal the spirit of heaviness, and grant the garment of praise; so that they might be called trees of righteousness, and the planting of the Lord, that he might be glorified.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; because He has anointed me to preach good tidings to the meek, and to bind up the brokenhearted; to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.

**\***

Dear Lord, I know that You hear me, and that all my prayers are breath to You, the very words You breathe. I know that when I call You hear me, and the inexpressible groaning within me. Dear Lord, if You would clean my lips with a burning brand, heated in the whiteness of Your fire; if You would change me, and make my name Infinite, like Yours…

Dear Lord, I know that you have a plan for my life, and that all Your thoughts toward me are goodness, and hope, and a seed for the future. I know Your tenderness is turned always towards me, and Your lovingkindnesses wait always to lift me up from my rubble. I know, dear Lord, that You will anoint me with boldness, and that fiery breath will spring from the ashes. Bold, bold lion-heart, You have changed my name to Fire. Bold, bold lion-heart, You have changed my name to Flame.

I wait in the shadows of Your wing for a fresh updraft of wind. I wait for Your Spirit’s cooling water. I wait for the emblem of Your sun. You’ve writ Your name in my metal, and stamped Your impress on my seal.

You are able, Lord, to work in this frail flesh, to transform me.

\*

10.27

Late I have come to love you, Beauty so old and new; too late I have come to love you. All along you were inside, while I was trapped without. You were there where I was trying to find you, and in those lovely bodies, made by you, that I threw myself at, unlovely. You were with me, but I was far from you. (They kept me far away, that wouldn't even exist, if they weren't in you.)

But then you called, and you clamored, and you broke through my deafness; and you blazed, and you shimmered, and you chased off my blindness; you gave off a sweet smell, and I drew in a breath; and now I pant for you, and I've tasted, and I hunger and thirst. You touched me, and I'm consumed with flame in your rest.

\*

Not a glimmer of doubt in my made-up mind: I love you, Lord. I loved you from the moment you broke through to my heart with the blast of your Word. \[...\] But what exactly do I love, when I'm in love with you? It's not the allure of a body, not the wonder of passing time. It's not the whiteness - ah! - of light, so pleasing to the eyes, not the honeyed-harmonies of Song in its endless expressions. It's not the sweet smell of petals, or perfume, or spice. It’s not manna, not honey. It's not arms and legs, so ready to wrap their skin together.

It's not these that I love, when I'm in love with my God. But even still, I do love a *sort* of light, a *kind* of song, a *certain* sweet aroma; a *kind* of food, a *certain* aching embrace of the inner man - that place inside my soul where He washes me with the light that no space can receive; and where He sounds out the song that no time takes away; and gives off the sweet smell that wind never scatters; and satisfies with food that feasting never lessens; and wraps me in the arms that satiety never slackens.

That is what I love, when love my God.

\*

*my sun will rise i trust him*

you endless hairy blossoms, ashamed in your awful ugliness, hiding from the sun;

you deformed blue asphodels that in your thirst fear the rain;

you down-bowed blossoms, bowed down to the cracked, blue dirt;

you flowers unguarded in the heat of the harsh white sun;

the pressure of the heat caves in on you;

the pressure of the sun sucks out your air;

o downy blossoms, with your smoke-blue hair:

there is some seed left, some milky hope that remains in your center.

feel it, there, alive in the crushing? feel it, there, alive in the rain?

feel the spark that jumps in the morning? the ache that calls to the rain?

there is some burning strength left. there is some seed of the rain.

there is an asylum in the crushing. there is some strength that remains.

the rain breathes through me, robs my breath;

the storm beats over me and and crushes.

i am a turgid, yellow asphodel, a smoker’s cough of the dirt.

the rain beats down and rages through me; the storm clouds pluck my petals;

the breath of my sickness fills me, blue-brown smoke of sighs:

*i have made this rain. the sun has seen my ugly.*

*the sun has made this rain. i have seen his lovely.*

i look to the east, where my sun comes from.

i press my face into the wind.

i expose myself to the raging rain;

i unfold my chest to its sting.

Selah.

tu es mon père

et les chuchotements dans ma poitrine.

je t’écoute pendant la nuit, quand le jour est parti

puis.

puis tu reviens à moi.

*the drops that redeem in the night* (this is actually an English translation of a poem that I originally wrote in French)

you are my father  
and the whispers in my chest.  
you are the little voice in my heart.  
i listen to you in the night, when the day has gone,  
and time passes by outside,  
and the clouds have fallen with nightfall  
and the whole world is silent, and empty, and pure,  
and i am hungry, and broken, and empty,  
and my life is completely open,  
and the cover is taken off,  
and i am small and feeble before you -  
  
then.  
  
then you take me in your arms.  
then you blossom in me.  
then you fill me with tender light.  
then you wash me with your rain that redeems.  
  
your raindrops come down.  
i press my face to the window  
where outside my room it rains.  
i feel the drops through the glass.  
i feel feeble, and cold, and pure.  
  
you are the little whispers in my chest.  
you are the drops that redeem in the night.

*Beloved*

my heart bursts beneath your brushes;  
when you brush against me my heart bursts.  
i expand in your glances,  
or shrink at your slightest retreat.  
  
you peel apart my deepest layers,  
or cover them up with a word.  
i collapse against your advances,  
or rise up again as you leave.  
  
i come undone at the slightest hint of your pressure.  
  
my masks crumble in front of You;  
and my clothes don't fit.  
my softest parts fold for you, open and close.  
  
you petal by petal collapse me,  
  
like a bright white blossom,  
like teeth of milk / in the rain.  
  
You compress me into an instant.  
  
Selah.  
  
a pale white rain,  
a memory of fire,  
an unadorned longing:  
your deepest breathing shudders through me.  
  
you silence me with your shushings.  
you encompass me with your plaintive hum,  
your voice a tender buzzing.  
  
i drink You up,  
at dawn,  
when the blades of grass cup damp, red drops of You in their creases.  
  
i claw you near to me.  
i drag you into the encasement of my ribcage,  
where You wait.  
  
i breath you in;  
my breath breaks;  
i breath again;  
  
Selah.

Dear Doug,

What address should I write to you at? The one I sent the last letter to, or to Ojibway Correctional Facility? I guess it won’t matter very soon anyways. Please let me know how I can contact you – by writing or phone – when you get out. I hope this letter reaches you before that time.

I know I apologized to you in the last letter, but I really want to sincerely ask for your forgiveness. The scripture I was reading was in Matthew 25 (Jesus speaking):

42 Because I was hungry, and you did not feed me. I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink. 43 I was a stranger, and you did not take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me. 44 Then they will answer him, saying, Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you? 45 Then he’ll answer them, and say, Indeed I say to you, Inasmuch as you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.

Sorry that was so long. I’ve probably read that Scripture three times in the last few years, and every time God’s totally convicted me that I should be keeping in contact with you. So I want you to know that I really wish I had kept in contact with you and helped you while you were in prison, and I hope you can forgive me.

So. No, I’m not hanging out with Andy anymore. I’ve barely talked to him in the last couple of years. I’m married to Carla – I don’t know if you knew that. We got married May 20th of last year, so we just celebrated our 1 year anniversary a couple of months ago. Her son – my son now, too – xxxx, is five going on six. He’ll be going to first grade this year. Also we have great news: we’re expecting a baby girl – xxxx Cassady xxxx – around Thanksgiving of this year. And yes, we live on university housing here at U of M, where I’m working on my PhD in Comparative Literature. I am going into my second year of this five year program. They pay my tuition and a modest stipend – about \$14,000 a year. My first year I was on fellowship – that means I didn’t have to work – but this year I will be starting teaching. I will be a graduate student instructor for a discussion section of a Great Books class. Carla is beautiful and I love her to death. She started a daycare in our home this summer so that she would be able to stay home with xxxx and xxxx and because she can earn quite a bit more money than at a nine to five.

I’m studying Greek, Latin, ancient philosophy, history of philosophy and some other things for my degree. I’ve been thinking about taking a break to get an MFA in poetry here before finishing the PhD, but we’ll have to see. I’m glad to see that you’re still writing, Doug. I miss you. I hope everything is okay. It’s been so long, I know we have to kind of get reacquainted.

We’re still going to Mt. Zion. We drive down most Wednesday nights for the Holy Spirit service, and we’re there on the weekends to visit mom and Stacey and because I still work with the mentally disabled on Fridays and Saturdays. Mom and Stacey are good. They are going through a very difficult time right now, because my dad lost his job and he doesn’t want to pay alimony anymore. It’s bouncing around in the courts, which is always angst-filled, as you know, and my mom knows that she won’t be able to continue payments on the house if there’s any significant reduction in the alimony. So in that sense it’s a very difficult time for her, but in another sense she’s still surrounded by people who care about her, and even in a worst case scenario she will have somewhere to go. She and Stacey are also still coming to Mt. Zion. Stacey just graduated from Mott last year and will be attending Montgomery Kingsley, which is the school for those with disabilities, in the Fall.

How have you been? Has it been rough? Lonely? Boring? Dangerous? I do hope you’ll contact me when you get out, and come get some coffee. God has really given me a new life, and I want to tell you about that and share it with you if I can. I’ll include some poetry and some other stuff.

My heart is just to help you get readjusted, or to be a help to you in any way I can.

\*

*a dream*

in a little clearing in the late afternoon

circled by elms,

an unchanging amber glow – late afternoon –

hanging on the branches,

and beating the blades of grass, dry

from the summer heat:

sparrows.

droves of flightless sparrows hobbling

in the grass.

i was feeding the sparrows,

and there was another person with me – faceless,

or, rather, not faceless, but from whose face

my attention slipped

like glass.

we gave the sparrows seed

and i put a little splint in the wings

of the broken ones.

it was the world’s late afternoon

the world’s orange

calm before winter.

now we’re in a car,

you and i,

along the highway

trees slip past on either side.

it’s later

afternoon now, the clouds are above it’s close

to the world’s dark night

as we pass under the bridge i feel

a violence skip my heart.

and then the rumble,

and a menacing calm

at the horizon’s limit,

where it swallows the road:

a wall of water as tall as the sky

rears above

and now it’s close enough that i see

the flotsam and the metal and the broken

tracts of the broken land swept up by its raging

hunger –

and now i am scared.

i look over at you

(and i realize, now, you’re my father)

and you put your hand

on my chest

to still me,

and you say – so silently,

(but i hear the words all the same) –

that “everything’s

going to be

alright. you don’t

have to be afraid, i’m

with you, son.

i’m with you.”

and then the wave breaks

on our car.

i’m swept away.

then silence.
