I have a terrible secret, a burning confession that I must confess. It is this: I believe. Every word, I believe. I am sick with belief, drunk with belief, *mad* with the thick poison of belief. My whole body burns livid with living belief. I believe really and actually, every word. Every word, every breath, every promise, every slightest utterance of His I believe. Every curve of his face, every ounce of skin, every lamma lamma sabachthani drop of blood, I believe. Real, real, real – my whole life suffused with real. It pierces apart my ribcage and straddles my hungry heart.

Your name is pierced in my silent heart,

where the laces unwrap,

And my face is slack.

Your silent fingers feel in the folds of my scars.

There is one man who makes me break,

And whose hands wrap around my heart while it quakes,

And whose fingers flame, and whose mouth is a coal,

And whose fingers touch my very soul.

Who are you, Lord, and why is your face so black?

Who are you, Lord, and why do you touch me like that?

I burn to be with you, where nothing changes anymore,

And the voice of your eternal sound is an endless roar,

And my mind unclasps, in a trickle of flame,

And I finally learn to pronounce your name.

Selah, selah, selah. The Lord is a consuming flame.

iii\.

Dear Words,

Will you come to me again? Will you change my mind to mindlessness and break me apart in my pieces? Will you fill me up with your bitterness so sweet it nearly bruises?

Only after I have wrestled with poetry, and maimed it, and left it with a dent in its jaw--then, it will return to me, when I have broken it to the ground.

O, for a pure language, one that bleeds from the mouth;

(To have spoken in Your tongue, and then descend to this fragile utterance,

Breaks me, and maims me, and swallows me whole.)

Move apart, my flowers; I’m afraid of His empty face. (My five frenzied flowers: the frenzied flower of battered mind, the frenzied flower of utter desperation; the frenzied flower of the restless natterer and tier of knots; the frenzied flower of the Musselmann and the mute; the frenzied flower of the stained white staircase and the trembling soul; the frenzied flower of the One, and the Multiple, and the Infinite and Nonexistent; the frenzied flower in mute mouth marked in madness)

Burn black breakers against that stretch of shore where I reach to reach you.

Dear meek speech on my speechless tongue,

Burst me, break me, find me again!

Home again, my darlings:

> tonight we shall reach the Father.

Home again, my dear ones:

> today we shall taste of the Promised Land.

Go in, young man, to the fiery clasp of the morning.

Go in to the heated heart of your eternal longing.

Go in, young man, where the breast bone breaks apart.

Go in to the fiery engines of the heart.

Poetry rips me apart again, in a destruction I’ve been praying for, for pardon;

That I would break apart in a million shards of mind,

And infinite thought, and the pale white wool of the Word;

That I’d be stripped apart by its dreadful mutters, and sucked apart by its tongue;

That my mind would bleed with Song the O the thoughtless lamb O Poetry!

Where red things walk, and apprehension quickens,

And mother punches holes in milkman.

Dear Love,

I am lonely. I miss you; I miss xxxx. I miss my mom and my sister. I miss my dog and I’ve been reading too much Nietzsche: Nietzsche is hopelessly lonely and he makes me lonely too. I don’t feel like reading anything. All the readings, that yesterday were exciting and full of life and promise and hope, are now bland and gray and pointless. I feel like reading a novel, but I know that I would just be deepening my loneliness to spend my day on recreational reading. So not even that thought offers any solace. I want to read nothing, write nothing. But I do miss you and I wish you were here. I am sorry for the way I treated you yesterday. I am sorry for pushing you away: honey, I want you here. I need you and miss you, and want to do what I have to do to love you and help you open up to me. Did you know that I feel loneliest when we’re together but apart? I think I feel most lonely now because I know that even when we’ll be together tonight we’ll still be apart. And so my whole life is lonely. I feel sad and hopeless. A little ache pinches my middle when I think about it. I feel incredibly sad that xxxx has to go to a daycare with someone who doesn’t even love him and can’t possibly provide the same thing that his family can. I feel like we’re just handing him off. I feel like I want to go get him so that he can be here.

I haven’t called my mom. My loneliness is running out of steam: even that doesn’t hold any appeal.

I feel very sad about Bob. It seems like Ending is everywhere; I don’t want it to swallow me up.

What happened, honey? Why can’t we have the kind of home life that we want? I have such high hopes for the kind of help we could be for each other, and it breaks my heart to see that hope falling apart in the day-to-day. Honey, we are meant to be a team together and an aid to achieving our purpose. We’re meant to build each other up in the Lord but all we do is tear each other down. I am bitter and pissed off. I know that we can do better. But how? Is it your fault? Mine? I want to do better.

So here’s this stupid letter that you won’t even like and all I want you to do is love me.

I am sorry that I used my words to speak death to you. I know that I can’t take those things back, and that it has an effect that can’t be erased so easily. You are loved and cherished, and I’m sorry I used my frustration as an excuse to blurt off deathful things. I want you to have an opportunity to change and I know it makes it harder for you when I lock you into the same place with my words. I want to give you the freedom to change, and I know that you do change and you have changed and I’m sorry for not giving you the benefit of the doubt and using my frustration as an excuse to tear you down. I do you a disservice when I say “always” and “never” instead of focusing on specifics and when I come to you in anger or as a reaction rather than as a loving encourager to change. I know that this makes conflict harder for you than it has to be. I know that you would be more willing to receive what I had to say if I could approach you at the right time and in the right way. I do want you to be open to receive what I have to say. I feel very frustrated when I do not think what I say matters to you or when I feel like I shouldn’t even bother talking to you about something because you’re just going to shoot it down or take it personally or turn it into an attack or something like that. I am more likely to approach you in frustration and anger when I feel like you won’t receive it anyways, because then I am mad because I feel like you *should* be willing to receive it and that that’s only fair, because I am willing to receive your corrections. So we are caught in a circle and one of us is going to have to grow up and go first and then the other one is going to have to follow and that is the only way things are going to get better.

It is so hard to work through conflict when I don’t know what kind of emotional state you’re going to be in: if you are OK and secure we can normally work through something. If you are feeling insecure and having a hard time emotionally it is nearly impossible. So I approach you emotionally and whinily and that just starts the whole thing over again. And so one of us is going to have to be willing to go first and make the choice to be loving and respectful no matter what. That is a big task, as you well know. There is no working together until one of us is committed to that no matter what. Can God work that in me? First he would have to clear away my bitterness and anger, next he would have to strengthen me with gentleness. (He would have to strengthen me with a certain type of weakness.) Then He would have to turn my words into words of life, and teach me how to set boundaries about respectful and constructive conflict without being a jerk to you. He would have to teach me how to know who I am and be able to love you whether you were respectful to me or not. And He would have to teach me to change the way that I think about you, so that my thoughts aren’t a constant litany of “She doesn’t love me, she doesn’t respect me, she doesn’t even care about me.” He would have to teach me what it means to be a man and to be strong without destroying, and how to be sure without trampling.

So that is a big order.

\*\*

beginning’s end is the breath of something Other; something Other’s nothingness penetrates the veil of morning violets; the veil of morning violets is a scrim on the skin of morning; the wholly violet morning hangs its long, pale scrim across the back of the horizon; the pale horizon passes back its hands to cover its pale, yellow violets; pale, yellow violets blossom in the stand of the morning; in the roadside stand of morning they are selling yellow violets; red blossoms bloom in the screaming scrim of time; time stands scrim in its still life portraiture of the blossom’s bones; the blossom’s bones become unbuttoned in the morning’s oblique phosphorescence; gondola grins like a gray gristle of goat games, the gist of this is the golden gyre of jam; jam’s golden gyre is goat-like and guttural.

the wholly violet song stands still-like in the ephemeral scrim of time; a clearing in the winter sings a strain of sand, a long black beach of ground-up bones in the scrim of winter; winter water cascades across beaten metal; my heart is an African violet made of bones and pale glass and an emblem; in an empty black-white structure, someone sings songs of architecture; someone sings songs of architecture in a pale white, burning structure. he comes and goes; he sings of archipelagoes.

someone stands in his room, the last before the infinite, and beats his chest as he stares down the stairs and clutches at his manuscripts; someone clutches his guns to his lips and stutters at the infinite, your lips; someone stutters at the infinite and clutches his guns to his lips; someone clutches at his manuscripts and stares down the stairs at his elephants; his blossoms are the last before your lips; his violets are the last before the infinite;

Dear Rich, I stand before you, not as sheep to his shepherd, but as a man, stripped of titles, stands before his equally titleless debtor. I stand before you as a man broken by the burden of life-giving gratitude. I am allowed this, because I know you forgive all debts, like your father. I come before you more like a son before his father, although I know you are but a shadow of my sublime father. One day we will stand on the final sands of the shores of Matter, hung, between the unseen ineffable abyss of the ocean of our Father’s infinitude, and the moldering and fragile cloth of this all too tired earthy substance; with the strands of this world behind us, whipping about on the horizon before the endlessness of space, in frenzied tatters, sucked forth by the ravenous and vacuum winds of the World-To-Come; and we will stare, unashamedly, into the eyes of our sweet Jesus, emblazoned white and silvery, full of fire and bombs and the end-of-all-imperfect-love laughing like a sweet infernal dove in the depths of the nuclear majesty of his endless and heatless explosions; and finally be free!

In that day, our heart’s deepest longings, and even those longings which surpass our hearts (because man is a fickle and fading creature, hardly able to lift his eyes to even the fullness of desire - he knows only that he feels desire, and not what will fulfill that pitiful longing); shall be personified, and we will no longer *hear* the music, and long to be mixed with it, and fill the dull and achesome sting of that loss that comes, when the harpings fade; no, we will no longer *hear* the music, we shall *become* the music; we shall mix with it for that one impossible second, never quite reached in *this* place, that will in that place stretch, impossible yet, for an eternity. We shall be one with our Creator, yet distinct from him as carven individual figures of his singular majesty. A multitude of us, all reflecting the light of *His* light.

keep in mind,

when your loneliness falls upon you

like an unlooked for wave,

and your hunger like the weight of the planet:

there is a time for loneliness,

and a season for being smothered in the weight of your dirt

and a place for being buried alive in your hunger and your hurt.

there is a season for hunger that doesn’t want food,

but only emptiness

and a fasting.

don’t fill your hunger without thinking

just because it visits:

i’m serious,

there is a time for hunger, and a season for rain,

a time for being smothered in the ocean waves.

the worm weaves for itself a house of silence

where it does its quiet work

of transformation.

so you, my dear ones, will be shaped by your season of hunger

and your time of silent want. your hunger is your house of silence

and your loneliness your worm.

would you be fat in your endless fullness?

fine then: fill it each time it asks you.

delight yourself in fatness

and quickly fill your silences

with chatter and with faces.

when loneliness stands on your midnight threshold

turn it aside to the world’s dark winter;

forget its empty face.

content yourself with fullness and with chatter.

does your loneliness need you?

*you* need your loneliness,

but your loneliness does without.

it is by nature solitary.

and does your loneliness lack voices?

or your hunger any food?

the smallest voices reign in silence

and the least crumb satisfies when hungry.

there is no silence, here, but a whisper.

there is no hunger, here, but a crumb.

your loneliness is the cloak of your whisper,

and your hunger is the clue to your crumb.

so don’t always turn aside your hunger,

or your loneliness to the night:

there is a secret there in her silences.

when she comes to you without warning,

pale on your porch and disheveled,

invite her in without question.

i’m serious: if she turns to go too soon

catch her arm with a wish

and ask her to stay for the weekend.

your loneliness won’t always be with you—

—she leaves too soon—

so bid her stay for a time at your table.

your loneliness is not so strange to you,

not some stranger to turn away.

so don’t turn her away!

your loneliness is your brother and friend! your loneliness is your sister!

your loneliness is just for a season.

it comes just once or twice

and when its time has passed it won’t return.

so entertain it in its time:

let your hunger be seasoning to your season of fullness,

and your aloneness salt to your season of friends.

there is a time for being smothered in the depths of the sea,

and for gasping beneath its water:

even then, in the season of crushing,

a little light remains,

and a glimmer from the surface.

even then, in the season of hunger

there is a little crumb left.

does your loneliness lack voices?

or your hunger any food?

the smallest voices reign in silence

and the least crumb satisfies when hungry.

there is no silence, here, but a whisper.

there is no hunger, here, but a crumb.

your loneliness is the *cloak* of your whisper,

and your hunger the *clue* to your crumb.

even a little candle drives out darkness,

and a little match shows the path at midnight.

your loneliness is but for a season,

indeed, your hunger for a weekend.

birdsong breaks with the dawn  
and your joy with the morning-bird’s warble.

you need your midnight,

because your birdsong is just junk without its ghost,

or the specter of your loneliness,

or the phantom of your shadows.

your birdsong is your butterfly

and your loneliness the shell of your dawn:

its womb warms the waking world-tops,

and your warble-wind fills the firmament.

birdsong is the blood of the robin:

it bares its bright-red throat

it bleeds its song of becoming,

it dies its warble of waking:

every time its warble wakes its blood beats out, a steady pulse:

an echo is left, my dear ones,

your ghosts will live in the folds of your dawn,

and your song be the shade of your noonday.

*psalm 1*

how long, o lord, will I shake with indecision?

how long, o lord, will my wet skin crawl with shingles?

how long will my eyelight stain and shutter?

how long will my mewly-mind mutter? and my senses bleat?

how long, o lord, will i be blue to you in a snow bank?

how long will my paper lips rasp against strangeness?

or my brittle pulse beat in fits and stutters?

Selah.

the Wolf came to cuddle your darlings:

his teeth caressed the feet of your dear ones

and closed around the throats of your lambs.

but you broke the teeth of the lion, lord.

the young wolf you ripped to tiny pieces,

the hyena you reduced to a pith.

you carry home all your scattered

and your darlings are not so distant.

i will sing with the lips of the happy,

and shout with the crash of the throng:

my god is a flame that remembers his ashes,

and redeems all his embers at dawn.

i will rise with the morning

and shake off the night with its longing.

he washes the mud from my blood-laced feet.

has there ever been one like my father?

has there ever been another beside him?

his face shines softly on those who seek him.

his Voice is a life-gushing river.

Selah.

Unfortunately, the record stops there. Lauren returned these letters in the mail after ending the relationship (as an act of benediction and a favor, not out of spite). I began typing them in 2002 shortly after I got clean; I was trying to sort through the last few years. I had no idea who I was. I got very quickly to the point you see now, but could go no further. The project began to drag. It was an incredible burden to continue. I was not yet ready to look myself in the face. Especially as the record neared those crucial moments when my world finally shattered fully, it was unbearable to be face to face with my own selfishness and lunacy, my own mad cycle of death and sin. There was too much sadness still.

Much later, the project still untouched (although plans continued to soar), I threw out the letters, the box, the drawings—the whole shot. Probably 1/3 of the letters remained to be typed, and there were a number of drawings, photographs, pictures, and postcards that I had before planned to include as part of this notebook. The letters that did not get typed were those that covered the most crucial—the saddest and most eventful—months. I know why I did it, but I will not say. Only that at the time it was important: my life was moving on. My reasons for regretting it now are not the same as my reasons for throwing it out then. But I sympathize with my then-self. Those reasons were important and I respect them.

So there is an indelible blackout at the most crucial point of the narrative, at the event-nexus of my life. And that is fitting: we see and hear nothing between Abraham binding Isaac and the moment he lifted the knife, ready to fall. Those words, or even those silences, deserve, by all rights, chapters. Yet there is nothing. Perhaps then in the same tradition this central void sanctifies my narrative. It is the structuring absence, the unrepresentable something at my core that makes my life holy. It is the unspeakable redeeming-thing that lends its little sublime glow to this work.

I will say this, only briefly: life continued much as it had. I spiraled deeper. I visited New Orleans. There was a shattering falling-out (it was shattering for me; she may not have even known). We continued to write and pretend although everything had been broken. I sunk deeper in my depression and madness. I began getting into car accidents and having near-miss encounters with the law. One in particular near the end of winter I think had an especial effect on Lauren: I passed out at the wheel, Andy sleeping beside me, and ran into a fire hydrant. It was not long before Lauren called to say that she thought we should quit. Our relationship was already little more then an empty outline, but I was devastated nonetheless. It was the emblem of my aloneness.

Now I felt I had nothing left. I continued to write some letters, but they were both elliptical and filled with resentment and anger. These too fell off. The drugs got much worse. I began experimenting with the needle, I found my friend heroin. This all happened very quickly. By September of 2002 (less than a year from where these letters break off) my cycle had intensified to a frantic peak and then finally ended in a visit to rehab. I only needed one. Counseling at the local church and a some-month process of conversion preceded it. One night I accepted Jesus: I said out loud that I needed Him; I declared myself a Christian in front of my peers. Within two months I was clean, but working through an incredible wreckage of the past. This is where the record picks up again, but in the form of poems and scribblings, and in particular with one long poetic project which began in the Winter semester. Over the course of two years and infinite revisions and mutations, I quit working on it. It is as follows, perhaps I will finish it one day. To the best of my estimation, it is the most direct descendant of the self-narrative that begins in the above letters, although in more explicitly creative form.

Since the letters to L diminished and trailed off somewhere between the months of April and September (although even then there was an occasional email), I suppose there would have been a fundamental void even if I had not thrown out the box of letters, especially at

those crucial moments, maybe the month or two of vital (mortifying) activity. I was not writing much. I was numbed and stunned out of expression. So the void remains. Again, this is appropriate. I will sort through my papers, and fill in the period between the end of these letters (December 2001) and rehab (September 2002) as best as I can, followed by the first and following drafts of the Rebekah project, miscellany, and letters to my beautiful Carla.

M

You are in the middle of your long apprenticeship to reading. It is your best instruction in writing. And I grant you, what you say is true – you may not yet be ready to write. Your apprenticeship is long and you are still clumsy. There is too much that you do not know, too much you have not read. Your ignorance assaults you every time you think, every time you put your pen to paper. On what grounds can you speak? With what weight of authority?

But for all of that, you cannot neglect your training in writing by daily practice. So what if you are not ready to write, and your fingers are clumsy, and your mind is adrift without the buoyant assurance of tradition? So what if you are the new kid – a stranger and an alien? So what if you are the bastard son of your unknown father, Books? To neglect your writing would not be humility. It would be utter laziness.

# xxii. the pressure of the sun

lord,

i am broken in half by this battle. is this where i will stay forever? i have let you down. i have failed. i cannot do better. i am spent. here’s where i break in half. here’s where i fall apart in pieces.

father,

when will you pick me up? when will you finally put me back together for good? when can i see you face to face? when can i be like you? i am so tired of the same tired words and the same tired life without meaning. i’ve even been considering using. i mean really considering it – planning it out. not just using, but a full scale submersion – to lose myself again in that madness, to let it swallow me up like a wave of forgetfulness. why can i not get through this mess? why must i make the same mistakes time and again? i do not think i can stand the sting of it.

fight for

i\.

Dear so-and-so,

I feel so bleak and hopeless and lost. I’m in a desert. Every time I try to break out of this repetitive and useless cycle I just get sucked back in. I need your help, God. I don’t know how I got trapped in this cycle in the first place. I want to blame it on marriage and the responsibilities of taking care of xxxx and having a home, etc. And that may be, but there’s no place to dig in from but right here, and it’s too much for me. I know that time is slipping by, and I’m making little to no progress. I see no way out.

I feel paralyzed. I need purpose and direction. Most of all I need fidelity to a purpose, fidelity to a vision, the strength to break the terrible inertia that holds me stuck, that breaks me right before the crest of the hill, so that at the crucial moment my spirit snaps and I crash back earthward to the hole I came from. I need a miracle. I need the Breath of Life to blow across me. I need a savior and a saint.

And there’s a hopelessness that He won’t even come. I’ve called out so many times and I feel like He hasn’t heard me. God, my God, where is Your face? Where is Your holy face? I’ve tried everything – I’ve strained my own will until it’s strained and panting and worthless, I’ve waited for You to move, I’ve waited knowing that only You could do the work, *only You* could make the difference – I’ve waited on You. You said that those who wait on You would rise up as on eagle’s wings. Well God, my God, where is my renewal? I have waited, I have waited on You, and *I am stuck here in this same valley*. I’ve trusted in You, my God. Where is Your saving hand? Lord, You *promised* that those who wait on You would rise up as on eagle’s wings. You promised that there would be a second wind. I’m here for Your purpose, Lord, not mine. I’m here for what You’ve called me to from the foundations of the earth. I’m here for Your good works. I’m striving with everything I am.

WHERE ARE YOU!?!?

I’m going to church, I’m reading Your word, I’m seeking You in prayer, I’m fellowshipping with Your stupid people; so *what is wrong with me?!* Lord, I need You to move in me, and I really mean this. I absolutely need You to work Your change in me. I’m being changed; I need You, Lord with everything I am I need You, to change to work Your transformation. I want to be transfigured, I want to be weightless and worthy. Come touch me, Lord, come change me, make me like You.

I have waited for my God

in the valley

for forty years

or forever.

I have sought his face.

I have longed to look on His beauty.

Who are You, Lord?

Come show me again Your face.

Let me see Your beauty.

Let me trade my ashes in.

If I could only look at You,

If I could catch a glimpse of Your face in the distance –

that would be enough.

That would satisfy me forever,

just a taste of Your holy face.

If I could be with You, Lord,

if I could be with You.

Come wash me, move me, make me –

come make me like You again.

that’s what i said to the man behind the counter as he slowly counted back my change. I said to the man behind the counter, “that’s enough of that nonsense, Momo, just gimme the change before I go nuts in this mother.” And that’s when he turned to me with his sad brown eyes that stared out from above his sad brown vest that stopped well above the cuffs of his worn white sleeves that opened out around his sad brown hands that wearily polished mugs all the day before hanging them back above the bar. He looked at me with those sad brown eyes and said to me squarely, “I need another dollar, man, before I can get this videogame to work.” And he pointed to this old black, beat-up, eighties-era arcade machine at the other end of the shop that had been sitting in the corner for God knows how long, collecting dust.

I took out my last dollar and gave it to the man, whose burning eyes spoke of power and life and cash, and that’s when the radio blared Elvis, and the white horse was free, and a man named Jim grabbed my hand and said, “Son, we’ve gotta get outta here quick, before the walls come down,” and then we hopped in his seventies-era car and we were outta there.

It was whack.

So how was your day?

You don't think it had an effect? I thought that there was a general curiosity in the room. Combined with distaste, yes. But a curiosity. I interpreted the willingness to listen to something new as a degree of openness. Forgive me for dropping into lingo ("Word").

I am not talking about the level of the intellect, of an intellectual acceptance or rejection of a statement, or anything like that. But I interpreted the curiosity as being a reaction to - at least in part - novelty.

Just to respond to one aspect, and leave the rest untouched (for the moment): At the intellectual level, I don't feel that I was doing a "Christian" reading of D + G - just a reading. I had had no intention of using the passage from Corinthians to speak about what it meant to me personally, but to tie it in to D + G on artistic creation. In the same way that the artist goes on a passage through the finite that records or preserves the infinite, Paul presents love as the record or marker of the infinite (that which is perfect) within the finite (the present, partial state). It is a monument contained in a few marks, a few lines. Now, clearly, Paul did not mean this in the sense that D + G mean it, when talking about artistic creation. And I would not have insisted on the Pauline sense, in my reading. It was a link between the lover and the artist, between love and the artistic creation. You asked me to go into the Pauline sense. I did not offer that. In fact, I have never in that class brought up a conversation about religion, God, or anything along those lines. In a way I don't feel the classroom is the place.

So at the end of the day, I am absolutely clueless as to what was "Christian" about my reading until I was specifically asked to talk about my faith. Perhaps it is so obvious that I can't see it. Really - I have zero clue what might have been counted as Christian in the (disorganized) way I was trying to approach WCW. I have zero clue in what sense I "Christianized" D + G. If you can help me with that, then by all means do.

I tried to share what I thought was actually going on in the classroom's reaction with Yago when I was talking about a table. If there is a table with two sides - I'm not so sure it has to be that way - but if there is a table, I think there is a double temptation, one for each side. On the transcendent side of the table, sure - there is a temptation to reduce the immanent aspect of D + G's thought, to subordinate it to the transcendent. To hear only "eternal" when they speak about an eternity coexistent with a moment, and leave behind the moment. To hear only "being" when they speak about the being of becoming.

But the same temptation is true for the immanent side of the table. What I felt was going on in class - purely at the intellectual level - is that there was a very deep resistance to allowing the other side of the conundrum, to let the paradox exist in the full tension of its complexity. To hear only "moment" in an eternity coexistent with a moment, to hear only "becoming" when they speak about the being of becoming. I certainly was not trying to reduce D + G to an eternity, to a being. But I was not willing to reduce it to pure moment - I needed both aspects. And that is the same conceptual tension I was trying to find in WCW.

So why do I consistently get the reaction as if I were reducing the complexity of their thought to one edge of the paradox? What I was trying to say to Yago was that, if what I am doing is a leveling, then the same charge can be leveled at what you're doing. I am willing to allow D + G their complexity, but let me focus on the aspect that is valuable to me. It's there in the text. There are multitudes there in their text. So why try to squeeze out the eternity from the moment, or the being from the becoming? I am not trying to make anyone get rid of their moment or their becoming - but both are there in D + G.

I felt that a part of the class's reaction, at least in the WCW phase of the presentation, was an unwillingness to allow D + G the complexity of their thought - trying to squeeze out the eternity from their moment. I was not trying to squeeze the moment out of their eternity, in terms of my reading of them - although, if pressed I will admit that I \<i\>personally\</i\> do not see it that way. I felt that, because it's clear that I have personal stakes in this - who doesn't?

You think it's a show of good will, but really you know what I have to offer. There's no way you can hear truth and not have a little bell ring in the back of your head. You asked me to go there - that was not the basis of my reading of D + G.

Dear Yago,

I feel that in general I have been struggling a great deal this semester. I have kept up with the readings, except for the second part of Anti-Oedipus, during which I was completing a paper, and the last couple of weeks of class, during which my wife and I were bringing a baby into the world. When I came to graduate school, I truly felt that I had something special to bring to the world of thought. I had a sense of purpose and direction, and a vision for the kind of scholar I would like to become. I feel that, since I have come to the University of Michigan, I have lost that sense of purpose. My sense of meaning in life had previously come from my spiritual walk – even my academic life flowed from an intimate relationship with God. I completed papers with zeal and enthusiasm, because I felt that I was called to pursue a PhD to make a difference in academia. Since coming to graduate school, I have doubted whether I have anything of worth to contribute to scholarly pursuit, here or elsewhere. I have been struggling with temptation concerning drug use and alcohol abuse in a way that I have not struggled since I was nineteen. God delivered me from heroin addiction and a life of chemical and alcohol dependence at that age. I have before struggled with desires to use or drink, but had never before fallen down until last summer. Last summer, preparing for teaching and trying to finish a late paper, I began to drink in secret. I feel isolated in my spiritual walk, cut off from my home church, and, in general, lonely. I do not know where to turn. I felt when I came here that my relationship with God would be enough to see me through this journey. I have let my spiritual life and my commitment to God fall by the wayside. I have allowed myself to become overwhelmed with fears, impossible responsibilities, and isolation. I have begun smoking again, after several years of abstinence. I have fallen in a major way. I feel that I have let down both God and my family. I have struggled completing papers and other academic assignments. I am filled with fears and self-doubt. I share this with you because you present yourself as a compassionate person, and I hope that a part of your motivation in the self-evaluative process is this kind of honesty. Mostly I just need someone to reach out to.

Since coming to grad school, I have struggled with being a minority. I have never met another born-again, Spirit-filled, Bible-believing, conservative Christian in the humanities, ever. I’m all of that. I am the religious right – I feel like the primary object of academic and criticism and scorn. I understand that only a part of the problem is the reality of the environment I am in, and that the majority stems from my own personal hang-ups and insecurities. Nevertheless, it is a difficult road. I need people to reach out to who are more compassionate at the level of human beings, first, and at the level of politics, second. I need people who care more about my status as a human being than about my political or religious beliefs. There are people like this, and they are probably less rare than my personal insecurities allow me to see. I believe that you are one of those people. You present yourself as compassionate and caring. Last semester, after you realized that I was a Christian, I really did sense a difference in terms of your classroom demeanor when dealing with sensitive issues. Perhaps this is just a product of my own imagination, desperate to see what it wants. But I don’t think so. I really do feel that you have exercised a certain sensitivity to the fact that there is a diversity of perspectives and viewpoints in the classroom, and that all those viewpoints, even my own, have a right to be there. This is precious to me because I have experienced so little of it in my academic career. I appreciate it more than you know. Although I have known, at an intellectual level, that differences of opinions on even sensitive issues does not have to create a wedge of separation between myself and others, I feel that I have continued to struggle with it emotionally and spiritually. It really is not a healthy – or even a Christian – mindset. It has contributed to my isolation and has put separation between myself and people who might be able to help.

So this is where I am at. It is not where I want to stay. My wife and my children need someone who has it together, but at the moment I am not together. I feel like I’m cracking apart. I cannot live two lives, but I have been struggling in a very real way. Mostly, I have been struggling with the idea that I am no longer living life for myself. Everything I do now has an effect on Carla, on xxxx, on xxxx. They need someone who can help them – they need someone who can be strong for them. I feel so very weak. I know that when I stand before God the first thing He will ask me is, “What did you do with your marriage?” It is the most important relationship in my life. Part of my responsibility does include – as much as I struggle with it – completing my responsibilities here at school, being there at home, balancing what seems like an impossible load. As much as this breaks me apart, I do not want to tell Him, when I stand in front of Him, that I screwed up my marriage, that I could not be there for her, or my kids, or even for the people here at school who need to see a person who really follows God, who knows His love and can share it. There are people here who need to see what God can do in a life. I can’t show that if I’m broken. I can’t do that if I’m turning back. I want so much, at the end of the day, to be able to tell Him, “Despite my failings, I fought with everything I have of this sad human skin to love her in the way that You love me. I was there for her. I was there for my kids. I was a demonstration of You at my workplace. I did what you called me to do at school and in life.”

I do not know if this kind of honesty makes a difference, or if you will hear it. Despite all the ways in which I am failing, I know that God can pick me up, if I call on Him. Despite all the ways I fall short, I still want people to see how good He is. He’s saved my life, He’s shown me what it means to love. That’s everything that matters.

It’s right here in my weakness that he can be my strength. I am writing at least half of this to myself. I needed to write to you to work some things through for myself.

If this is too honest please pretend you never read it.

Yours sincerely,

Matt

Yago, I just don’t know how to write this evaluation. After several attempts, I’ve decided that writing the real self-evaluation, the self evaluation that matters, is impossible. In one sense, you are perfectly aware of one of the major struggles I have had, this semester and last. In one sense that struggle is as clear as day, perhaps more to others than to myself. Our blind spots wouldn’t be blind spots if we could see them. If I could formulate it in writing, or even inside my head, it would no longer be a blind spot. If I could work through this dilemma set in front of me – if I could lay it out on the page – maybe in an outline, a chart, a well-constructed essay with tight transitions and footnotes[^1] – that would solve many problems. But somehow I don’t see that working. Here are some reasons why:

- formulating the problem means not only evaluating myself, but expressing it in a way that will register within the evaluative framework you’ve already developed

- formulating the problem means having a clear grasp of external perspectives concerning it, which I don’t have

- formulating the problem would be in some sense grappling with those same perspectives, difficult when I don’t understand them

- formulating the problem would be in some sense communicating my own perspective to those other perspectives, difficult when I have been unable to do that.

So in short, the note on which this evaluation begins is one of failure. It has failed from the beginning. It never began. The only way to get through this evaluation is to march under the flag of its failure.

So – on what basis did it already fail? It’s clear to me that the failure is one of communication. I feel that if I could just communicate clearly, there would no longer be a problem. At first, I tried doing an *honest* evaluation. I thought that honesty would certainly make things clear. After setting that failed evaluation aside for a period of time, and rereading it, I realized that it would do anything but make things clear to you. It would probably deepen the dilemma. It did actually help make things clear to me, or if not clear, at least better. There’s a certain therapy to honesty.

I guess I’m dying for more dialogue about what happened in class last Wednesday. I’m dying to understand exactly what happened.

Yago,

After several attempts at writing this evaluation, I have accepted failure. I have several pages of several failed evaluations that I simply can’t give to you, although in a way I wish I could. I can give you a perfunctory evaluation that shies away from the core of the issue. That core I can’t express. Or I could, but I won’t. Or I could, but I’m not willing to open myself up to that kind of rejection. In a sense, I would like more dialogue about certain aspects of classroom discussion. In a sense, I would like more time to really understand different perspectives on what, exactly, happened in class last Wednesday, and at other points, this semester and last. But after several attempts, I’ve found that this evaluation is not the place. I think part of the problem is that I just don’t understand how you’re interpreting what was going on in class. I really don’t understand your perspective – not in terms of politics or religion or anything like that, although I claim no special knowledge of your perspective in that arena, but in terms of what was happening during classroom discussion. I feel that if I understood your perspective a little better, I might be able to express myself and respond to that.

Until then, I can give you the perfunctory evaluation, and leave an invitation to dialogue openly and at length at any point in the future, if that’s what you’d like.

The perfunctory evaluation: I enjoyed the readings, and kept up with them except for the second part of Anti-Oedipus, during which I was completing a late paper, and the last couple of weeks of class, during which we were having a baby. I regret not reading all of *What is Philosophy*, because, of the three, it was turning out to be my favorite. It was far more accessible than the others – not that density is unenjoyable – and had a manifesto-like quality that made for an exciting read. I’d like to finish the reading, and incorporate the material on affect and art into my writing at some point. I struggled participating in classroom discussion many weeks. I have only my perspective and the points of reference that come along with it, and I just don’t have the nerve or endurance to put that on the table, most nights. I wish I had spent a more time organizing the readings for my presentation, but, at the end of the day, I was okay with the way it turned out.

In my personal life, I’ve struggled a great deal this semester. At many points, I have lost my sense of purpose. I have felt overwhelmed by responsibilities and changes at home and at school. I’ve been pretty broken down. For a period of time I started smoking again, after several years of abstinence. I have struggled with defining myself and my role here, and with communicating myself to others. I am anxious about having to commit to a dissertation topic etc. On the plus side I’ve found teaching to be a great joy, although of course it carries its own anxieties.

Thanks for teaching this class. I enjoyed it, and have learned a great deal from you.

Sincerely,

Matt

i stayed behind in an empty spot,

a place crisscrossed with shadow,

in the darkness,

with the stillness

and the river of the sound of leaves,

and the silences,

and the forest’s resonant empties;

and the deafening night

escaped its borders

and muffled my light

and the sound of a heart in my ear;

and yr ghostly fingers rose around me

and as a haze of light you came,

and poured into my deepening pressure

and blazed alive like a fiery nightmare

and my skin piled up with sweat

and a bead of it fell down my face

and a mask of it formed a thin wet film

and an out-of-time thrumming pounded sideways

and my heart’s blue beat escaped its echoes

and thundered up the throat

and crashed at the back of the teeth –

and some stranger’s teeth inside me,

and some stranger’s teeth, the wall of the mouth,

and some wall of the mouth my muzzling silence,

and some wall of the mouth my locked-up tongue;

and like a hit of dope my warmth lit up

and thudded in the backs of my legs,

and pulsed in my stretched-out fingers;

and an arc of flame in my muscles,

and my dental floss tendons alive with heat,

and the arc of my back, a rag of brightness;

and deep inside, a thrum in the sternum,

and a little bell @ the back of the neck,

and rags my rags a body of twine,

and my hands a snarled ribbon;

and there in the night a mist above,

and a palpable presence there inside me,

and yr sun an exploding light,

and yr face a sword in the night,

and yr mouth a word that crushed me –

and in a patch of dirt

where my breath wore thin –

Dear Sally,

you are a poser. take your orange butterflies back to Russia. You Soviets are always in here with your ridiculous butterflies. There is a sign in the doorway with 3-inch lettering that clearly states that only yellow butterflies are welcomed in my place of business.

You Soviets and your butterflies-becomings. The next time I see an orange butterfly, I might go get my gun. And when I get my gun there’s going be a haze of shrapnel. And when the shrapnel hits the back of your throat it’s going be a poem – a loud roaring *gun* of a poem, just like mother Russia.

Hear that? I’m going to get my gun and load it up with intensities-becomings and send these astronauts back to space. When America finds out she’ll be livid. When America finds out she’ll take off her parka.

Dear Sally you are a poser. When my yellow butterfly becomes, things will change in an instant. When my yellow butterfly blazes to life and ricochets off the walls, I think that guy with the microphone is going to make an announcement. And when he makes his announcement all my butterflies will be on sale, because it won’t be just any announcement but a performative speech act: “yellow butterflies on sale, all intensities-becomings free in aisle 6.”

Dear Sally fuck you go fuck yourself I fucking hate you.

Sincerest heartfelts,

President Nixon

the margins are set to three inches so that i will have room to breathe, but not too much. if i keep the writing up at just the right pace – sometimes the speed of light to break the prisons of the margin, to batter against the constrictive straightjacket of page and line and word. will you come to me? the only real shred of writing i have left is a nameless plea to poetry, that she would explode in a haze of shrapnel and rip apart these hapless rags these rags O timeandspace. the only real shred of writing i have is not even that, but only a dispersed and coagulate gel of voice that echoes somewhere in the depths of Stomach – a whirring little tremble of light, a butterfly down there, a catatonic butterfly or an exploding yellow butterfly of being. So there you have it. My poem is an exploding catatonic butterfly of being. That’s more fancy than the orange kind and fancier by far than Sally could hope to come up with. I bet her exploding butterfly is something more like a hiccup – a hiccup-becoming, a hiccup of intensity, an exploding yellow (orange) intensity of hiccupping-becoming. Dear Poetry, my friend Sally asked me to write and see if you could irradiate her yellow butterflies with hiccupping-intensities. Also if you don’t mind she would like to borrow your car this Saturday. Sincerely your pal Matt.

What a strange character I play. Such a stuffy mask I put on! My self – my inmost self – is offensive to you, a nasty secret that I need to hide. He is my passionate lover. Does this make me a whore? Am I a whore to you? Is this dirty and obscene? He is my all in all.

So does this make me a whore, Academy? I could tell you that the relationship is Platonic. Although you wouldn’t like it, you would allow it: something distant, and transcendent, and sterile. You would not like it. But you would turn the other cheek.

But I am not, he is not, we are not –

I love Him so bad, it makes me shake when I think about Him. It makes me shudder and cry. I love Him and He loves me and we love each other more than pumping blood.

(and like a heart, our love is an engine)

But I know you – really deep down you need Him. When I see through your masks... when, for an instant, I see your need – then I love you the way that He loves me. But I know my love is dirty to you, and makes you turn your backs.

father why do people who need You

turn You away?

why do fragile people (whom You love –

with a real love, a love like nothing

else that exists)

keep You out?

why do they close

themselves,

like hairy petals?

don’t they know that You are the god

of small things?

don’t they know

that You are tender?

i break apart with this.

i shatter apart in a wave of rain.

dear god send yr rain.

dear god wash across this world

and make it new.

dear god put together these people.

dear god please gather yr sheep.

dear god please breathe yr breath

out and back

across this grass.

dear god send yr wind on all flesh.

i am empty and spent,

my breath is gone.

my tears poured out for this people.

this is how you feel.

this is yr loneliness in heaven.

this is yr turned aside tenderness.

like a breath of rain i bleed through the pages,

like ink on my fingers i stain.

my breath whooshes out to you,

forth and back.

my whole body trembles

while my lungs pump fast.

my

breath

is

the

blood

of

you.

you are my shameless secret

more dear to me than breath.

when i see through yr masks

then i love you.

but i know that my love

is dirty to you

and makes you turn yr back.

but i know you.

i have been in the emptiness.

i have lived in the ugly valley.

i have paced the night.

i have broken with the evening.

i have spattered apart in sparks of pain.

i have faced the impossible nonsense.

i have lost myself amidst myself.

i have burned apart like fog.

i have felt

in the night

the fragility

of breathing.

i have turned aside from everything

to gain it back

from Him.

(*this* sweetness structures me.

*this* makes me live.

*these* are the breathings / in between me)

*intermezzo*

On the path of life,

in the midst of the way,

I looked aside and strayed,

and found myself at the dismal gates

whose bars are lined with symbols

in Italian, fiery black –

whose mouth is the mouth of

doom, and turning back.

(You who enter, abandon your light.

Leave behind

your depths and heights.)

They were familiar to me,

these gates, as if in a life I’d lived

in dream, they’d risen

from the mists of sleep

to tower above with their glowering

deep.

This fiery prison

somehow I *know.*

(but through these gates,

if they lead to you,

I’ll go,

I’ll go,

I’ll go.)

Perhaps I have addressed your concerns about the rough draft. Certainly I’ve created a entire universe of new concerns and critiques. I’m not sure whether I’ve taken it forward or plunged it into a mire – c’est la vie.

Yours,

Matt

p.s. to respond in greater detail to your comments about my writing style: the repetition, I think, has little to do with the circumstances of writing, and interruptions or lack thereof. I think by writing, and as my thought progresses I accumulate a great deal of written debris. Going back later and sorting through the debris sometimes nears the impossible, and so I have repetitions, rephrasing, etc., as I approach within my own thinking the heart of what I’d like to say. I’m a poet: I produce affect, sensation, image – and so academic writing – the writing of organized thought – is very difficult to accommodate my voice to, hence the schizophrenic weaving of registers and tone. I have only a finger’s hold on scholarly prose. It is far easier for me to write than revise. I would often rather write a new paper than revise an old, and many times in the space of a week or a day or an hour my thoughts have changed to the point where I can no longer write the same paper. The thought of both reassessing my own ideas, expressing them, and then going back and accommodating what I wrote last week to the new form of thought – all before my ideas have time to take new shape and change again – is overwhelming. There is probably still a good deal of repetition in the paper. As a poet, I have a difficult time seeing those parts that are only there because they indicate a shift in register. Affective registers are the air I breathe, and separating them from intellectual content can be difficult.

I would be happy to work with you on projects at some point in the future. You’re not in my field (whatever that is), but you’re comments and suggestions have been practically and theoretically helpful. Thanks.

\_

between channel blasts. Oil barrels

balloon in outer space where the milky way race

is armed for chocolate. Chocolate, I say, I say chocolate,

If all of these words are like a static

drifting softly in and out between my brain,

and the words that come to me an electric ghost –

some specter of the still-breathing circuits –

and yr small, sad dog waits expectant in Salem, impaled

on a weathervane yapping:

If all of this, an electric butterball staying fresh

for a century:

then I can only follow the vacuum.

I can only be true to the trail of the trimmers

that leads me

far and near by a nose ring

out past the bounds of space and the far-circling black

of the final oblique boundary stone:

I can only be true to the machine that beats me to death,

and the gear that’s ascendant in mush,

and the breath of the teeth of the factories,

and the conveyor belt of Assemblage,

and the itinerant chasms of Ish,

and the vertebrate countenance, Frailty,

and the reciprocal tongs of the cairn,

and the abundant baths of the batteries,

and the liquid-like effulgence of throng,

and the ridiculous semblance of maw-mouth,

and the respectable sages of sand,

and the dust-like apparitions of Sideways,

and the flat-level appurtenance, doom,

and the equitable furnace of fanning,

and the burn of the turn of the moon.

leaving off is a subtle pain that

pleases in the beginning of speaking. and one knows

great waves of words that rush inandout at a razor’s

bandwidth, bright bright information oars

slicing down through waves of thought,

down and through the silence –

and one knows the wake of the mind as a subtle bleating,

a raked-out rut in reams

a pale-frail purple cloth

rippled up and up and out

I break away and I stay away.

**father i don’t want to be weak anymore**. i am so tired of falling, of doing the same sad things that let you down. i am tired of deception, i am tired of hiding things from my wife. lord, i want to be like you, whatever that means. father i want to know you, but i don’t want it to hurt. can you change me? can you change what it means to me to be changed? lord, i am so tired of being weak. you overcome. you beat death. you know what it’s like to die, and be weak. i don’t want to go up and down anymore. i don’t want to draw close and then fall away. i don’t want to fall away from you i want to worship you everyday. teach me how to worship you. make me willing to walk in the place of stretching. make me willing to grow. make me willing to reach beyond myself and know you’ll catch me. dear god i don’t want to fail my daughter, my wife, my stepson. does anyone know that i’m not good at this? does anyone know how i’m failing, how i’m falling short? did you make me to draw near and fall away? did you create me to fail? i can’t believe or understand that. and yet i find myself failing and falling away. does that mean i’m living in the world without you? does that mean you don’t guide my life, that you don’t order my steps? i am tired of life, lord. how i long to be with you, where i’m warm in your stillness, where i can see your beauty. god this world is so broken. god it breaks me apart everyday, and i am so tired and broken and drawn far out beyond myself. how i long to be with you, where there are no more tears, and where i see your face, and where you touch me in the secret place. what is the meaning of brokenness? what does death mean? or the murder of little children? could your terrible justice, and your fires that burn forever, ever make that right? how do i make sense of my own broken experience of failure and hurt? does every one of my tears fall into you? do you catch them as they fall? can you wipe them off my cheek? can you heal my brokenness? can you pick me up from my pieces? because all i see are pieces. all i see are the fragments and shreds of a promise that can’t come true. i live in death.

don’t give up on the faith that you have. even that shred – it’s enough to see you through. even a shred – remember, even a tiny little candle cracked the back of death.

remember – a tiny little flame put its foot on the throat of shadows and crushed them in the dirt. hang on hang on hang on. even a little brightness can make it through the night. even a little love can see you through to dawn. i will see you in the morning, you in the night, you in death and you in life, i will raise my hands to you – all the shambles of dreams that leak between my teeth will gleam. you wouldn’t have put this desire in me for your holiness if i couldn’t one day be dissolved in it.

moleskine \#1

gb201 summer 2008?

I cannot write this paper because every sentence screams at me, "This is not the purpose for which you were created." So I tell myself that I will only whore my gifts for another month, another year, another decade, another lifetime--then I will return to my soul. Then I will once more live.

But there is no second chance. Every minute gone is gone forever. You are not a parasite--you are a creator. What the atheist Ayn Rand and the Christian author of *Don't Waste Your Life* share in common is a life of courage. No one understand or *will* understand the gift that sleeps in you. There are none you can follow, for you are the *first* (as is anyone who *lives*). So rather than live, you run. You hide yourself, when soul and being cry like a dying child for water, food, air--and you with deliberate precision slowly submerge its face in the water, and hold it there while the shudders build.

There will be no defense, no forgiveness, for what you do you do knowingly, what you do no murderer has done, because you do it *feeling* every spasm and twitch of horror, each molecule bleating and sobbing with need--you feel all, know all, but will not relent. A face held in the water.

There is no act more bloodthirsty or savage than this waste of my life.

I want to return. If I wrote, it would not be of Rand's perfect Roark, but of Keating. How does the one who has turned aside turn back?

I've whored myself to this cause. I cannot escape, or pay its price, nor do I have it within me to finish.

This Academy is a consortium of cowards who have turned away from their courage to live in the muck as leeches.

Perhaps... knowing this... I could write the trash to which they'd give their approval. If it were somehow completely detached from the leeches--somehow mine, and mine only.

But how?

I need some rite or ritual, some purification to clean away the miasma, to make these ashwords sizzle with blue heat, pure, refined by holy fire.

Because I know this: if it could be pure... the pure is worth my life and calling.

What rite? what magic symbol? what wafer transformed to living flesh?

Something as simple as the hand and pen, something as physical as the notebook--so defiant and brave, the hand's black scrawl. so unlike times new roman.

i will write You with handwords. formed in yr image, like fingers my love will be brave.

and where will you write?

i will write you in the night--when the whole unworthy world is dead, and asleep to Your beauty (as it always is), your brilliant brightness. then i will write, in anonymous shadows. in the dark i'll be noble, and savage, and lonely, and brave. the daytime can have my menial works, my deadwords and ashes and valleys of prose. and the valley will make me lonely. and my thirst for You will grow.

among all the wasting lives in the world--only You will know of our sweetness. only you will know my name in the dark.

quiet and lovely and holy and black.

silent and thirsty and worthy and bright.

\*

i've forgotten what it means to be a poet. i've forgotten why it was important to me.

hadn't you found in poetry a secret? that it was your substance, and vice versa: that you were the substance of poems? the competing pull of outward confirmation + inward being + the moment when the outward sign becomes the essence of the thing, + you lose yr heart and blood?

but you can't turn away from the outward to write "only for yourself," because speech is *ex-*pression, a pressing outward that touches--

i miss you, Lord-- i miss all the beauty You stand for. i miss yr beautiful hair.

to be free.

sleep.

it's advanced to the point that i can accomplish very little. a disease clutches--no--strangles me, anchors me to the couch. i go to work, i sit in the chair for hours and stare--just stare and wrestle with the hollow resonances inside my head. there is no writing, there is no reading, there is no cleaning. there is no purpose, no forward momentum, no goal. i am trapped inside a life that i don't want. what's more--i've been through wisdom and back again, the spiritual veils lifted--i know that no change of place, of job--no financial success, no external change will satisfy. i have none of the receding illusions that comfort the foolish.

8/23/11

The tiny death living

Alive in lungs, the gray waiting

Scrim behind

Saltwater sting in eyes: I scream @ the Lord

Of hosts, a liar:

The mouth + the flame, the sacred

Concubine + bride, the whore: you fucked me sho’;

If I, this tiny mite, have the right

To call the lord to account –

Where yr promises? Where yr soft white fingers? Where yr doves of comfrt? Where yr rod yr staff?

Stripped of you I’m stricken

My cloth-bright grave-cloth ghosts of grace

My once-white linen of holy;

A tongue of flame yr tongue, yr arms a physikal

Stricture, a drop of architincture;

How long will you drown yr dear one, + hold my face

In the mutter? r cast me down in the dreary flames frever?

Figures. Yr characters lovely beloved

sheep yr radiant dear ones

Had their kingdom fr a handful of decades –

In the tumble of thousand years.

Is this what the lord can do? Is it really yr gift of grace?

To leave me strung out here

a disease in my stomach

eating me alive in my prayers?

To let me rot in my desperation?

Or have I not called on you?

Have I not worn yr name before the nations?

Have I not answered yr call,

When others stood aside frm the fires?

Have I not answered the call of yr called out ones

Calling them home from the deepness?

Have I not known you in yr secrecy? Have I not seen yr face and adored you? Have I not broken myself in pieces puling my heart’s petty longing? My desperate anger of need? Have I not waited on you? The lord so high and mighty?

## An Elegy for “Howl”

When the last

forgotten recess

of your ultimate weary

drawer of dust

coughed out the yellow petal

of its one remaining

folded rose,

and the sheet of blood-

smeared paper, stained

with poems like

ink,

gave up its ghost:

i saw nothing.

There was nothing to see.

The best minds of my generation expired while little more than seeds.

you did not see.

you were not seen.

Poker-faced hysteria starved in silence

and exhausted itself in lame dysfunction

to be pinned insensate to a cluster of symptoms

as a matter of course

by moth-dust fingers of DSM lepidopterists

in formaldehyde rooms of science.

i heard nothing.

There was nothing to hear.

The eli eli lamma lamma sabachthani cry was drowned in words.

you did not hear.

you were not heard.

Jaded sincerity choked on its tongue

and shook with neural crescendo of seizure,

in pig shit halls of knowledge.

there was no mouth to take the sigh

and the final rattle passed

unremarked.

in final hope asphyxia brain

set down its speechless fury

the last pale spark of fire as

a footnote

either to suffocate

or burn, perhaps,

in time that’s yet to come.

you were not saved.

there was no savior

you do not preserve

the salt lost its savor.

The absolute heart of the poem of life was butchered, but soon spoiled.

The poem of life resolved as a joke

of lambs of bodies brutalized

by despair and dope

and inert and septic nectars spilled

on ground in vain libation,

or on altars thick with fire burned

but could not rise

as smoke.

a memorial

for ‘howl’

a beautiful lie

but fragile.

\*

## Why did I leave you?

Why did I shut myself,

and bury

every remembrance?

father, something must be wrong, because these words do not

come out. I know I cannot remember, I know it is my nature

to destroy the memory of the truth, and to hurt

myself with my fashioned lies

I don’t know if what I have

should be said / transformed

to song – it is not

proud or pretty, even

in a slant-wise look, more, rather

shameful, and anything to change it

what all the poets

have done

so, the real problem is,

what do I believe?

and I knew what to write when I believed rightly, and owned it,

but cannot claim it.

part of the problem is my

mindset.

and-bury your-memory,

Dear Barrett,

I just wanted to take the time to thank you once again for all your help with letters of recommendation, and to apologize for pestering you so much while you were in Germany.

I consider you a model of what it means to push the limits in the realm of thought. The way you negotiation of the role as a poet-critic inspires, to say the least.

In terms of contemporary theory, I have been getting to know Eric Santner’s thought, and spending some time with Žižek, Badiou, and Agamben. Santner has briefly introduced me to psychoanalytic theory, so some volumes of Freud are waiting in my near future. I’ve been pushing deeper into the philosophical tradition—Husserl, Levinas, Spinoza, Nietzsche—as well as continuing to widen my basis in the classics—Aristotle, Plato, Lucretius. I’m continuing study in Greek and Latin, along with classical Hebrew, and plan to study German next summer, possibly at Middlebury. Where this is all taking me is still, for the moment, wide open, but it involves a strong commitment to innovative approaches to the classical tradition and to religion as it is being variously appropriated and dealt with in contemporary theory and culture.

Just wanted to let you know what’s going on in my world. Also, on my shelf I discovered one of your books, the Reception Studies Reader. If you send me your address again I’ll drop it in the mail.

-M

Leibniz’s thought is painfully beautiful. Complex majesty – infinite and alien spiritual atoms, each a universe unto itself. One possible problem: it could be argued that the only power it leaves to God is the power of creation. Since spirit has no direct effect on matter, or vice versa (or spirit on spirit? is matter the only efficacious thing?), the only act that God could truly perform was the single act of creation. In a way this leaves no problems since, because He saw everything beforehand and coordinated it perfectly, there could be no possible need for him to interact on physical matter: all His work was accomplished, from the beginning of time to its end, at the moment of creation.

But could He interact if He so chose? Could He act on matter outside of the initial act of creation? \[This problem might be coming about simply from my taking an overly simplistic and naïve view of time.\]

How does Leibniz come out of this mix (Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz) as the most seemingly spiritual? Why is he so often ignored in contemporary history of philosophy, and the entire age cast in terms of Descartes, when Leibniz clearly seems to have posed more satisfying answers to the questions plaguing metaphysics?

Lucretius, from De Rerum Natura

You, who were the first to find a way to lift so bright a flame,

from such deep darkness, and shine its light on the joys of life –

I follow you, you diamond of the Greeks. I set

the straining traces of my feet inside the imprints of your path.

It’s not so much from a desire to usurp you, but out of love,

because I long to be like you. What? Can a swallow match blades

with swans? Or a little goat with its legs aflutter

on the racetrack strain with the speed of a thoroughbred?

You are my father, the inventor of my oeuvre. Your pages,

star, provide me with a father’s precepts.

Just like bees, which taste all the nectars in flowering fields,

I graze on your golden words.

Golden, and more than worthy of life eternal.

The moment your thought starts to loudly announce

the nature of the universe, unveiled by your holy mind,

my spirit’s terrors scatter, the bars of the world

melt away. I see all that goes on throughout the emptiness.

Peaceful thrones appear, and spiritual power,

against which no wind howls, nor clouds with raindrops

spatter, nor hoary snow, sharpened by sleet,

lashes against and pierces. The cloudless ether ceaselessly

protects it; it glows with scattered light.

Again: in everything it is self-sufficient, and not a thing

for even a moment interrupts its mind’s tranquility.

On the contrary, the rivers of Hell are nowhere apparent.

Not even the earth prevents a piercing vision

of everything that goes on in the bottomless beneath my feet.

In the midst of this a certain supernatural joy

spreads over me, and a trembling: because by your power nature

is so manifest, so naked – the veil is stripped from every shadow.

that leads to what is and is real:

That is why we must adhere to firm philosophy

concerning, not only things above – how the orbits of sun and moon

come into being, and by what force each particular thing

is accomplished on the earth – but also and especially, with savage rationality,

we must investigate both what constitutes the intellect, and the essence of the mind,

and also what it is that, meeting us while sleepless, struck with sickness,

terrorizes our thoughts, or while buried in the sepulcher of sleep,

so that we seem to see and hear, in the flesh, the presence

of those departed in death, whose bones the earth embraces.

…

Therefore death to us is *nothing,* and its meaning less,

since we believe that the soul, by its very nature, has its end on earth.

It’s no different than this: we now feel none of the pangs of that point in history

when from every side the Carthaginians poured in to rage against Rome;

when the entire planet heaved with the panicked crash of battle,

and cowered, and trembled beneath the high expanse of heaven;

and no one knew which, of the two standards, would be staked

over land and sea, above every man, and woman, and child.

The same, when we no longer exist, and that final violent rupture

between body and soul (from the union of which, we are) is a fact.

The truth, for those of us who won’t exist, is that nothing at all

will be able to wake our senses, or bother us by happening.

(Not, at least, if dirt is mixed with water, and water with sky.)

5/5/08

The sad-tragic thing about writing is I don’t know how to do it. For the first time in my life I feel the fear. Sit down look at the page the cold blank page that’s nothing. Sit down, feel blank blindspot behind mind in down below mind in gut that’s where the writing comes from but it’s blinking, little caution light little check engine light on the dash beep-beeping from my gut.

There’s the Terror in the walls. Nothing to do but sit down face the gut-sick rustiness of lack of practice and unflexed spiritual expansion muscles and bite the ridiculous silly bullet until the wind comes back out of my mouth. Nothing to do but keep moving in the awful awkwardness body-consciousness of new writing, of writing after long escape.

Writing only comes in a flow. You know when you sit still and that terror cockroach rummages around in yr gut y’r on the wrong track. You know when you have to paw around that gutter mind for some filthy coin that appropriate word y’r off the narrow way, y’r down down in the broad wide paths of words, when writing in fact has little to do with sentences or phrasing or words or a quarter.

Writing is more like a movement. One thought leads to the next with a necessary pendulum-like appropriateness that follows, one on one to the moon – which is where all writing ends.

Seperateness – jewel-eyed mind center memory-object let it unfold there for you, lose yrself in the object.

Yeah yeah – it’s not that writing is a talent, or that it has anything to do with words. The sad-sick thing about not writing is that it’s not yr words that get sick and stale but yr little scrap of song that’s all you have on the planet – that little scrap of song yr soul. And writing is soul-expansion, feeling out of soul / feeling out for besides-itself.

There is one thing I want, though. I want the words to be practiced and sharpened and true – because I have a desire, a method-desire I’d like to be fit for, to put Kerouac and Isaiah together, and I can’t even express it words so worn and vacuous and silly.

If I could write one word, one word that’s really real. Sad sick delirium tremens of the sad-sick wordless soul.

Wordlessness.

Kerouac in hell. You see maybe I’ve just gotten tired in general in my life no will no wisp to make the journey up the mountain. You see maybe I’ve just lost the will to bite to fight through the sinking sand. And to know that someone else will have to read this, and yet I’m sitting here just writing as if I’ve got no spark in the world, as if all the spark’s gone out and just some old black charcoal just some lump of coal not glowing. When in fact I know that old eternal bright-eyed morning of the created world the planet – that bright old echo of the eternal one that making – when in fact I know that little light lights up in me and illuminates the inner worlds and all the substances of mind and brain come jumping up come sparking there on the inside –

Why? That would be a question worth answering, and to have answered it in part even worth this ridiculous scrambling.

Why tired? Why the process translated into internal one only – interior monologue for self alone that continues – yes, that yet goes on in the mind but through lack of practice resonates all hollow like a rusty metal drum.

Expansiveness word mind pendulum humdrum butternuts.  
electric red-shot hannover in a basket pendulum mutters like a nun.  
Red-hot ruts in the road red utters like, cow.

the Nameless Ache. or rather, it is not an ache

without a name, but instead the ache of name-

lessness. a Form of home-

lessness, a restlessness

without rest. it is then, properly speaking,

nothing. things have names and a name

is a kind of home, and a home

is a place to rest – resting in its name a thing becomes

as it is and was. and so a thing without a name

is not as it is, or was, it has no home and there is

no rest – not being a thing at all it’s only

Nothing. and those, I think, are the words I speak,

when asked about the thing that isn’t, when it visibly

haunts my face and so

gives a sign for the world to read – as if some

thing were there to haunt me, as if

I could give it a name. a thing without a name

is not a thing

at all, and so I say “it’s nothing, really,

nothing at all.”

ii\.

this curse, though, is what compels me. I’ve never created a thing

without its compulsion. there’s only one way to manage it and that’s to run

in a particular way. I have to run because it drives me

with the force of necessity

towards something. but in the direction I have

some choice, if only by

privation. suffocate the lips, or suffocate

the heart, suffocate the whole or suffocate

the part. but in this manner the will

is involved. I catch on something that is

Nothing: the will is the form we choose

of slavery, whether a circle or

straight line. the monad, the dyad,

the One. Six hypostases walked into a bar, a Jewish

hypostasis, a Catholic hypostasis, and one

made out of a straw. by my reasoning, the straw

had the best of it, Q.E.D.,

because you can use it

to drink.

from birth I was called to philosophy, and I have pursued

that calling

to hell.
