# Rebekah Goes to Hell

Rebekah thru the underworld (lyrical prose, fiction), July - August 2005

I.

Rebekah lay in her bed. Her room rose up around her. Her wide apartment window leered across at the glassy eyes of the adjacent building. Muted horns drifted in to her like the lingering scent of a heavy perfume. One long room with a flat and sculptured ceiling curled around the edge of Babel's endless towers. It ran some thirty feet, in length, an enclavature for the couch; some fifteen, in width, a tiny kitchenette with a small yellow light exhaustedly burning above the oven, set off from the somber silences of color in the darkened flat. A sheet of glass, animated by a skeleton of thin metal bars in a hatch work pattern, composes the eastern wall. The entire eastern wall separates the night from the room with only its thin glass; the large, overlarge night outside a baleful Charybdis, an endless vertiginous mouth; an illusory slant; a need to trail one's hand against the furniture, the wall, to brace oneself against falling in; but the thin latticework of iron, though paltry, insubstantial against the violence and weight of the gaping night, is enough; it breaks the illusion; levels; affirms the constancy of planes, the firm division between this world and the next. A thin latticework, though thin, boundary against the impenetrable darkness; and what darkness? What darkness this? Not that of the Prince of Flies, that bobble-head Lucifer grinning, grinning, grinning on the eternal dashboard of the mind; that one they called the Daystar whose fall was a burning comet seared on the flesh of the lower aether; but darkness; that which is not the unknown, but nothing; the specter of anxiety which flits above the void is the mind of man. And the iron latticework of the window, between her air-locked bubble above the concrete and the soundless vacuum of the night; a vellum shield, so thin that the light of blackness bleeds through; the pretension of definition and category; the arbitrary structure of perception; subduing; attempting to pacify the relentless unbecoming of ; the entomologist’s pathetic glass jar, containing the living metal insect of Time.

Her bed occupies an elevated alcove in the inmost corner, surrounded by a nightstand, books, reading lamps, pillows; marked off by a liminal threshold of plush, white blankets. A nest. From this heart of the apartment, books, stacked in odd, careening towers, flow out in haphazard blood arcs, sustaining the most distant limbs, unifying with the omnipresence of their substance. If the blankets create a nest of the bed, it is the books that create a nest, or some raptor's sullen roost, of the apartment. Like the bars in the window, they provide structure against the otherwise arbitrary pale of the wall's nondescript gray.

Excepting the distant, dim glow in the kitchen, the lights are out. Darkness. Rebekah lays very still, neither sleeping nor definitively waking, a gray specter made up by the shadows darting across it. A white beam from the window divided the room in hemispheres of dark and light; the night and the purple glow of the city's tired moon. No grain of mixed elements blended between their hemispheres; the boundary of light hung above her, precise; cut by a knife from its brother blackness. The weight of time gently pooled in Rebekah's thighs; her eyes fixed above her, motionless but open. Stillness sat on Rebekah's face like a mourning dove of smothering; gently cooing as it drank her life, unresisting. A pneumoniac restlessness clutched itself inside Rebekah's chest; rocking itself gently to madness. Beneath this, this three-faced darkness, lay Rebekah; the queen of silence and her unwarranted subjects; the weight of time; stillness; madness. Her fingers fluttered at the corners of her nightgown.

She'd filled her day as she filled each day. With business. With objectives and hopeful wanderings, crisscrossing the grid work of the city above its bottomless vent; issuing grim clanks and the sounds of alien metals from within, the impenetrable veil of its deep-earth engine; that monster that invisibly, perpetually orchestrates the city.

Rebekah lay in her bed. Her breath raked inward. Clung. Shuddered and slowly, with pathetic fingers clutching, she dragged it outwards. Again. Her breath rakes inward. Clings. Shudders and hesitates and strains (so like a living thing, to fight for life) before collapsing back into the monstrous night, devoured. In one. Out. In. Out. She shudders a bit and rearranges the weight of her body stiffly, lifting the weight of her hips and legs first up, on the small of her back, then pulling herself slightly downwards with the balls of her feet and relaxing, her weight recentering on her shoulders and butt. She breathes; a breath crawls in; shudders; drags it out by the hair (and endless, neurotic codependence); flings it to the wall where it sticks and glares at her, sliding into oblivion; shifts weight; breathes; shudders; shifts; weight, shudders: the small of her back aches. She struggles out with a breath and shucks it off; then turns, slightly, first drawing beneath her her arm, then rolling forward onto it her body's other half, pulling tightly up into a question mark on the bed where the sheets rub, rub, rub. The sheets are soft and cool. A synthetic silk. They burn beneath and above her with their stillness and, demure, shrink-wrap around her softly. The weight of time; stillness; sheets; she breathes in deeply; shudders; claws it thirstily to the surface.

In one. Out. Shudder. Respond in; one. Out; shudder. Slowly, revolving shapes posit themselves on Rebekah's eyelids, her eyelids cool and soft and slightly wet as they hit their bottom, from which she raises them, scattering images like a school of minnows startled, dispelling them. The small of her back aches. The fetal position exerts a pressure on her spine that slowly builds into a throb. Exhales and. Deeply breathe. Inhale. And. Abruptly shift from the side to the back. Stare at the ceiling, a flat black projection screen for the rusted neon machinery of exhaustion; shapes and strange, geometric impressions; sensate; corporeal; beginning indefinable oozing green-black depressions in the ceiling, melting, sliding off the eye's edge into the pale black nothingness of the room's white frame around it; with black and white pixels that slowly rotate, expand, are expelled and extinguished by a fluttering eyelid; bide their time (bare moments), resolve, rotate black and white patchworks of extraterrestrial plaid, a smattering of red mandalas bloom in the mixture, forcibly shaping the contours of vision, alienating perception from the shards of its body; slowly resolving.

The shapes played in a mandala of rotating memory. The projector wheel (the weight of time; stillness; madness) turns excruciatingly and clanks thread worn reels into overlarge existence on the ceiling; the reel rolls; her eyes coalesce in a single point, lock on a vision, shimmer, blur (she doesn't know whether, now, they're shut or open) and a tinny soundtrack grinds into existence; image flutters up, the liquids of her mental theater congealing into a misshapen figure of clay; a memory: John, the flower store full of gardenias, peach-colored carnations, baby's breath in a long metal container inside the cooler filled with spring assortments in this dreary winter (this is the day that's playing back before her; her day just past; a randomized sunburst of memory from the string of empty moments that rotate like thick black stars around her dwarf of sea blue mourning (Ichabod; what words do I have for you? If you are lost to me... then so it is. It is. But your memory - I gag. A strong red bile that bites backwards from the funeral mound of the stomach. The small of my back aches. The sands of time are - they are. The whole dry desert shifts beneath me; a single grain falls down to you in the underworld. I've lost all frames, Ich. There's no definition, boundary. All the frames blend together: some dull gray mixture, neither present, future, past; an indeterminate slush.)) black and white at first with a jumpy reel; missing frames and, from time to time a second's speck of fly-wing stuck in the amber-like film; whole colonies of dust distorting the strange configurations attempting to fashion themselves from the colorless alien tides of a far off moon; some colorless far off moon full of pockmarks and scabs and meteor craters stabbed in its flesh and an infinite, tranquil sea (her ceiling); strange configurations: gold-winged hyacinths flecked with purple flecks of incandescent flesh; long silk stems of leathery green;

(There is a consistency, at least, to this fracturing of forms; I am in the flower store, you're with me, but dead; I am twelve; I'm with my mother at the nursery; we're buying a cutting from fine German grapes; It's Tuesday, today; John talks to me about business and the poor state of things since the presidency began to fumble; I respond appropriately, with a placating smile, a sad little yes, yes, can't believe we're coming to...; this reverberates both backwards and forwards; a node, my body a single node in a flexing cloth pattern of time and space, all interwoven; my yes sings backwards through the years; my mother hears it and she takes my hand tightly as we proceed to the checkout (there you are, John, but you're younger, so much younger, and handsome; strong black hair and smaller glasses; a kind and angular face, well-formed, your long green apron stained with dirt) where she fumbles through her purse for a dollar bill which hovers there above the counter of past and future, resolving into my hand, my bill (but a ten this time, ah, yes John, inflation is destroying our nation; those Democrats will have it under in no years flat) for a single rose (long white roses; ah rows and rows of roses, Ich; (it's the day of your funeral; the roses, blinding white, on the thick brown mahogany box of your bier as it sinks into the ground, a wave of relatives in black surges in around you, pulled forward as if by the gravity of your distant moon sinking, sinking, plowing down through the sea to the distant shores of some outer planet where we mourners may not follow; I was a rose, there, a single rose in the ugly dozen black of the terrible hour; blinding blue; a rich, royal blue I wore to the funeral because I could not, could not bear to surround you with black, and impassive, matte black of living rejection; a living mouth that echoes out a rolling No, We deny your life, We cast you from us as dust, as you fall backwards and your body sinks down into the warm brown earth that welcomes you;) and I whisper, yes, John, yes, take the money, please, and his question booms out over the arch of centuries and settles upon its roost to caw its sign over the entire panoply like a curved, orange beak of question: Are you alright?

My fingers flutter. Even now they flutter, and I drag a breath in and drag it out, and shudder, and wait for the answer to come rolling out of my stomach. But it doesn’t. I spent the day like I spend each; just please, pretending, trying to make it alright by going to and fro, only for this terrible question to pierce me to my empty heart.

It’s been, what? Three months? Three months since you left me. And so I am not alright. I mourn. I sleepwalk while waking. I go through long periods where I’m fine, and I feel like this endless weight has been lifted by some blessed god who succors, succors; for days like this, and then one day I wake up and my head is an empty hole and my breast burns and my stomach sings with a freezing sadness; and I’m not alright, but there is nothing to do but wait; wait with stillness in the bed; think nothing; breath with a shallow breath; wait for that slow building of sound in the inner voice to say: Rebekah. Wake; and god awfully fall (literally fall) from the bed to drag myself through my rows of books (ah, like roses, so like flowers there; a solace; as if you’re smell is burned there in their pages; a blissful forgetting (which is what your scent is and always was) that thrums strongly, strongly, with the familiarity of pages; blessed forgetfulness; and yet there are times; I turn a page, and there I so no letters, but your face, again your face so vividly - ah! aching face! accuser! forgetter! and I slam shut the book and salt water stings out from the ducts and I close my eyes and wait;)

I am sleeping but awake; young but old; the past swarms in a ghostly overlay on the present, the future (not its shadow, but the radiant sun of its pewter becoming).

The fire of dream burned above her in the sky and alighted on her in tongues of flame. She woke, she slept, she never moved. The walls of her apartment were swiftly transforming and dropping away. Their borders dissolved and became grayly transparent, before buckling (like the fog, whose ending, though indefinite, may sometimes burst forth unexpectedly) and receding backwards into the depths beyond the reach of sight; the color changed, the murky silver-gray slowly overtaken with a deep blue-green (summer colors; ah, you remember last summer in Belsen, when the wind whipped over you and stole your hat and the sweat of summer dresses, 100% cotton filled with deposits of breath beneath the cherry tree that summer spent sitting, singing, waiting for the world to open up beneath our fingers and crawl inside our trembling hearts and stay there, take up unearthly habitation for the coming winter which, for a time, you thought it had; taken up habitation there; come under the laurels of your corporeal house because of the blessed youngness, or, or (no names for this period of untold blessings, no names for the blessings that touch upon one, maybe once in a life, those periods filled with enchantment and unearthly sense of unreality, composed, as it were, not of movies, but of their ultra-actual signifieds, the living flesh of the moment seared in the stills and stuck there, on unending repeat (You go from dream to dream inside me. You have passage to my last shabby corner, and there, among the debris, you've found life. I'm no longer sure which of all the words, images, dreams or ghosts are "yours" and which are "mine." It's past sorting out. We're both being someone new now (You were always mine, Rebekah, as I was yours and so remain. There is a layering of this dream, where levels drop away and are lost; but no matter: it brings us here to the inmost. Parenthesis implies a sort of anxiety; the sense that we're being folded into neatly compressed squares and tucked into deeper and deeper wells, a heart of darkness pierced by no light; a claustrophobia (We drift more freely now, tucked away inside the heart of God whose shape is an infinite unfolding) as the thread (oh poor, oh lamentable, oh tragedian scholar; Ariadne the infinite reader) that leads to the lower levels (you deceive yourself to believe, poor deceivable, that the lower levels are lower, or anything but contrivances arranged against the limitless upward, downward unfolding of infinite levels) unravels to leave us lost (ah, poor lamentable Hansel, lamentable Gretel) at the maze's heart; yet here, together, lost, in the inmost - here -

Now you're flying; the silence of the upper air; unearthly; motionlessness; enveloped by whiteness, thinner than it looks from the ground; gray tendrils of cumulous saffron filled with dust and mist; a lethargic fog; cloud-thunderer; lightning lancer napping now; Zeus the lethargic wetly assenting to your passage; floating softly across his back; he glances at you and curls more tightly up on the ledge of the sky; a thinning in his sidereal hair; his embrace dulls and slips free; the cloud thins, thins and is gone; the ground looms below you; realize now you're rushing, rushing, and have been, at unimaginable speeds; whipping faster down towards the distant earth (what now; 3000? 4000 feet?) dress billowing out behind you like a mad pyrotextile blossom burning out the tiny breath of its short-lived flame with a dithyrambic abandon; the skin of your cheeks sucked backwards (Zeus, lethargic thunderer, don't you see your daughter?); your eyeballs curling backwards, backwards, sucked up inside your skull as you struggle, struggle against the weight of Gravity the Eternal and Speed the Unattainable Lover whipping, whipping, beating away at you as you rush down and the earth, as well, a blossom, a mathematical blossom rendered and digitized and tipped on its axis and dissected on a screen before you now; gyrating madly as it rotates, stretching up across your vision, filling it, tipping on its digital axis to encompass the bottom of the screen; then disassembled, broken apart into a swarm of truncated strings of code like maggots exploding from the bottom of the garbage can and rushing across your body like a perceptual infection to reassemble at the top of the field; (all this marked with no internal feed from you, dearheart; your fear is still up there, somewhere, disembodied gibbering and popping out its eyes while your body rushes towards Earth the Impenetrable Hard Surface of Doom at a thousand miles per second per hour or more).

The slim towers of the city, a jagged canopy of metal jungle glaring up at the heavens, daring the gods to roost in its spiny turrets; first a fist of metal in the distant spread of sea and earth; the strand of the island a malformed ear on its studded metal head; but soon, soon, sooner than you thought it could it grows up large and rises up to meet you; the sullen, scarred face of the polis turns to you to meet your screaming descent; it sneers at you and calls your bluff, doing nothing but unveiling the glass-sharded structure of its crystalline battlements; on and on you fall and the strand of light that attaches you to your fear is shrinking; the rubber band tension that left fear behind on first descent is stretching, stretching, rebounding and snapping it off its claw-marked ledge and rocketing it down, down, winding up as it drags it back into your back and kicks it in to the cavity of your lungs where finally a scream rips free and the city glowers and swallows it up; rising now; rising now before you; opening its stone-hinged mouth to accept your sacrifice and; splash! through the canopy of the upper leaves, missing the stone-towering trunks; straight down above a small patch of green; slowing (Don't worry, dear; it's all been staged); the wind brushes its calm, strong fingers across you; slowing; the park resolves where she sat in August, shortly after my funeral;

A warm breeze blows. Long shot: a branch or two obscures the lens; slow zoom, part the branches; appears the long green expanse of a soft autumn park; wrappers and obscure lumps of paper like patches of beautiful, white-blossomed weeds. Center: cast iron park bench with chocolate-colored wooden slats; on it a drawn blue figure, seen from behind, slats ribbing the sight of the royal blue back; feet set closely together; hands drawn up on the lap; head, the back of the head of luxurious black, that summer-soft black of hair that crowns her now and always like a winter angel (It's you yourself, dearheart); A wispy black strand of hair brushes past the side of her cheek. Close-up: her hand slowly brushes it back to rest, two slim fingers pressing against the temple.

Short shot now of the back of the bench, camera angled slightly downward, placed slightly above the level of the top of her head; her eyes are invisible, but her head is fixed on the city, which lays before her in the cleft of the park's green frame like the Holy City seen from the river's distant side; some Promised Land in the valley nested between the rivers of Eternal Prosperity, in the West, and the mysterious flow of Human Invention in the Face of Need, in the East. Some bright egg of promise thrusting itself up from the cool, smooth lap of the Holy Earth.

The white light like a fluid gently suffusing.

A strand of the sparkling sea separating that land from this, the city from park; a garbage tanker slowly roiling across the calm blue water; the city hovering; not the specter of madness and pockmarked fortresses seen from above, but a mother; a calm gray mother stretching out achingly; from the bottom, seen from here, imploring; will the heavens fall today? Please be kind to my babies; let them sing across my back awhile; let them go about their days in the calm of my stony lap; sing, sing; let me put my hands together and pray; please, Father, let them sing about my back today in safety.; and the soft light of late afternoon, no hint of red yet or even orange but the soft amber yellow glow of 3 or 4 o-clock suffusing, blessing, kissing the vision with a strange, candescent oneness and stability; a holy grove in the lap of the Holy One where silence reigns and sings of its King the Eternal Succor;

An incredible stillness. The moving things, even; the chattering of the chipmunks as they dash around the trunks of trees; the lilting cry of the birds as they wash out over the park with their soft tongue of song; the wrappers rustling in the manicured grass; the distant call of the barge and the whine of afternoon traffic; the net of horns; all compose a part of the stillness; not a sterile stillness, but that of the living, breathing Becoming in its oneness; (from the heart of the violet mound cries Holy! Holy!); the wind ripples around her royal blue lap; her soft hands rest there, folded, peaceful; the sun hangs above the city and breathes its light out over the her head, hair, face; warmth; everything rustles; breathes; is suffused in warmth and light; a soft white Holy! ever glow bulb; the grove in its silent stillness;

There, then. The vision rests. The park; Rebekah's back from the bench; the city across the river spread out before her; the sun slowly sinking, spreading out its echo.

The sun sinks, slowly sinks; its lower edge soaking the skirt of the city's upper boundary; yellow sinking into orange that bleeds around the edge of the stony outline; the buildings' facades becoming black as the sun's brilliance enfolds them; the dark side of the moon; an eclipse; concrete spear piercing the sun as it sinks lower, lower; orange sinking, lips of red stretching out to kiss the city, to sparkle rose colored tips of fingers tracing the miracle face of the water; she sits. Silent, impassive. Soaking it up. Unmoving. Unthinking.

A dot appears on the opposite shore (this vision is inscribed by a circle and inverted; the first half holy, blissful, radiant and soft; the second, pierced by this figure, and the sinking sun; rose red; no malevolence; not quite the open coldness, the tragedian howling of an autumn evening's bleating, but the absence of the light in its fullness; a soft melancholia; a gentle inversion).

(Pay attention, now; it's your dream-soft eye that captures this; you'll need to draw it with you as you clamber back onto the shore of the waking (morbid suitor that it is)).

Destiny inscribes the moment like the circle. There is no sense of the uncanny; all was predetermined, precalculated; all variables set ahead of time, placed in careful alignment to fall into place as this moment; still, no glimpse of her face; seen above her head, the indistinct figure at the murky, distant boundary where water fades into the lip of the rising city; a dot, growing; moving with an bobbing, steady security; walking out across the water now (and walking, yes; a figure, a man, a man in a long black tux); walking out across the water across the ruffled trail left by the barge and coming closer (doesn't anyone see?); he grows, features becoming visible (ah, the beaked white nose; those absent, sandy eyes; that auburn grimace thrown on by a fluke of design; the lanky stride (the one and only, dearheart; yours in the flesh, from the dead and back; a miracle man walking on the water like a messianic specter of divine incantatory dance step shimmy; \**splam*\* from the underworld in an otherworldly flesh); "Ichabod," she whispers, without a trace of dread or surprise (this moment, see, this unfolding so precise like unrealized memory); and now he's close.

The red lips of the sun bleed out above the city's teeth. A cool breeze blows. He brings with him a dampness, a dampness in the wind like autumn eyelids brushing the skin. A cool breeze blows. Shot of the side of her face: the breeze rustling her black hair around her ultimately pale complexion, hands folded in her facile lap; head tilted downward, eyes half-shut; lips slightly parted; a pale burn in the side of her cheeks that shows so clearly on her transparent skin; her breath draws calmly up the inside of her stomach, raises her chest, her shoulders; releases. He covers distance quickly, floats. He's near now, in the park, floating (though moving his feet he floats, he moves so quickly without rushing) above the grass and the litter, now sad in the soft blue light beneath the red, depressive ceiling hanging above in the sundry firmament; and then he's there, here, looming up before her in the fullness of his stature; thin, tall, impressive, non-threatening; and she, still, barely moving but for the soft, small rise in chest and shoulders, and that not hers but the wind's subtle fist of clenching, unclenching inside her; face tilted down with no emotion, or some unknown, intense emotion playing beneath the surface but refusing to break free in the eminent text of her cheeks; and he reaching a long-fingered hand out to clasp it gently around her down-turned chin and pull it, softly, so softly, not forcing, only uncovering to what the body gives itself in yielding; and her eyes draw surely open with a swift, clean movement, neither over-hasty nor detained; precise, sure, predestined; and there they lock (not fawning, now; erase the penny-novel pedantry from your imagination); caught there; idyllic, frozen; some bizarre biologist's species sketched out in a curious diagram; or reassembled from bone to tower eidetic in museum walls, cordoned off with a plush blue velvet, gazed at. For a moment only, fixed.

And the moment ends. He drops down on the bench beside her, arms flung out for a second as he reasserts his balance, then set calmly on the drawn up knees; coattails fluttering in the dirt on the ground behind the bench.

(silence. she peers at him.)

-Ich, there's such a strange veil around your face.

-Ah, ah, (his hands flutter around his face) must be something with the weather, or this blasted wind that's blowing it's-

-Ich, it's an ink. Yours eyes that used to shine- it's like an ink (she's peers inside the cavity where his features should be); it's like an ink, Ich; I can't see your eyes.

-Must be something with the weather or-

(she punches him in the gut)

-Ooof!

-Imposter (punch)! Hypocrite (punch)! Terrible liar (punch)! *Three months!*

She punches again, harder; he doubles over; weakly lifts his hands against her fists.

\-*Three months* in the pall of death!

-Enough.

She continues pelting; he bats away her hands and, getting angry, grabs her wrists; she struggles against him; kicks; he braces his leg on her shin, presses her back.

-I said e*nough!*

The word rings out over the park. The cool wind returns it coolly, elongated.

-(softly now) Enough.

She untenses. Falls back into the hard wood of the bench. Shakes; head down; shoulders shaking slightly; crying, like; a little storm trembling up inside her.

-I can't stay for very long.

-No. (shakes) You... how could you?

-Please, Rebekah. Our time is short.

-Shorter than we know.

(silence)

-The days, I mean. They go by quickly.

-Bek-

-You were so cold, at your funeral. Dead! You, the invincible dancer - dead.

-Things go more quickly... than we intend, I guess. (pause) I never intended-

-To leave. (pause) I know. I know, I know - I'm sorry, Ich. This is just all so unexpected.

(silence)

-My days have passed like a passage through desert - I wander all day, I sort of sleep, like this, though, filled with ghastly visions, all night.

-Astray.

-Oh, astray (sardonic)- what's better, then? This way, that? I wander no more or less. The pitiable state of wandering, though - so clearer -

-Ah, ah, dearest- it's worse than I thought.

-You thought?

-Nothing. I'd just hoped that-

-What?

-My job-

-Your?

-Yes. (pause) Business.

-Ah. (she returns her gaze to her lap. They sit in silence.)

-And you'd hoped that?

-To find you.

-And?

-I have. (pause) You're sort of lost up here.

-"Lost" implies a way to find, I-

-(raises his hands to stop her) Fine, enough. Fine. (absently) What a downer.

-(frustrated shout) You're *dead*!

(silence)

-Awfully blunt, Bek.

-You're infuriating.

-It's all about the approach, these matters-

-You'd *dead! You - are - dead.*

-(throws hands up) *Fine*.

\-*Fine*. (crosses arms)

(silence)

-The next time I decide to march up from the doldrums depth of hell - yes, hell, the blasted land, the blight of the central sewer star - a *long - freaking - walk -* the next time I decide to-

-Ich-

-What?

-I'm sorry.

(silence)

-I just feel like you left me.

(silence)

-Sorry.

-S'okay.

(silence)

-(sigh of frustration) So easily distracted.

-Hm?

-Distracted. See, my job - a mission - business.

-What?

-A message. I've to deliver a message.

-What?

-The subway station.

-Hm?

-On 42nd.

-The?

-Go there.

-To?

-You'll be waking soon. You need to go there. You've been called. We're to meet. I'm just... the messenger, see.

-What on earth are-

-There's not much time. I'm dead, you see. There's not much time.

-But Ich, you're just a dream, I-

-Nothing of it. Look at my face.

-I can't, a darkness-

-That's the ink of the underworld. My features, my eyes - no substance. Inky. No substance. In the underworld, there - you'll be able to see me - but now. Back

-To-

-Back. I must go back soon. I'm sorry.

-But-

-Sorry. I'd like to say I've missed you.

-(face crumples) Oh Ich-

-I have, in my way. But it's different there. The ties you held so dearly - different there -

-This dream-

-The timbre of the ultra-actual.

-Yes.

-Yes.

-Goodbye.

-So-

-Soon. Goodbye. Come. Quickly. All will precipitate. Come quickly. 42nd. The red line.

-I’m confused, I-

\-*Come!*

He rises, bows, begins to hum a tune beneath his breath. The Italian words float back with his coattails as he goes.

...loda di Dio vera,

chè non soccorri quei che t'amò tanto,

-But Ich-

-Bek (drifts back)

ch'uscì per te della volgare schiera?

non odi tu la pièta del suo pianto?

-I haven’t even seen your eyes.

-Not now.

non verdi tu la morte che 'l combatte

su la fiumana ove 'l mar non ha vanto?

-But when-

-Soon. Come.

-will I see you?

\- soon.

(his last words are lost)

\*

II\.

A cool breeze blew. The summer sky was blackened. A hint of chill rose up off the waters of the bay. Rebekah sat very still, his presence echoing in her body and the slender slats of the bench. The wind caressed the cilia of the ear's inner sanctum, whispers audible but unintelligible; sensed like a half-felt touch that brushes the hairs on the back of the neck. A hush. The smooth, white scar tissue of her being; his appearance like a clean but brutal gash. She feels herself, unconnected to the purple-black park, floating above the body (or within it; down; beyond the reach of the central nervous system; felt as a reflection in the small, black pool in the gargantuan caverns of the body; the endless catacombs of the empty flesh; unnoticed there in the depths: a small black pool; her reflection; water dripping ceaselessly). A split in the continuity of presence, however visualized; conscious of her own still body breathing on the bench, aware of it as if seen from overhead; breathing. Still. Small movements in the fingers; on odd amalgamation of cause and effect; feeling the neural impulse, the balletic arc of electricity from dendrite across synaptic cleft, shot down the slender alleyways of corded conduit organon, brain to hand, to move the fingers, unlike the purely visual impression one would have when watching the movement of another; yet without causal consistency; seeing the fingers move before the impulse to move them registers. Aware of the park around her. Ghastly purple-black. Only the plasticked lights of the city in the distance, the body of water lost to the sight, registering only as the disembodied lapping against unseen shores.

Some corner of her consciousness is aware of the dream as dream. Yet it is cordoned, isolated, quarantined by the fracturing of person. Rebekah finds no locus for her self; she is aware of many things, yet even this awareness has no locatable center; her awareness of her mental and physical processes spreads across their totality, yet remains an observer only of them; also without the ability to focus or sharpen awareness on any particular facet; sense information registers here (the purple-black park; the trees that rustle like the thousand lost sheets of nature's never-published manuscript); emotional there (the old throb of loss; the fresh slash of Ichabod's entrance).

The throb of a city clock gongs across the dream, building in the aural plane its ripples, spreading through the cloth of the body, the park, stretching through them like the head of the wind, softly pulsing through the cavity of summer's open wind to buckle and undulate; the sound waves spread through the dream, shiver the bed and the waking body; splash out across the apartment, uniting sleep and waking. And Rebekah cannot find herself; she finds no center for the awareness that spreads across the multiple planes of experience.

Rebekah lay in her bed. The sick glow of the moon diffused itself on every surface. A soft green glow suffused every corner. A radiant emptiness bathed the room in its fluid. Midnight's purgatory: the clock flashes red zeros: 00:00. They blink on and off, digital eyes peeking repeatedly into the room. The buzzer ratchets awake inside its plastic shell.

Flashes of color burst above Rebekah. The dream careens beneath her. She lay still, eyes closed, deeply sleeping. Static shots of song flowed out from the alarm clock radio: (italian). The words wrapped themselves around the walls and clung to the room with their thick red presence, a florid growth. The buzzer ratchets through the room. Two worlds converge in its icy aural verdict.

The boom of the city clock gongs out over the cityscape. Its ripples spread through the bed sheets. Rebekah's fingers flutter: there, for a moment, dream and truth collide in the superimposition, convergence of hand with hand, the dream-fingers fluttering with and in and *as* the pale, sweating fingers wrapped in sheets. Rebekah's awareness drifts haphazardly in the flotsam wash of staggering currents. She stands up from the park bench. Steps forward. The world of the park is compressed, flattened, takes on a 2 dimensional character, rotates around her. The entire sequence rises before her like a pictorial outline: lying in her bed, moving into memory, replaying her encounter with John at the flower store, a drifting deeper in sleep: the coming of dream, Ichabod's voice (so real!) recounting Belsen's short season: the tongue of dream descending: flying above the city, into the park, Ichabod's entrance, his message; the drift of his coattails as he slunk from her back into the abyss of the city; each moment represented by a visual icon (coattails; the motion of his hand; the flare of his nosy beak as it appeared; the mist of the clouds; John's coalescing shape) and united on a color-rich palette; the living substance of sequences compressed and flatted; the park itself around her crystallizing.

For a moment, in the thetic break between waking: the light touches her. A single, split-second beam illuminates: she sees her partitioned body, spirit, intellect; some Rebekah she has never met, frantic, standing in the gap between the known Rebekah (sleeping, vulnerable) and the vortextual abyss of an ocean, vast and wide, its waters the pure machinery of meaning; mediating between them; converting those chaotic waters into palatable Image; funneling them through the theater of dream.

All this in the moment's caress of the light, invincible and eternal. For a moment only; gone.

Rebekah snaps awake in confusion.

She startled up; she gasped. First fear: deep, quick breath; darting eyes; dilated pupils, wide and black. Hands clutching the blanket instinctively around her. Next, confusion. Breath slows; fingers relax slightly (but still hold the blanket); eyes dart, more slowly, scanning for something to substantiate their cerebral adrenal effulgence. She checks, and then again. A product of her dream? The alarm clock clambers noiselessly from 2:03 to 4, no buzzer. The silver-gray light shines constancy, as before. Its omnipresence dampens sound and color. The night's great gears have shifted, and a later hour come. Yet stillness, solitude, and the silver-gray light: they remain. She shakes her head, attempts to make sense. Finally, the fallout. Shoulders slump; breath whooshes out; the body slackens; the head sinks down to her chest, the neck a flaccid stem.

I can't take it, can't take it. (shakes her head). Can't take it. (fingers flex weakly). I can't take it can't- (breaks off). She feels blindly about the seething shape inside her, looking for a handhold, something to name. Some face to place on it, some easy word to drown it with. Some anything to move the immovable mass. Her hands pass insubstantially through it. What do I do? (shakes her head). What do I- (face crumples) You've got no right to haunt me. (no response). I said you've got no right to haunt me, now or ever! (silence). She can't escape the reality of it, the thick, living presence of it still shivers within her. She shivers.

She sits on the side of her bed. The clock rolls over into 2:15. She taps her fingers against her legs. She looks out the window, bites her lip. The dream is still so strong inside her, the textures and smells, colors and sounds - his very speech humming. The product of the crystallization persists, a small, smooth mental object tucked away inside her. Compact, she knows that tracing along its surface will activate it, a precise, panoptic memorial, the series of moments materialized in this metallurgic precipitate. She bites her lip. Stands abruptly, hands clasped in front of her, crosses the distance to the window, looks out; furtive, looks at the clock; thinking, thinking, begins to pace between the bed and window, thinking. Her right thumb rubs above the left thumb nervously, worrying the skin into pale pink dunes.

Where did it start? She runs her inner fingers over the curves of the hard object. I was in my bed, and... she stops, bites her lip, thinks. Finding the exact threshold between dream and waking will, somehow, contain this madness. Her thoughts, she knows, were wandering, that late night theater of memory and thought and shape and sound that marches out before her, splayed in bed, almost every night, every night since sleep became an agonized game of waiting; an absence speaking of itself and its need; phantasmagoria disintegrating demonically the boundaries between night and day. She knew that that had come upon her, as it often did, while she waited torturously for sleep to come and blissfully swallow the day. If only she knew when the dream had started, then, when his voice had invaded my slumber in this, this way, this way it never has before; her fingers search, she feels every cornice, every impression, looking for the notch that marks its beginning. There -

There. The theater had dropped away, then - The walls had dissolved, vision receded; and summer came; his voice, welling up as if it had never left, so close to the ear - I hadn't even questioned. Belsen, he said, you remember that summer in Belsen. That had been the beginning, and then he had taken me elsewhere, drawn me to a place we could meet (she was sure of it, sure that he had brought her to the park). Satisfaction. I may not understand, what or why, but at least I have it, now, its edges. From his voice declaring Belsen, to the fracturing and crystallization, that moment of light before I woke - its edges. A hard, compact pictorial object that I've surrounded, defanged, compressed in a subinfinite block of thought - here. She held the object in the palm of her hands. Here.

A tickling - a little scratch at the back of the brain that signals that urge. She looks across the room to her writing desk, then bites her lip, then goes there, flips the switch on the tiny desk lamp, sits.

A little warm halo of light shines down from the desk lamp above the cluttered writing desk. It is homey, comfortable, familiar. Rebekah opens her drawers, rummaging quietly around for a small, decorated writing pad, white, with two small butterflies dancing wistfully away in its corner, and regular, soothing blue lines dashing its chest from top to bottom, and lays it before herself on the desk, smack in the middle of the warm little pool of radiance spread out by the light. Her long black hair brushes against the desk and pools, as she pauses to think, to search the distant drawers of her brain, first, for the pen, in a specular black pool beside the writing pad. Somewhere, there, in the dim mental drawers, she finds them, and turns quickly to the small bottom drawer where she rummages, pushes aside a stack of old journals, loose papers, grocery lists, paid bills, packets of paper clips, to bring back a sealed pack of bics, blue, and holds them up, shutting the drawer before tearing off its plastic head with her teeth and dumping the dim intestinal contents on the desk.

She takes the pen, poises for a moment, and writes:

I'm so tired of these long nights punctured by pools of day, like this, this light on my desk that marks my sleeplessness. There's nothing I can do to describe what's going on inside me, although there's nothing more I'd like to do. It's possible that these two things are linked to each other - a divine irony - that, as my desire to express the unbearable thing in me increases, proportionate to that my expressive faculty is shattered like a dumb glass bell. An example: that psalm that so many singers redo - by the rivers of Babylon - (by the rivers of Babylon / where we sat down / and there we wept / when we remembered Zion / over the wicked? carry us away to captivity / require from us a song / so let the words, of our mouths, and the meditations of our mind / be acceptable in Thy sight / oh ...) their most desired thing, Zion, is lost to them - black nostalgia - but it's their captivity, their loss that requires from them a song, and the song, in turn, that paves the way to redemption. Their song recreates the impossible object.

I guess, actually, that doesn't relate - except as exactly the opposite of how I feel and what I'm trying to say. I'm an anti-Israelite; my capture is complete, Zion never was, my song is an icy brand that pierces the heart of the road back home. An anti-song, in fact.

I want some opaline language to erase the Promised Land - some system of dark mutters to wrap the land up in its harsh, guttural swear words; some black semiotic death machine to swallow up its memory. That, that should be my song - some consumptive dearth to blot out the impression left by the sun, some desperate death pall to bang on the gong of Eternity Sleep. Sleep, sleep, sleep - Nihilism! Non-Being! Religious Perfection!

(her pen stops. its scratches continue in her memory banks. she pauses, still. thinks.)

-"Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart"-

Let them contain their inversion, let them be self-negating, so that their coming-into-Being unfurls into its deathly white negative: Non-Being; a conundrum. Useful words for thinking along these lines - ouroborotic: of or pertaining to that snake that bites its own tail. Möbius strip - one of those paper ring visual illusion things that twists around itself so that there is no definable edge, per se. Of course, these words are only useful if one understands that they don't exist.

(Rebekah stops writing and lets out a vaudeville villain's laugh: "Mwaha ha ha, Rebekah, intellectual queen of the Night.")

So then let the tongue have its reign - let it be a devouring fire, then - a flame, a dark flame to scour the pages clean, to wipe away the dross and burn up the scrub - to destroy and devour and completely undo what was, to rain down destruction on the bitter, tangled thickets of the past - ah, ah, the Old Spirit sleeping there in the forest *is* old, he dreams of memories and long lost cities and ancient gold - he sleeps peacefully, deep in the most hidden sanctum of the old, old wood, there in darkness, under a mat of centuries rainfall, leaves, the prickling mat of pine needles - there he sleeps, everywhere he sleeps, in the forest - this is his place, his memory hall, his past - fire fire, let the fire come and burn away the excess scrub - let it bring to nothing then the tall, great trees of gray and deceitful yesterday - soon, soon, soon, a blanket of new blossoms - a mat of violets on the empty stumps of tomorrow -

Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue (Ps. 52:4)

For a moment, then, she's forgotten about the deathly dream that persists within her. These are small condolences, these moments, beneath the cataract eyes of her books, tucked snug away, even in the heart of the night, leviathan augurs of ill-omen banging about at the window, less than (the clock says 2:52) an hour away the inexplicable dream - these moments, a tiny pool of light in the incomprehensible single long day that is her life. It's really quite appropriate that Rebekah’s invoked...

\*

So here I sit. Without a sequence of time or events. In a small little pool of lamplight, the most melancholy midnight in Ever. Displaced. With only this sound of Scratching Pen to push aside the otherness of where and who I am, at this moment. And all the psychic material I can't make light of. That dream - I don't want to think about it. It's still there, right under the surface. How can I not think about it? By being someone else than who I am. By losing myself in the pen scratch.

(she stops and puts the pen to her lip and chews on its tip)

But here it is. What a strange divide in me; this lightness of spirit in the midst of melancholia. But is it really lightness of spirit? Or a clever forgetting? It's still right there! How can I not go?

(you need a crystal snapshot of Rebekah at this moment)

\*\*

Rebekah wears black. She is tall and slim as she smokes her cigarette, a statuette beneath the yellow-green fluorescent pulse pervading the cafe, degrading quickly from the twin rows of tubes on the ceiling.

A small, sad breeze blows. It fills the city with its howling. It fills the city with its forlorn touches, with its bankrupt fondling, its aching perambulations. The wind flutters its lips over stone skin, the flying buttresses in the city's wind-weary heights, the sandy ledges of its office buildings, its nest-strewn battlements. The wind drags itself across the city's rigid body, all the while, far above the act it howls; howls; pumps its ephemeral diaphragm; wraps itself in night. A hollow howl spreads its echo out. The wind whips and whispers.

\*

The streets are black. Rebekah emerges from their depths, a diaphanous figure that shimmers at the edges of the street as if the darkness of the night were a heat that burned above the sultry concrete.

Rebekah's eyes shut and open, shut and open, and the street before her wavers in the frame of consciousness. The streets are dark and small, fleeting animals dart in the mouths of murky side streets and womb-like alleys that swallow the glow of the moon. Rebekah hurries forward, stumbling on the cobbled stone (as it remains in the historical district, the ghost of the aching past which blind eyes trample) and catches herself on the side of a building, rests there a moment before lurching forward again into the river of blackness. She keeps her head close to her center of gravity, drawn and tightly strung above her curled up shoulders which cower from the endless eyes that watch her, milk-white, from the windows above as she passes deeper into the city's center and forward, forward to the call of occasional death and the silence. Her ragged breath breaks out hysterically and she stuffs it back in her chest and quickens her footsteps whose echoes fade into the ancient concrete of the moon that surrounds her, towers above her. She peeks above her tense procession to look into the distance where she sees the dim red glow of the station.

Almost there now, soon - the wind that carries me is a black one, may it not give out before dawn.

She glances back at the street behind her to see if she is followed; it stretches back in utter blackness, unrelenting. A bitter wind blows up from the bowels of the towering monoliths behind her and the light of a savage moon beats down.

There is some silence, back there; some unnamable; some thing whose name I know but cannot name; some dark suffering waiting there for me in the depths of the city from whence I've come, and hurry through, and to which I proceed as I howl forth; some silence whose name is an endless moaning. Ah, Ichabod, your ghost - your ghosts is ahead of me now, getting nearer. In a dream I've seen you; in a dream your face reared up before me and those terrible, death-kissed eyes without substance pierced me to the straining lungs. There in a dream you drew up before me to haunt me and accuse of your loss, “Rebekah Rebekah, you've been lost to me.” Oh, those eyes that drank in the light, that stirring in your fingers as you reached for me, “Rebekah, you've been lost to me, not even your soul is remaining; dearheart, lover, my imaginings are an emblem, my name is a sordid magic,” and that cry as you shrank from me and melted in the materials of the abyss that called you back to it, “Come for me,” you said, “come to me in the valley where the river drinks in memory and sleep is a heavy garment; come for me, come for me, come -” I bolted upright and a sickly sweat soaked me to the icy bone and I wept and clawed for you at the mattress.

Some dark echo reverberates with the thoughts that shake her, all in the space of a backward glance, and gurgles forth behind her, beating faster with the rhythm of her slippered feet on the heavy street. Do not, dearest, be afraid; you're not alone. A deep and horrid buzzing punctures the equilibrium of the night's scattered silence. A staccato rumbling fills the air. Rebekah's steps quicken, then break into a light run. She looks behind her and sees a remarkable nothing, a nothingness that swallows the streets she's passed and the images on the skyline. Her heart beats. She must get to that light; if only she can make it to the station there will be some chance.

\*

Dorris' statement of poetics (lyrical prose), 12/13/04

I feel like a refection, or I would like to, massless and transparent, but this brick of ice in my stomach seems to disagree. I am watching the snow cover everything in a cold white net of silences, and I feel there is no poetry. Look at the breeze whip those tiny flakes around; they drift along in one motion towards the ground to merge in a sea of whiteness. I am having a hard time completing a thought, or following through on a metaphor, or seeing anything but snow - just the chemical reaction of light bouncing off the flakes and against the ocular stem. Pure white dots without meaning. Internally, everything melts together into a slush that I sink into. I hold my breath; everything is bruised like spoiled fruit. I look out the window, watching brown-specked bananas drift down in a bruised yellow heap of indifferences, and I feel there is no poetry. I hold my breath; it creates a vacuum. I reach down inside myself and scrape out all the cameras. I reach inside myself and scrape out all the bananas and the slush. I scrape out everything, and spoon it into a large transparent sandwich bag that I keep beneath my pillow. The bag is a great viscous snoglobe, a mucous-shaped membrane with yellow-green tints in which I see visions. I sink inward:

(Dorris stood at the edge of the window screaming and spitting at the beetle-like cars and threatening to jump on a stroller which she saw as a minuscule speck, all of this as a sort of performance poem, a symbolic act of retribution for her own squamished childhood, and as a recreation of the artistic and representational signification of her own experience as falling through life with no handholds. However, An-D threw a cup at her back and drew on his reserves of compassion to cry to her in her distress, “get a hold of yourself you drunken rat”, and so instead she came inside and drank and with an exacto blade carved this artistic statement into her stomach:

> The poet is a devourer of sandwiches. She consumes whole planets of language and gorges on pre-prepared thought. The poet finds suffering and punches through it. The poet imitates God and becomes Him in the act of creation - immortal, all-powerful devourer of sandwiches. The poet is a discontinuous bubble machine. Neither bubbles nor poetry exist. There’s no such thing you’re a liar. The poet is an intense rage-ball of overturned dishes and unslept in beds with no sandwich. Everything is a sandwich machine and nothing weighs fifty cents. I am Dorris hear me roar. I am Elvis hear me . Everyone is sandwich-maker. Tuna-belts for your armhair.)

I snap out of the dream. I see experiential deserts. Everything

is white and the door’s been left open, and so the snow piles

in and everything is covered in whiteness. Sadly, there is no

poetry, only a sheet of freezing whiteness and a despair

because I am sinking, and everything soon will be whiteness.

Nature abandons me. Nature never existed. I drown out the

silences and write a pure-white word in the blackness and then it exists.

0 0 0

The pure-white word is

1\. another stone on a tumbling heap – the heap in its fall, while it falls – this has always been my interest – not the towering geometric spires, not long straight and regular or Stonehenge, but the falling, scattered – beauty here irrepressible, something more organic and natural than any frozen natural system (and by this I mean any natural system which is

2\. decontextualized to the point where it may be examined – not the Nature of scientists, no) but that living complex of system which is its absolute lack and may only be seen by completely dismembering one’s self from temporal perception and simply sensing – feeling – all things at once wind rain fire ice birds falling nest eggs crackling everything moving dying living

3\. being born time slipping up and around close and fertile and sucking up around the neck and pressing, pressing – smothering – that pattern most closely resembling a fractal, but so escaping it (and the fractal itself I take to be the living emblem of the artistic endeavor -) as to remain an empty symbol, a hollow remembrance like a

history written

by the dead.

13

I realize that I have died. I see out the frost sheaved windows and there is nothing there but whiteness. I write a history and it sounds like this:

I push

through the machinery,

like a miner with my silly

hard hat

in the gargantuan

elevator

shafts

of the mind.

drilling,

while the whole world

is dying

for lack

of this oil,

for the breath

of this fuel and the calm

dark flower

in pressure.

I reach

and redeem,

by any

necessary

means.

by the violent drill

or the desperate,

on the slick flesh

of the beast,

many stratums

reach

miles up,

deep -

there can be

no surrender

to silence - many

miles tower, many

miles wide but

not

so impossibly

thick.

the only way

is through.

others

have found

their way

to the center, but

it must be

always

renewed.

by any means -

the violent drill,

or desperate,

i drive

to the center

because the calm

flower's absence

would gray

all the colors

of morning.

**these marks**

**on the pad**

**will flower**

**on the chest**

**of the risen**

**Messiah.**

Now Rebekah was my girl--ms (prose, fiction, poems), 12/20/04

June 19th, 11:40 a.m.

Now Rebekah was my girl and had always been my girl. We knew sure-fire we would stick, and had no doubts about it.

However.

Her mother and her ex-step-dad had had a nasty split, and she immediately and with little warning had had to scram the state with her dear mother to Florida. Our strategy was to straight-away and with little to-do engage in an extensive letter-writing campaign, all kisses and hugs and such. As for myself, I had never been much of a writer, but engaged straight-away in rigorous and thorough letter-writing for Rebekah’s sake, because she was my girl and always had been.

Now, “Dearest Rebekah,” I wrote, “I am awfully sorry to see you have to scram like that on such an extended and unwelcome vacationary period. However, you are my girl and always have been, and so therefore we must immediately and at once engage in an extended letter-writing to-do with one another, during the course of which we will record our inmost souls and quotidian dailies and what-nots, precisely recreating a living similitude of each other for each other. Now, if it’s quite to your liking we will spend great care and effort in inscribing our very emblems here, so that we may access the symbolic what-nots of our deepest love-things. I certainly do hope this idea is to your liking, as I have already included in these pages the manifold essence of my being. Hope you enjoy it quite well along with a drawing I’ve included of the docks, reposed in the mournful silence of the city’s mid-afternoon.

Looking very much forward to our rendezvous in spacetime and etc. etc.,

Yours with deepest and most heartfelt sincerity,

Ich”

That was how I wrote it.

June 21st 12:03 p.m.

You must be acquainted with Rebekah, to understand the full import of our enumerations. Rebekah is like a character out of a gothic film with hair in long gashes of black against the horizon and very pale, like some flower on the nuclear surface of a winter sun, a pale winter sun that dies on an icy air and freezes down on the tundra and gives me headaches through the windshield, heat headaches no matter how cold it is. She is not so tall, but gives the impression of being tall and, though entirely too slim, does not give the impression of being entirely too slim. Rebekah laughs at everything like the sky is falling and she is the empress of the world's end. Despite this, my Rebekah is made of pink sheets and tastes just like satin.

She is a good girl with a wild streak and shows it only to me or those in the immediate circle of my closest heartfelts. I cannot stress enough the nature of Rebekah's laughter, which is like a freezing blue disease of wildflowers multiplying and buzzing like bees and blazing across the whole world and smothering it in electric shocks, and which could describe to you her character far better than my invisible words.

The night Rebekah and I met I had had a bit too much to drink. This is not a common occurrence, as I am often a clear-eyed presider-over-of-affairs who watches out for the drunken gang and stays quick on his toes and sharp as a sharp razor. But the night I met Rebekah was my birthday. The gang had gone to the trouble of knocking off a small liquor store nearby the house (which functioned like our piggy bank, our hard-weather stash which we drew upon for only the direst of needs) in order to get together the cash to take me out to Wallabee's Bar and Grill and get me absolutely trashed until I was slumping on the bar and mumbling about politics while singing. I was jubilant, unintelligible, and surrounded by the whole gang minus An-D, who had absolutely necessarily had to meet some friends in old-town immediately or else become a bar of soap.

An-D is a thin and sallow and pockmarked individual who rarely says anything yet manages to encompass the whole of everything in the warmth of his soul’s embraces. He is the subject of my deep fraternal affection, which I express to him regularly and to which he replies, “if you were to let me borrow 50 dollars I’d stop threatening you with my knives.”

Unexpectedly and without warning I saw two old friends who happened to have reneged on a debt of a large sum of money the spring before last and of whom I had not seen hide nor hair since nearly June. Being in a state of mildly exaggerated emotional response, I in one fluid motion snapped the neck off my bottle on the bar and lunged towards the entrance in which they were framed, chasing them from the bar and through the streets, waving my bottle like a glinting question mark, an accusation against and exclamation proceeding from the betrayed inner child whom I nursed with rage (I am a man of my word and loan out money only to those with whom I instill my deepest trust, and betrayal of that is a grievous assault to my personabilities and tenderest emotives).

Needless to say, it was a stormy night, inside and out, the night I met Rebekah. While I was chasing them through the streets, I must have tripped and fallen, because I woke up the next day in the middle of the street, wallet entirely gone, a long gash across my forehead, Rebekah having appeared to me in a ghastly and pallid vision in the delirious night, a tumultuous visage of Rebekah, wroth with anger and jellybeans, a haloed and pallid illumination of the ghost of our future rendezvous.

That was how we met, in a vision above the sky. We stuck sure and true from first sight.

June 25th, 9:32 a.m.

I received a letter with the morning mail, which is hastily stuffed in the rust-stained and barely visible mailbox. With little hesitancy she had written me back to say that she was Xs and Os concerning our plot to maintain lines of communication. Her mother was in quite a bad state at that time and drinking heavily, which was bad in many ways but meant that my dear Rebekah had just about free reign of the house and the car and all the personal what-to-dos contained therein. She promised posthaste to snitch enough money for a busticket down to the sunshine state, and I could in the meantime sit tight in my place of residence (a true centrifuge for cultural enlightenment and avant garde social practices and liberated systems of being, including but not limited too all varieties of shaded characters, if you happen to catch my drift). Now I had gathered about me a close circle of tightly-knits, a ragtag assortment of ne'erdowells and night urchins who, despite their lack of upward social mobility, were the emblematic containment of all my heartly matters, vessels of deepest latenight theorizing and drunken ramblings and, yes, camaraderlie love which we all held for each other so tightly as to near smothering. There were five of us who lived on the fifth floor in a two-bedroom box overlooking the Detroit River, that magnificent life-valve of the Holy City which contained all its detrital excrements. We were ragtag, slovenly, a bit bescabbed - but a family, and the love we held for each other was infinitessimal in its degrees of irrepressible gushings and slaverings.

Despite minor turbulence, all was going well and I wrote to tell Rebekah so, and express a number of joys at our newly found conjoinment in the sphere of the written. “Dearest Rebekah,” I wrote, “I was infinitely happy last night when we talked on the phone. Afterwards I sat down to finish your letter. There are bits of it scattered over several different days and several different notebooks. I remember I had wanted to write something to you about writing like this - letters like the last one you wrote -

Writing letters like this reminds me of riding the Greyhound late, late at night when all these strangers, all these sleeping faces - stream around me and myself-alone-awake, dim spotlight on in the overhead - the only pool of awake on the whole bus and vast hills-darkness-forest-sky all unknown and alien slipping by outside, the feeling that destination and origin have all shrunk to nothing, have all been imagined and are being imagined and will never be and never were, and all there is is the darkness and me, the only pool of awake on the bus and all those aliens slipping by outside the window, unnoticed, and the driver an alien creature just silent automaton and robot - his pool of light mechanical and alien sabbatical far far far up the aisleway and the big engine humming and burning and rumbling deep inside its stomach as it rockets smooth across the moon-flesh of the empty road, a long black silver strand of blackness taut across the entire blackhole universe and pierced by intermittent yellow dashes buzzing and strobing regular and rhythmic beneath the metal bus-stomach and the engine and the tires. Everything suspended. Time suspended. Me suspended. Everything unknown.

Writing letters like this feels like that. An exodus. A strange journey and I have no idea where it will dump me out.

Yours with heartfelt and most sincere sincerity,

Ich.”

July 17th, 6:02 p.m.

Things carried on like that for quite some time.

I must tell you that, despite all the debauchery and ill-repute of my outer appearance, within I hid a sensitive man with an ear to the redeeming aspects of our paltry existence, including but not at all limited to symphony (imaginations of the haggard slaves and mishaps of war’s gears marching by while Tchaikovski looked on, a darkling in his window, these encapsulated and globular bubbles of the living past slipping up to me through the dark rivers of time and blasting through the stereo speakers at many, many decibels (now, many times, in response to this, my uncultured and decadent neighbors had tried to put an end to it through various manipulative tactics and arm-twisting machinations, including letting off firearms through the walls, floor, or ceiling, bludgeoning me with various objects (lampstand table leg chair leg police baton elbow brass knuckles steel knuckles iron knuckles beer bottles broomsticks frozen turkeys (this really happened) amish hams baseball bats splintered 2 x 4s unsplintered 2 x 4s 2 x 8s splintered 2 x 8s 4 x 4s and splintered 4 x 4s splintered 4 x 8s and 4 x 8s (of pine, oak, mahogany, cedar, luon, fabricated plastics, plywood, pressed wood)) in the face, torso, legs, neck, arms and back, although never thankfully the hands because I need them for my craft), calling the police (laughable, in my neighborhood), pleading, whining, cajoling, begging, threatening, bargaining, denying, going into counseling, being assertive, passive aggressive, ugly, charming, sweet, sinister, melancholic, and many shades of general pissed-offishness and remorse. )), literature (everything I could get my hands on), the visual arts, wooden figurines, and theater.

I did not write, but observed all of this as an avid spectator, until quite recently - an out-thrusting of incontainable emotional energy caused by my absolute depth of destitution, moral and spiritual bankruptcy engendered by the Void left in Rebekah's absence - I found myself scribbling poems - ecstatic hunchings over notepads and napkins which I would rise from as one who wakes from a dream, shaking, sweating, unable to name the mass I felt beneath my fingers.

laps

push

thump

of the motor

lulls everything

streets

spread

like the heart's

veins

over all

dim alleys

inside me,
